q1073.h1: Look at the shape and color of the sign, and at the number inside it.
q1073.h2: A sign with a number indicates the road number. The color distinguishes between a main road and an expressway.
q1073.p: Good. A number on a sign is always a road number.

q0605.h1: There's a number here. Ask yourself what type of road the color indicates.
q0605.h2: Here too it's a road number, but the color indicates an expressway and not a main road.
q0605.p: Correct. The color is what makes the difference.

q0464.h1: Look at the slope line inside the triangle.
q0464.h2: A red triangle is a warning. The descending line means there is a steep descent ahead. You should engage a low gear and not rely only on the brakes.
q0464.p: Correct. On a steep descent, you brake using the gear, not just with your foot.

q0466.h1: Look at the drawn tire tracks.
q0466.h2: A red triangle with a skidding vehicle warns of a risk of skidding. Slow down and do not brake suddenly.
q0466.p: Well done. On a slippery surface, you slow down in advance.

q0533.h1: Look which way the point of the triangle is facing.
q0533.h2: A triangle with its point facing downwards means: Give way to traffic on the road ahead of you.

q0537.h1: Notice that the sign is held by hand and not placed on a post.
q0537.h2: This is a portable stop sign. It is binding as long as it is placed in front of you, just like a permanent sign.
q0537.p: Correct. A portable sign is just as binding as a permanent one.

q0525.h1: Look at the lines inside the circle.
q0525.h2: This circle prohibits both stopping and parking, on the side where it is placed. The two lines signify a double prohibition.
q0525.p: Correct. Here you don't even stop for a moment.

q0621.h1: Look at the symbol inside the sign.
q0621.h2: The chair symbol indicates parking for a vehicle of a disabled person with a parking permit. Parking there without a permit is an offense.

q0416.h1: Look at the figure of the worker inside the triangle.
q0416.h2: A red triangle with a worker warns of road works. You must slow down and expect changes in the road.
q0416.p: Correct. In a road works area, you slow down.

q1219.h1: Look at the shape of the drawn opening.
q1219.h2: The sign indicates a tunnel ahead of you. In a tunnel, you turn on your lights and the speed is usually limited.
q1219.p: Correct. In a tunnel, you turn on your lights.

q0490.h1: A solid red circle is an absolute prohibition.
q0490.h2: This sign closes the road to all vehicles, in both directions. Not to some vehicles – to all of them.

q0414.h1: Look on which side the line comes inwards.
q0414.h2: The triangle warns that the road narrows from the right side. Stay further to the left and slow down.
q0414.p: Good. You noticed the correct side.

q0430.h2: The sign indicates a roundabout ahead of you. Slow down, and give way to traffic already in the roundabout.
q0430.p: Correct. In a roundabout, the traffic inside has priority.

q0461.h1: There is a picture of another sign inside this sign.
q0461.h2: This sign precedes and informs that a stop sign is further down the road. It gives you time to slow down.
q0461.p: Correct. This is an advance warning.

q0488.h1: Look at the symbol inside the triangle.
q0488.h2: The triangle warns that bicycle traffic crosses the road ahead of you. A cyclist is small and hard to see – slow down.
q0488.p: Well done. Bicycles are hard to see in time.

q1307.h1: Look at the symbol that indicates a concentration of buildings.
q1307.h2: The sign directs to the city center or town center. It is a direction sign, not an instruction or a prohibition.
q1307.p: Correct. This is a direction sign.

q0407.h1: Look at the non-straight lines inside the triangle.
q0407.h2: The triangle warns of an uneven road – potholes and irregularities in the road. Slow down so as not to lose control.
q0407.p: Correct. On an uneven road, you slow down.

q1036.h1: A diagonal line on a sign means 'end'.
q1036.h2: The crossing line marks that the urban road area ends here. From here, the rules for a non-urban road apply.
q1036.p: Correct. A crossing line means the end of validity.

q0542.h1: Look where the arrow is pointing.
q0542.h2: The sign instructs to turn left, and to do so before the sign itself and not after it.

q0677.h1: Look at the symbol above the lane.
q0677.h2: The sign prohibits driving in the lane below it. You need to move to another lane as soon as possible and with caution.

q0675.h1: Look at the symbol above the lane.
q0675.h2: Here it's the opposite – the sign confirms that driving in this lane is permitted.

q0558.h1: Look at the directions of the arrows.
q0558.h2: Two opposing arrows indicate that from here the traffic is two-way. Vehicles will also be coming from the opposite direction.
q0558.p: Correct. From here there is traffic from both directions.

q0588.h1: Notice which arrow is larger or more prominent.
q0588.h2: In this narrow section, the right-of-way is yours. It is still advisable to make sure the driver opposite has understood this.
q0588.p: Correct. The right-of-way is yours, but be careful.

q0683.h1: The diagonal stripes mark something physical on the road.
q0683.h2: The marking indicates a narrow passage or an obstruction. It doesn't prohibit – it marks exactly where the obstruction is.
q0683.p: Correct. This is an obstruction marking.

q0603.h2: The sign indicates a campsite or an overnight parking area. It's a service sign, not a driving instruction.
q0603.p: Correct. This is a service sign.

q0585.h1: Read what is written on the sign, not just its shape.
q0585.h2: This is a pick-up/drop-off point for soldiers, for boarding and alighting only. It is forbidden to wait there.
q0585.p: Correct. You drop off or pick up and continue on your way.

q0607.h1: Look at the arrows above each lane separately.
q0607.h2: The sign shows where each lane ahead of you leads. You choose a lane according to the direction you want to go.
q0607.p: Correct. Each lane and its direction.

q1022.h1: This sign does not resemble any familiar sign.
q1022.h2: This is a sign with a mandatory message that does not have a permanent sign in the sign chart. You read it and obey.
q1022.p: Correct. Even an unfamiliar sign is mandatory.

q0592.h1: Pay attention to the color of the arrow.
q0592.h2: The yellow arrow indicates that this direction is permitted for public transport only. A private vehicle does not drive there.
q0592.p: Correct. Yellow here means public transport.

q0434.h1: Look from which side the merging line is coming.
q0434.h2: A side road merges from the right. You are on the main road – they give you the right-of-way, and turning onto it is forbidden.
q0434.p: Well done. This is not a simple question.

q0454.h1: Look at the railway track symbol.
q0454.h2: Ahead is a railway crossing. Slow down and prepare to stop if necessary – a train cannot stop for you.
q0454.p: Correct. At a railway track, you always slow down.

q0450.h1: Here too, it's about a railway track.
q0450.h2: Slow down and prepare for the possibility that you will need to stop before the track.

q0667.h1: A steady yellow light is not like a flashing yellow.
q0667.h2: A steady yellow means to stop before the junction. You only proceed if stopping would be dangerous – for example, if the vehicle behind is too close.
q0667.p: Correct. Yellow means stop, not accelerate.

q0693.h1: Think about what's on the road, not just on the traffic light.
q0693.h2: Stop before the stop line. If there is no stop line – stop before the pedestrian crossing, so as not to block pedestrians.
q0693.p: Correct. Before the line, and if there isn't one – before the crossing.

q0183.h1: Think from where you will be able to see the intersecting road.
q0183.h2: Stop at a place from which you can see the traffic on the intersecting road, without entering the junction.

q0641.h1: Look at the type of line on the road – solid or broken.
q0641.h2: A solid dividing line must not be crossed. Drive to the right of the lines and do not cross them.
q0641.p: Correct. You don't cross a solid line.

q0368.h1: Look for the sign on which people are drawn walking.
q0368.h2: The sign that warns of pedestrians nearby depicts figures of people. There you must especially slow down.
q0368.p: Correct. Where there are people – you slow down.

q0402.h1: Look for the sign where the vehicle is drawn at an angle and not parallel to the pavement.
q0402.h2: This sign permits parking at an angle, meaning not parallel to the edge of the pavement.
q0402.p: Correct. The angle is the clue.

q1802.h1: Look for the symbol of a battery or electric charging.
q1802.h2: This is a sign for a battery exchange station for an electric vehicle. A relatively new service sign.
q1802.p: Nice. A new and less familiar sign.

q0037.h1: Think about who needs to arrive quickly to save lives.
q0037.h2: An emergency vehicle includes an ambulance, police, IDF, fire brigade, and law enforcement. All of them — not just an ambulance.
q0037.p: Correct. Several types, not just one.

q1536.h1: Why did the vehicle in front of you stop at all?
q1536.h2: It stopped because someone is crossing. If you overtake it, you will not see the pedestrian — therefore overtaking there is forbidden.
q1536.p: Correct. You don't overtake near a pedestrian crossing.

q0282.h1: Think about who will pass there after you.
q0282.h2: It is forbidden to leave an object on the road that could obstruct or endanger road users.

q0058.h2: Every road user — driver, rider, and pedestrian — must obey the traffic signs.
q0058.p: Correct. The sign is mandatory for everyone.

q0198.h1: Think from what distance the driver behind needs to see you.
q0198.h2: Place a warning triangle so it will be visible from a distance of at least one hundred meters to a vehicle approaching from behind.

q0392.h1: Stopping is not enough. You also need to listen.
q0392.h2: Stop, turn off the radio, open a window, listen, and look along the track. You hear a train before you see it.

q1376.h1: Service brakes are the brakes you always use.
q1376.h2: These are the foot brakes. They operate on all the wheels and allow you to stop in all road conditions.

q1737.h1: Think if someone who is about to cross will see you.
q1737.h2: It is forbidden to park on a pedestrian crossing and within the area twelve meters before it — a parked vehicle obstructs the view of pedestrians.

q0261.h1: This light comes on by itself. When?
q0261.h2: The reversing light operates only when reverse gear is engaged. It informs others that you are reversing.

q0248.h1: They need to pass. Where is the clear space?
q0248.h2: Move the vehicle as far as possible to the right, give the right-of-way, and stop if necessary.
q0248.p: Correct. To the right and clear.

q0767.h1: Stopping in a junction blocks everyone.
q0767.h2: Stop on the right side of the road, far from the junction, so as not to block the emergency vehicle inside the junction.

q0768.h1: The signal is for the person behind you, and before they need to react.
q0768.h2: Signal a reasonable distance before the deviation. A signal during the deviation is already too late.

q1746.h1: Who is driving slowly and delaying those behind?
q1746.h2: The shoulder of the road is not for driving, except for a non-motorized vehicle, a tractor, and a slow vehicle that is delaying traffic.

q0031.h1: Dipping the headlights is two things at once.
q0031.h2: You turn off the high beam and turn on the low beam. You do not remain without light.
q0031.p: Correct. You turn one off and another on.

q0271.h2: A new driver convicted of driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs will not receive a standard license.
q0271.p: Correct. Alcohol leaves a long-lasting mark.

q1398.h1: On a motorway, everyone drives fast. A stationary vehicle is a hazard.
q1398.h2: It is forbidden to stop on a motorway, except for stopping on the shoulder when the vehicle has broken down and cannot continue.
q1398.p: Correct. Only for a breakdown, and only on the shoulder.

q0064.h2: Yes. A military police officer in uniform has the same authority as a civilian police officer.

q0272.h1: Where is it safest for a cyclist?
q0272.h2: A cyclist rides as close as possible to the right-hand edge of the road, far from fast-moving traffic.

q0276.h1: Five details. What's important is what will allow them to locate you later.
q0276.h2: You provide your name, address, driving license number, vehicle registration number, and the vehicle owner's name.

q0862.h1: Before driving — what do you need to know?
q0862.h2: You need to make sure you are familiar with the operation of this vehicle. Every vehicle is different in the location of its controls.
q0862.p: Correct. Get to know the vehicle before driving.

q1765.h1: The headrest should support the head, not the neck.
q1765.h2: The top edge of the headrest should be level with the top of the head. Otherwise, it does not protect.
q1765.p: Excellent. A low headrest does not protect.

q1646.h1: What happens to an object that is rubbed a lot?
q1646.h2: Continuous braking heats up the brakes, and they become weaker. Therefore, on a steep descent, you engage a low gear.
q1646.p: Correct. Hot brakes are less effective.

q0831.h1: Three actions, and one of them is to look back.
q0831.h2: You look mainly backwards, signal, and slow down gradually. A sudden move to the shoulder is dangerous.

q1483.h1: What slows the vehicle down besides the brakes?
q1483.h2: A low gear allows the engine to restrain the vehicle, so the brakes don't overheat.
q1483.p: Correct. The engine helps to brake.

q1697.h1: In the dark there are two problems, not one.
q1697.h2: In the dark you see less, and others also see you less. Both are affected.
q1697.p: Correct. Seeing less and being seen less.

q0849.h1: When skidding, a sharp action makes it worse.
q0849.h2: You moderate a skid with correct steering and controlled braking. A sharp movement increases the skid.

q0816.h1: What is obscuring your view of the road?
q0816.h2: The greater the distance from the vehicle in front of you, the more of the road you can see.

q1480.h1: When do you feel a pull to the side?
q1480.h2: Centrifugal force acts in turns and on curves and pulls the vehicle outwards. Therefore, you slow down before the turn.

q0782.h1: Who might be on your right without you having seen them?
q0782.h2: When turning right, a motorcycle or bicycle might enter from the right. Check again before the turn.
q0782.p: Excellent. This is a danger that many people miss.

q0140.h1: Not just for your own vehicle.
q0140.h2: You slow down when there is an expected danger to your vehicle, to road users, or to property. All three.

q1291.h1: What gives you time to react?
q1291.h2: The slower you drive, the more time you have to react and prevent an accident.
q1291.p: Correct. Slower means more in control.

q0875.h1: When reversing, there are two problems.
q0875.h2: You see less, and the operation is also less comfortable. Therefore, drive slowly and check beforehand.

q0611.h1: What makes the danger on a wet road worse?
q0611.h2: On a wet road there is a risk of skidding, and it increases the higher the speed.

q0897.h1: Who is already on the crossing?
q0897.h2: You slow down and even stop, and allow the pedestrians to cross. They have priority.

q1703.h1: Fog affects one sense in particular.
q1703.h2: Fog affects vision. You turn on low beams and slow down.

q0687.h1: There is one word here that is decisive.
q0687.h2: You always apply the parking brake when parking, even on a level surface. The vehicle is not supposed to move.

q1010.h1: An airbag alone is not enough.
q1010.h2: The airbag works together with the seatbelt. Without a seatbelt, it can even cause harm.

q1013.h1: In a rear-end collision, where does the head fly?
q1013.h2: The head restraint reduces the backward movement of the head and prevents whiplash.

q1030.h1: A soft tyre is pressed more onto the road.
q1030.h2: Low air pressure increases friction, and therefore also fuel consumption and pollution.

q1047.h1: If one side is low — where will the vehicle pull?
q1047.h2: Low pressure in one front wheel pulls the vehicle to the side of that wheel.
q1047.p: Correct. It pulls to the weaker side.

q0987.h1: Again, the brakes and the heat.
q0987.h2: Overuse heats up the brakes and reduces their effectiveness.

q0991.h2: Stop and wait for the brakes to cool down. There is no way to speed this up.

q1498.h2: Pressing the clutch disconnects the connection between the engine and the wheels.

q0995.h1: The name hints at the function.
q0995.h2: The starter starts the engine. That is its only function.

q1499.h1: A jacked-up and moving vehicle is very dangerous.
q1499.h2: Before jacking up, ensure by all means that the vehicle will not move — parking brake and chocking the wheels.
q1499.p: Correct. So the vehicle doesn't move.

q1000.h2: On a long downhill drive, engage a low gear, so the engine will brake instead of the brakes.

q0999.h1: A brake fault is not something you wait on.
q0999.h2: Stop driving immediately and have the vehicle towed to a garage. Do not continue cautiously.

q1064.h1: The danger is not in the device but in your eyes.
q1064.h2: The GPS distracts from the road. Set it before the journey.

q1045.h1: What is its function when the vehicle is stationary?
q1045.h2: The parking brake ensures the vehicle does not move or roll away.
q1045.p: Correct. It holds it in place.

q1578.h1: Three systems: to stop, to turn, and to accelerate.
q1578.h2: The control systems are braking, steering, and acceleration.

q1673.h1: Even a tyre that hasn't been driven on gets old.
q1673.h2: Check the manufacturing date. Rubber dries out over time even without use.
q1673.p: Excellent. The age is important, not just the appearance.

q0477.h1: Bring to mind a round sign you have seen.
q0477.h2: Every shape has a function. Ask if it warns, or demands something of you.
q0477.p: Good. The shape tells you the sign's function.

q0606.h1: Think of the 'Give Way' triangle sign.
q0606.h2: Only one triangle on the road is inverted — 'Give Way'. All the others are not.
q0606.p: Correct. The orientation of the triangle makes the difference.

q0401.h2: There are signs that instruct what to do, and there are others whose function is completely different.
q0401.p: Good. Not every sign instructs what to do.

q0691.h1: Where have you seen an orange marking on the road?
q0691.h2: Ask yourself when an existing road marking is changed for a limited time.
q0691.p: Correct. Orange marks a temporary change.

q1761.h1: The sign stands on one side of the road.
q1761.h2: Ask yourself if a sign at the side of the road applies to only one lane.
q1761.p: Good. A sign at the side of the road applies to the whole road.

q1763.h1: This sign is held by hand, not on a post.
q1763.h2: The size of the sign and who holds it do not determine its validity.
q1763.p: Correct. The validity does not depend on the size.

q1772.h1: Look at the lines painted on the road.
q1772.h2: Ask if colour or location change the legal status of a marking.
q1772.p: Good. A marking on the road is also binding.

q0027.h1: Look at the driver who is continuing to drive.
q0027.h2: If they are forced to slow down or swerve because of you, you have not given right-of-way.

q0175.h1: Follow the path of the turn with your eyes.
q0175.h2: Consider who is coming towards you, and who is arriving from the side that the standard rule favours.
q0175.p: Good. A left turn yields to two.

q1764.h1: You are entering a road, not driving on it.
q1764.h2: A driver joining traffic does not get to choose who yields to them.
q1764.p: Correct. The one entering the road yields to everyone.

q0744.h1: Imagine two vehicles in one narrow section.
q0744.h2: If you can both pass together, no one needs to yield.
q0744.p: Nice. The need arises from a lack of space.

q0059.h1: Look at what changes at the intersection.
q0059.h2: A traffic sign is permanent, while a traffic light responds to the situation. One of them overrides the other.
q0059.p: Correct. The variable overrides the fixed.

q0706.h2: The rules of the roundabout do not discriminate by the type of vehicle within it.
q0706.p: Nice. The rule applies to every vehicle.

q0422.h1: Look at what exactly is depicted on the traffic sign.
q0422.h2: Not every traffic sign deals with right-of-way. There are dedicated signs for that.
q0422.p: Correct. Not every sign relates to priority.

q0811.h1: The stop begins before the brake.
q0811.h2: There is a time when the vehicle is still travelling and you have not yet pressed. It is counted.
q0811.p: Nice. The thinking time is also measured.

q0812.h1: Where does the reaction stage end?
q0812.h2: Notice when the thought ends and when the braking action begins.
q0812.p: Correct. The reaction ends at the start of the action.

q1489.h1: Are the brakes already working at this stage?
q1489.h2: In the reaction stage, you haven't touched the brake yet. Two factors remain.
q1489.p: Nice. Time and speed create distance.

q0809.h1: Imagine the same second at two different speeds.
q0809.h2: In the same second of reaction, a fast vehicle covers more metres.

q0853.h1: You stop only for what you see.
q0853.h2: If the stopping distance is longer than the range of your lights, one thing needs to change.

q0871.h1: Who is behind you right now?
q0871.h2: A sudden slowdown surprises someone. It's good to know about them in advance.
q0871.p: Correct. Check behind before slowing down.

q0001.h1: Who else is on the road besides drivers?
q0001.h2: The law speaks of 'road users' — a definition that does not depend on a license.
q0001.p: Nice. The road belongs to everyone.

q0002.h1: What does the police officer ask to see first?
q0002.h2: The vehicle test and ownership relate to the vehicle. The question here is about the person driving it.

q0003.h1: You are lending your vehicle to a friend.
q0003.h2: The owner is responsible for who gets the key, not just for the vehicle itself.
q0003.p: Nice. The key is your responsibility.

q0004.h1: Who will sit next to you on your first drives?
q0004.h2: There are two legal combinations — license seniority and age, not just one of them.

q0005.h1: Imagine being stopped at the roadside without documents.
q0005.h2: The delay is because you cannot be identified, not from the severity of the offense.

q0006.h1: Think who is the most exposed of all on the road.
q0006.h2: The more severe the injury, the longer the disqualification period.

q0007.h1: Picture a scale of three disqualifications.
q0007.h2: Between the thirty and the ninety is a case where there is injury but not death.
q0007.p: Nice. In the middle of the scale.

q0008.h1: Think what is the most severe thing that can happen.
q0008.h2: The longest period of all is reserved for the most severe outcome in an accident.

q0009.h1: Think how severe driving without a permit is.
q0009.h2: The punishment is measured in years of imprisonment, and it is a maximum, not a predetermined penalty.
q0009.p: Correct. A maximum, not a fine.

q0010.h1: Where else do people pass besides the carriageway?
q0010.h2: The criterion is the public's right of passage, not the type of paving in the place.

q0011.h1: Think about driving in fog in the middle of the day.
q0011.h2: The definition is determined by the actual visibility, not just by the time of day.

q0013.h1: Think about how you sit and how you steer.
q0013.h2: The difference from an ATV is in the steering mechanism and the number of wheels.

q0014.h1: Imagine how you sit on a motorcycle.
q0014.h2: The seating and steering are like on a two-wheeler, but there are more wheels.

q0016.h1: Pay attention to the words road, vehicle, and direction.
q0016.h2: 'One-way' describes the number of permitted directions, not the type of road.

q0017.h1: Think about the moment after sunset.
q0017.h2: The law adds a short margin at each end, and does not stick to the sunset itself.

q0019.h1: Imagine a bridge that passes over a road.
q0019.h2: The difference from an intersection is not in the location or the number of roads, but in the height.

q0021.h1: Stand at the corner and look at the edge of the road.
q0021.h2: The area is derived from the boundaries of the road itself, not from a marking or a road sign.

q0022.h1: Think about who is sitting in the back and who is driving.
q0022.h2: Ask yourself if the responsibility stops only with the one who isn't buckled up.

q0023.h1: Look where the white lines are painted.
q0023.h2: The lines are marked on the surface the vehicle drives on, not beside it.

q0024.h1: Imagine a barrier and tracks crossing a road.
q0024.h2: If the train passes above or below, it is not a crossing by definition.

q0028.h1: Imagine the road is clear ahead of you.
q0028.h2: The law doesn't count how many vehicles, but checks if the overtake is safe.

q0030.h1: Think about someone standing next to the road.
q0030.h2: The definition is broad, and is not limited to one form of road use.

q0032.h1: Stand at the corner and see where they meet.
q0032.h2: A meeting at the same level creates an intersection. Different levels are something else.

q0033.h1: Look at the line before the traffic light.
q0033.h2: Ask in which direction the line extends — along the direction of travel or across it.

q0034.h2: The special status doesn't happen by itself — a sign at the entrance declares it.
q0034.p: Correct. A sign at the entrance.

q0036.h1: Think of a tractor on an inter-city road.
q0036.h2: The threshold is lower than the permitted speed on a regular urban road.

q0038.h1: Think what distinguishes a taxi from a private vehicle.
q0038.h2: Transport for hire requires a different type of license, not an agreement or an installation.
q0038.p: Correct. Private is not a taxi.

q0039.h1: Think when a vehicle is considered very old.
q0039.h2: The threshold is not a round number, and it is higher than what most people guess.

q0040.h1: Count the seats in a large family car.
q0040.h2: The count does not include the driver, and the number is less than ten.

q0041.h1: Imagine a vehicle with a sticker on the windscreen.
q0041.h2: The permit to move is restored only through the same form that took it off the road.

q0042.h1: Think of a bicycle path in a park.
q0042.h2: Ask if the path is intended only for pedestrians, or for other groups as well.

q0043.h1: Imagine someone directing you in a car park.
q0043.h2: The question is whether it is a permission, or a duty from which there is no exemption.

q0044.h1: Look in the mirror before you open the door.
q0044.h2: The danger in opening a door relates to who is passing by, not to the distance from the pavement.

q0045.h1: Imagine a concrete island between two directions.
q0045.h2: The word 'built' indicates a physical installation, and the division is lengthwise.

q0047.h1: Imagine a child sitting higher in the vehicle.
q0047.h2: The seat doesn't bring its own belt — it adapts the vehicle's belt.

q0048.h1: Think about an electric vehicle and a diesel vehicle.
q0048.h2: Ask if the definition lists types of fuel, or talks about the propulsion itself.

q0049.h1: Open the glove compartment and list the documents.
q0049.h2: The list also includes insurance, and also certificates required for a specific vehicle.

q0050.h1: Think of a large company's vehicle fleet.
q0050.h2: The permit is narrow, and is related to an authorized body that approves the photocopy with its signature.

q0051.h1: Who decides when to present them — you or the police officer?
q0051.h2: The obligation itself exists, and the only question is who determines the time.

q0052.h1: Think what is recorded after a traffic conviction.
q0052.h2: The record pertains to traffic offenses only, and is not cyclical by years.

q0053.h1: Try to read a faded and crumpled licence.
q0053.h2: There are two requirements here — both where they are kept and their condition.
q0053.p: Correct. In the vehicle and legible.

q0054.h1: Look at the rear window of a vehicle in front of you.
q0054.h2: Its location was chosen so as not to compete with the brake light at the top.
q0054.p: Good. At the bottom of the window.

q0055.h1: Think about how long the 'new driver' status lasts.
q0055.h2: The period is measured in years, not in months like other periods.

q0056.h1: Imagine a correction made with a pen on the licence.
q0056.h2: Writing on an official document alters it, even if the intention is to improve it.

q0057.h1: Think about what is required of you in order to drive.
q0057.h2: The reporting concerns systems that affect control, perception, and reaction.
q0057.p: Correct. Report to the licensing authority.

q0060.h1: Imagine a police officer directing traffic at an intersection.
q0060.h2: The obligation is not limited to a specific role or a specific type of instruction.

q0061.h1: Imagine a police officer not in uniform, with an ID card.
q0061.h2: The identification confers the same authority, even over a written instruction on the road.
q0061.p: Correct. An ID card is sufficient.

q0062.h1: Think about what is within a traffic warden's authority and what is not.
q0062.h2: The authority exists, but it is limited to the subject the warden is in charge of.
q0062.p: Good. In the area of traffic.

q0063.h1: Imagine a worker with a flag at a road paving site.
q0063.h2: The authority stems from the place where he is working, not from the type of road it is.

q0065.h1: Imagine a police officer signalling to proceed at a red light.
q0065.h2: There is no list of exceptions — the live instruction overrides the fixed sign.
q0065.p: Good. A person over a sign.

q1741.h1: Look to the right as you approach an empty intersection.
q1741.h2: When there is no sign, the rule specifies a fixed side — not vehicle type and not direction of turn.

q1779.h1: Follow your path crossing the lane.
q1779.h2: You cross the path of the one coming from ahead in any of his turning options.

q0123.h1: Think about which lane the slow vehicle is driving in.
q0123.h2: In Israel, you drive on the right side, and overtaking is done from the free side.

q0129.h1: Look ahead until the next turn.
q0129.h2: The condition relates to the state of the road at that moment, not to the type of vehicle in front of you.

q0130.h1: Try to see past the truck in front of you.
q0130.h2: Overtaking requires seeing the entire section ahead, not just the vehicle itself.

q0131.h1: Imagine railway tracks a hundred metres ahead of you.
q0131.h2: Near a track there are no mitigating conditions — the train cannot swerve.

q0134.h1: The vehicle in front of you has stopped. Ask why.
q0134.h2: Stopping before a crossing hides from you the one who caused it to stop.
q0134.p: Good. It stopped — there's a reason.

q0135.h1: Someone is overtaking you now on the left.
q0135.h2: The more you make room and maintain your speed, the faster the overtake will be completed.

q0257.h1: You are in the middle of the oncoming lane right now.
q0257.h2: The lane you left is still clear behind you, and that is the shortest way out.

q0258.h1: Consider if overtaking has a special exemption.
q0258.h2: The maximum speed is set for the section of road, not for the action you are performing.

q0281.h1: Imagine the entrance and exit of the tunnel.
q0281.h2: The prohibition also applies outside the tunnel, at an identical distance on both its sides.

q0357.h1: Stand a metre before a pillar in the middle of the road.
q0357.h2: A stationary obstacle is not a vehicle, and you pass it without entering the oncoming lane.

q0479.h1: The overtaker is currently stuck beside you on the left.
q0479.h2: Only you can increase the gap that will allow him to get back in.

q0772.h1: Look ahead before, and again in the middle.
q0772.h2: The road can change after you have pulled out, so one check is not enough.

q0099.h1: Think of a tractor holding up traffic.
q0099.h2: A loaded tractor moves slower than any other vehicle, and its limitation is uniform on every road.

q0141.h1: Think about when you can't see the road ahead.
q0141.h2: The duty depends on what is obscuring the road from you, not on the type of place.

q0143.h1: Imagine a herd crossing an intercity road.
q0143.h2: Anything that might move without warning requires slowing down, even if it is not a vehicle.

q0332.h1: Think about the moment just before a danger.
q0332.h2: The duty is determined by the expected danger, not by your speedometer.

q0444.h1: Imagine a busy highway during rush hour.
q0444.h2: The maximum speed is a ceiling. What is below it is determined by the traffic.

q0626.h1: Imagine a long downhill with hot brakes.
q0626.h2: On a downhill the vehicle accelerates by itself, so slowing down is required, which is not required on an uphill.
q0626.p: Correct. On a downhill, you slow down.

q0733.h1: What do you do before touching the brake?
q0733.h2: You start with information, continue by removing power, and only then actually slow down.

q0802.h1: Think about driving in the rain on a familiar road.
q0802.h2: Control alone is not enough — both the law and the conditions are taken into account.

q0803.h1: Ask if there is a situation that permits exceeding the limit.
q0803.h2: The maximum speed is an upper limit, and a reasonable speed is always within it.

q0805.h1: Think how much distance a slow vehicle covers.
q0805.h2: All three distances are derived from speed and move in the same direction.

q0806.h1: Think about what happens at the moment of impact itself.
q0806.h2: Speed does not change the reaction time, but it does change the energy.

q0807.h1: Think about what happens when you lose control.
q0807.h2: The measure is not what others are doing, but what you actually have control over.

q0252.h1: Imagine a vehicle with one headlight at night.
q0252.h2: A missing headlight changes both what you see and how others see you.

q0253.h1: Think about a street lit by streetlights.
q0253.h2: The prohibition is not absolute; it depends on the existing lighting and on dazzle.

q0254.h1: Imagine lights approaching you from ahead.
q0254.h2: Dipping the lights is for whoever sees the beam, and that happens when they are in front of you.

q0255.h1: Look at the mirror of the vehicle in front of you.
q0255.h2: The person driving in front of you also gets the beam, through their mirrors.

q0256.h1: Imagine a parked vehicle with its lights on.
q0256.h2: A vehicle that is not moving does not need a long beam, but it still dazzles.

q0260.h1: Think about when the air itself reduces visibility.
q0260.h2: The permit relates to weather that reduces visibility, not to the type of road you are on.

q0347.h1: Think about who approves changes to a vehicle.
q0347.h2: A technically correct installation is not enough without an entity that approves it.

q0351.h1: Ask if the clock alone determines it here.
q0351.h2: The definition combines two situations, and one of them does not depend on the time at all.

q0655.h1: Think about what is already on before you add more.
q0655.h2: The fog lamp is an addition to an existing system, not an independent system.

q0747.h1: Imagine cross-traffic that has a green light.
q0747.h2: Making way for a vehicle does not cancel the danger from which the red light protects you.

q0851.h1: Try to estimate distance in complete darkness.
q0851.h2: At night, both how much you see and how correctly you judge are impaired.

q0852.h1: Where to look when the light is too strong?
q0852.h2: There is a fixed reference point on the side of the road that is not affected by the beam.

q0998.h1: Imagine how your vehicle looks from a distance.
q0998.h2: A single headlight might be read as a two-wheeled vehicle, and change the estimation of others.

q1019.h1: Think what is closest to the bulb itself.
q1019.h2: First check the smallest and cheapest link in the circuit, not the whole thing.

q0671.h1: Run a finger over the tyre's grooves.
q0671.h2: The grooves channel away water. The less of them that remains, the less grip.

q0843.h1: Think of a struggle between two forces.
q0843.h2: A skid begins when the force pushing forward is greater than the force of the grip on the road.

q0846.h1: Think about what separates rubber from asphalt.
q0846.h2: Any layer that gets between the two acts the same way, whatever its material.

q0847.h1: Think about what depends on you and what depends on the road.
q0847.h2: There are two sources here — one in the driver's action and one in the road surface itself.

q0850.h1: Think about what sharp movements do.
q0850.h2: Prevention is done before the skid, mainly through speed and the manner of braking.

q0950.h1: Imagine a curtain of water on the windscreen.
q0950.h2: Pouring rain harms visibility like fog, and therefore the same lighting is permitted in it.

q0189.h1: Someone is already in the middle of the crossing now.
q0189.h2: Someone who has started to cross cannot go back, and therefore completing the crossing takes precedence over everything.

q0206.h1: Think from which side the vehicle is approaching it.
q0206.h2: A stationary vehicle hides someone who has not yet entered the crossing, not someone who has exited.

q0516.h1: The overtaking driver does not see what is in front of the vehicle.
q0516.h2: Overtaking near a crossing hides exactly the area you need to see.

q0778.h1: Think about where drivers are already slowing down.
q0778.h2: A place where the driver is slowing down anyway is the place where it is easier to stop.

q0157.h1: Look for a line, and if there isn't one — look for a barrier.
q0157.h2: There is a descending order of signs here, and each one applies only in the absence of the previous one.

q0161.h1: Stop and listen carefully near the tracks.
q0161.h2: The obligation stems from the presence of the train itself, and not from the sign at the location.

q0195.h1: Think about who must work on the shoulder itself.
q0195.h2: The permit is given to someone for whom the shoulder is their workplace, and not for convenience.
q0195.p: Good. For the purpose of one's role.

q0199.h1: Stand and check what your vehicle is hiding.
q0199.h2: The prohibition is judged by the effect on others, not by the state of your vehicle.

q0200.h1: Imagine getting out of the vehicle into the oncoming lane.
q0200.h2: Parking on the left requires crossing the road on every entry and exit.

q0201.h1: Think of a baby carriage on the pavement.
q0201.h2: The pavement belongs to pedestrians, unless a specific marking has determined otherwise.

q0202.h1: Stand at the junction and check what you cannot see.
q0202.h2: A vehicle parked at a junction blocks the field of vision that all turning drivers need.

q0209.h1: There is no second lane to overtake in here.
q0209.h2: Anyone who comes across you will be forced to cross a solid line, and that is a forbidden action.

q0222.h1: Look at the marking painted on the asphalt.
q0222.h2: The manner of parking is determined at the location itself, and not according to the type of road or the day.

q0234.h1: Think about who doesn't work on Saturdays.
q0234.h2: The permit is given to the most common type of vehicle, and not to work or commercial vehicles.

q0244.h1: Think how much space a vehicle takes up diagonally.
q0244.h2: Width and size do not permit or forbid — only what is actually marked.

q0294.h1: Think about when buses do not run.
q0294.h2: The stop becomes available only on days when it is not in use, and only for one type of vehicle.

q0689.h1: Imagine a vehicle parked on a steep slope.
q0689.h2: The name 'parking brake' indicates when it operates, not on its braking power.

q0722.h1: Imagine a dark figure on the shoulder at night.
q0722.h2: The obligation applies to anyone exposed to traffic, and not just the person who was driving the vehicle.
q0722.p: Correct. A vest for the one getting out.

q0069.h1: Think about what reacts to traffic in real time.
q0069.h2: A flashing yellow has no instruction of its own, and therefore it is the exception here.

q0133.h1: Think who is arriving at the intersection from another direction.
q0133.h2: At an intersection, traffic enters from every side, and the oncoming lane is not really clear.

q0203.h1: Stand at the corner and try to see to the left.
q0203.h2: A vehicle close to the corner hides exactly what the turning driver needs to see.

q0775.h1: Imagine a child running to the crosswalk.
q0775.h2: Anticipation is a driver's tool, even when the other person behaves incorrectly.

q0781.h1: Follow the right wheel in the turn.
q0781.h2: A wide arc opens a space that a two-wheeled rider might enter.
q0781.p: Good. Keep close to the right.

q0789.h1: Imagine yourself stuck inside the intersection.
q0789.h2: Whoever enters a full intersection blocks those who will get a green light right after you.

q1718.h1: Think how long a U-turn takes.
q1718.h2: A slow turn requires both good visibility and the absence of a prohibition at that location.

q1751.h1: The green light does not clear a space.
q1751.h2: The permission to enter does not create a clear space to stop in on the other side.

q1285.h2: Two colors together mark an object that fulfills more than one role on the road.

q1750.h1: Think what comes immediately after the yellow.
q1750.h2: The steady yellow appears at the end of the permission cycle, not at its beginning.
q1750.p: Correct. Red is on the way.

q0075.h1: Think when one hand must leave the wheel.
q0075.h2: The exceptions are all for operating the vehicle, not for personal comfort.
q0075.p: Good. Only for the vehicle's needs.

q0285.h1: Imagine a long descent without engine braking.
q0285.h2: In neutral, the engine is disconnected, and all the stopping falls on the brakes alone.

q0288.h1: Think about fuel vapors around the opening.
q0288.h2: A running engine produces heat and sparks near a substance that evaporates quickly.

q0329.h1: Think about the most common license.
q0329.h2: A regular private car is in this category, and its grade is the basic one for a driver.

q0688.h1: Imagine two tires of different sizes.
q0688.h2: A difference between the two sides of the axle pulls the vehicle, so the size is critical.

q0692.h1: Think what additional brake exists in the vehicle.
q0692.h2: There is a second, independent braking system, which does not depend on the foot pedal.
q0692.p: Correct. There is a second brake.

q0735.h1: Think what changes around you while driving.
q0735.h2: The choice of gear is derived from the actual speed, not from what is permitted by the sign.

q0739.h1: Imagine a vehicle starting to move on its own.
q0739.h2: Before releasing one brake, another must already be engaged.

q0741.h1: Think what will prevent movement at the moment of ignition.
q0741.h2: Starting the engine is safe only when the gear is not transferring power to the wheels.

q0841.h1: Think what slows the car besides the brakes.
q0841.h2: The engine can take part in the slowing-down work, and thus the brakes cool down.

q0863.h2: The checklist combines several stopping mechanisms, and does not choose one.

q0872.h1: Try to turn the steering wheel with only one hand.
q0872.h2: The grip determines how precise the turn is, in any vehicle and at any speed.

q0873.h1: Think what happens in too high a gear.
q0873.h2: The gear and the speed are connected in every vehicle, not just on descents.

q0935.h1: Think which system is giving a warning here.
q0935.h2: A warning in the system that stops the vehicle does not permit continuing to drive.

q0080.h2: The rider is kept to the right side, so only a lane on that same side is suitable for them.

q0087.h1: Imagine entering the driveway of a private house.
q0087.h2: Crossing the sidewalk is permitted as a short crossing, and not as a regular way of driving.

q0119.h1: Think about where a U-turn ends up.
q0119.h2: Permission is broad, and is only restricted where a marking or sign prohibits it.

q0126.h1: The vehicle ahead of you has already moved out of your path.
q0126.h2: Someone waiting in another lane is not blocking the lane you are driving in.
q0126.p: Correct. You pass on the right.

q0164.h1: Think about from when to when you should signal.
q0164.h2: The signal is meant to give advance notice, so it starts before the manoeuvre itself.
q0164.p: Good. Before and until the end.

q0173.h1: You are crossing a sidewalk that people are walking on.
q0173.h2: A driver exiting premises is entering an area used by others, and therefore is the one who must adjust.

q0191.h1: Look who is directing traffic at the blockage.
q0191.h2: When there is someone directing traffic on site, their instructions override your own decision.

q0192.h1: The obstacle is on your side only.
q0192.h2: The one whose lane is clear does not need to make way for the one who is forced to swerve.
q0192.p: Correct. The one with the clear path proceeds.

q0223.h1: Measure about one and a half hand-widths.
q0223.h2: The permitted distance is less than half a metre, so that a passage is not created beside the vehicle.
q0223.p: Good. Less than half a metre.

q0753.h1: Think about where you need to position yourself before a turn.
q0753.h2: Only a left turn requires getting into position on the left side in advance.
q0753.p: Correct. In preparation for a left turn.

q0754.h1: Think about when you yourself should move out of the lane.
q0754.h2: Leaving the lane is justified when you are the one taking action, not when someone else is.

q0755.h1: Look what is marked on the right-hand lane.
q0755.h2: Sometimes the right-hand lane is reserved for others, in which case you drive to the left of it.

q0387.h1: Look which of the signs is round and blue.
q0387.h2: A triangle warns of what is ahead, and a blue circle instructs what to do now.

q0403.h1: Look for the inverted triangle among them.
q0403.h2: Only one shape here is inverted, and it is reserved for giving right of way.

q0404.h2: A unique shape, with no other like it, is reserved for the most serious instruction.

q0425.h1: Look if the triangle is standing on its base.
q0425.h2: A triangle with its apex pointing up only warns, and does not assign right of way.

q0429.h1: The shape here depicts a road junction.
q0429.h2: A drawing of a road is not an instruction. It shows what is there, not who goes first.
q0429.p: Good. It describes, it doesn't instruct.

q0438.h1: Look which line connects to which.
q0438.h2: When one line joins another, the one joining is the one that waits at the entrance.

q0697.h1: Look at the green arrow on the instrument panel.
q0697.h2: In a left turn, you cross only one lane — that of oncoming traffic.

q0698.h1: Check from which side the bicycle is coming.
q0698.h2: A bicycle is a vehicle in every respect, and the standard rule regarding sides applies.
q0698.p: Correct. The one on the right goes first.

q0699.h1: Count how many lanes you are crossing.
q0699.h2: A left turn crosses the path of both oncoming traffic and traffic arriving from the side.

q0700.h1: First, identify who is coming from your right.
q0700.h2: You always start with the one coming from the right, and continue applying the same rule.
q0700.p: Correct. From the right and onwards.

q0701.h1: Look at the green arrow and then to the right.
q0701.h2: A left turn puts you last, in relation to both oncoming traffic and traffic from the right.
q0701.p: Good. The one turning is last.

q0702.h1: Check which of the two is on your right.
q0702.h2: When everyone is continuing straight, the side determines priority — not the type of vehicle.

q0703.h1: Follow the green arrow on the diagram.
q0703.h2: You are turning left, so both of them go before you, according to the order between them.

q0704.h1: Look for a triangle sign next to one of them.
q0704.h2: The one facing a 'Give Way' sign loses their place in the queue.
q0704.p: Correct. The sign sets the order.

q0705.h1: Read again what is said about the red vehicle.
q0705.h2: When the red vehicle is not an emergency vehicle, it is just a vehicle approaching from your left.
q0705.p: Good. The one on the left waits.

q0711.h1: Look at the green arrow and then to both sides.
q0711.h2: When turning left, both oncoming traffic and traffic from the right have priority over you.

q0973.h1: Look for an upside-down red triangle on the side of the road.
q0973.h2: One of them has a sign, and that is decisive, regardless of who arrived first.

q0976.h1: Look where the big white arrow is pointing.
q0976.h2: The big arrow marks the direction that has priority in this narrow section.
q0976.p: Correct. The big arrow is yours.

q0394.h1: Count the diagonal stripes on the post.
q0394.h2: The number of stripes counts down the distance to the crossing, one stripe for every hundred metres.

q0498.h1: Look how many vehicles are drawn in the circle.
q0498.h2: The prohibition is about the action, not the type of vehicle doing it.

q0751.h1: Look at the opening drawn in blue.
q0751.h2: The prohibition doesn't stop at the building's edge, but continues for the same distance on both sides.

q0826.h1: Look at the dark vehicle in the opposite lane.
q0826.h2: The lane you intend to drive in currently belongs to the opposite direction.

q0884.h1: Look how much of the road the truck is obscuring.
q0884.h2: The closer you are, the less you can see of the road ahead of it.

q0887.h1: The vehicle in front of you is finishing an overtake now.
q0887.h2: Someone who has finished overtaking needs space to return, and that depends on who is on the right.

q0923.h1: Look at the yellow sign on the bus.
q0923.h2: The bus doesn't forbid passing, but it signals that someone might come out from behind it.

q1053.h1: Name which vehicles are drawn in the circle.
q1053.h2: The sign isn't about overtaking at all, but about who is allowed to be here.

q0132.h1: Look what the vehicle before the crossing is obscuring.
q0132.h2: The vehicle in front of you is blocking your view of someone about to step onto the crossing.

q0190.h1: Look at the island in the middle of the crossing.
q0190.h2: The island allows waiting in the middle, so each side is considered separate.

q0205.h1: The vehicle in the picture is stopped after the lines.
q0205.h2: The one obscuring the crossing is the one stopped on the side the vehicles are coming from.

q0214.h1: Look at the railing along the pavement.
q0214.h2: A railing directs pedestrians to one place, and a parked vehicle blocks it there.

q0376.h1: Look for the lines painted in blue.
q0376.h2: A triangle warns about people, and blue shows where the place itself is.

q0389.h1: Look what exactly the railing is blocking.
q0389.h2: The railing exists to channel a crossing, and parking next to it negates its function.

q0567.h1: Look at the number in the blue circle.
q0567.h2: A minimum speed requires a pace that a person or a bicycle cannot reach.

q0776.h1: Count how many paths cross here.
q0776.h2: At a junction, every direction of travel crosses others, and every crossing point is a risk.

q1507.h1: Look what is blue and what is red here.
q1507.h2: Blue permits and instructs, and a red circle prohibits. The colour tells it all.

q1535.h2: There is a road entirely for fast vehicles, and therefore pedestrians may not enter it.
q1535.p: Correct. A road for vehicles only.

q1769.h1: Look for a pair — one on the road and one above.
q1769.h2: A crossing is marked both with paint on the asphalt and with a sign that is visible from a distance.

q0139.h1: Think what changes on a wet road.
q0139.h2: Control alone isn't enough. The legal limit also remains in place.

q0148.h1: Think about an ATV on an open road.
q0148.h2: For a small, slow vehicle, a single speed limit is set, regardless of the road type.

q0150.h2: The fastest road has the highest speed limit set by law.

q0151.h1: Imagine a concrete barrier between the directions.
q0151.h2: A structural divider raises the permitted speed, but not to the level of a motorway.

q0152.h1: Think of the two default numbers.
q0152.h2: In a built-up area a low number, and outside it a higher one — both are multiples of ten.

q0154.h1: Look at the playing child on the sign.
q0154.h2: A street where children play gets the low number from the signs.

q0348.h1: Think how you would know your current speed.
q0348.h2: Without a working speedometer, there is no way to know if you are within the limit or outside it.

q0521.h1: Look at the ascending arrow in the circle.
q0521.h2: The sign announces entry into a zone, and this zone has a fixed number.

q0629.h1: Look who is drawn together with the vehicle.
q0629.h2: When people and children share the surface, the number drops to a low level.

q0937.h1: Read the number on the round sign.
q0937.h2: When a number is explicitly posted, it overrides any default in the law.

q0941.h1: Look at the diagonal line in the circle.
q0941.h2: A line crossing through cancels a restriction, and returns the road to its regular limit.

q0963.h1: Look at the yellow sign on the right.
q0963.h2: The high number is reserved for only one type of road, marked with a special sign.

q0674.h1: Look at the lights next to the barrier.
q0674.h2: A flashing red light at a crossing does not permit passage even after a complete stop.
q0674.p: Correct. Wait for it to turn off.

q0149.h2: The law sets how often the test is done. The base is every year, and the law can also set a different period.
q0149.p: Correct. The law sets when the test is due.

q0114.h1: Check which lane on street A goes toward the junction.
q0114.h2: The solid line on street A separates two directions. Only lane 1 goes toward the junction. Turning left? Enter the left lane, next to the separation area.
q0114.p: Correct. Left turn — into the lane by the divider.

q0727.h1: Follow the red line. Where does it go before the turn?
q0727.h2: Before a left turn, move to the left side of the road in your direction. That way you do not cut across other lanes while turning.
q0727.p: Correct. Turn left from the left lane.

q0156.h1: The picture shows a barrier and a traffic light. Do they replace your caution?
q0156.h2: A barrier and a traffic light help, but they do not replace caution. Near a railway you slow down every time.
q0156.p: Correct. At a railway crossing, always slow down.

q0098.h1: Who gives permits for vehicles and drivers?
q0098.h2: A cargo tractor does not normally carry a passenger. You need a special permit from the body in charge of licensing.
q0098.p: Correct. A passenger in a cargo tractor needs a permit.

q0280.h1: There are casualties here. What do they need first?
q0280.h2: When there are casualties, you stop. Help them as much as you know and can, and call for help.
q0280.p: Correct. At an accident with casualties, stop and help.

q0773.h1: The sign marks disabled parking. Do you have such a permit?
q0773.h2: Disabled parking is only for a vehicle with the right permit. Even when all the spaces are empty, it is not for you.
q0773.p: Correct. No permit, no parking there.

q0018.h1: Find the pavement next to the road. Who is it for?
q0018.h2: The pavement belongs to pedestrians, and only to them.
q0018.p: Correct. The pavement is for pedestrians only.

q1366.h1: Mudguards stop mud flying from the wheels.
q1366.h2: If there is no wing over the rear wheel, mud flies onto others. So a mudguard is needed. A slow-moving vehicle and a tractor are exempt.
q1366.p: Correct. No rear wing? You need a mudguard.

q0162.h1: Look at the barrier and the lights by the tracks.
q0162.h2: A warning signal at a railway crossing means a train is coming. It does not matter who was there first — you stop.

q0083.h1: Think about the word "separation": the area separates, it is not parking.
q0083.h2: A separation area is not meant for parking. You park there only if a sign allows it.
q0083.p: Correct. No parking in a separation area without a sign.

q0212.h1: Notice: both before the stop and after it.
q0212.h2: The bus needs room to enter the stop and leave it. So you may not leave a vehicle 20 meters before the sign and 20 meters after it.
q0212.p: Correct. 20 meters on each side of the stop.

q0120.h1: Reversing is allowed — but on what condition?
q0120.h2: You may reverse when there is a need. The condition: do not endanger, hurt or disturb anyone.
q0120.p: Correct. Reverse only when it is safe.

q0259.h1: A searchlight is a very strong light. Who could it dazzle?
q0259.h2: A searchlight dazzles drivers. So you use it only when stopped, and never aim it at another vehicle or along the road.
q0259.p: Correct. Searchlight only when stopped, never at drivers.

q1714.h1: Who operates the vehicle while it is moving?
q1714.h2: The driver is responsible for the condition of the vehicle he drives. That includes the smoke that comes out of it.
q1714.p: Correct. The driver is responsible for the smoke.

q0752.h1: The rule is to drive on the right. When do you move left for a moment?
q0752.h2: You always drive on the right side. To pass a vehicle in front of you, you must move left for a moment.
q0752.p: Correct. You leave the right side only to overtake.

q1553.h1: The distance is very small. The wheels are almost touching the curb.
q1553.h2: A standing vehicle must be close to the curb, so it does not block traffic. The allowed distance: up to 40 cm.
q1553.p: Correct. Up to 40 cm from the curb.

q0726.h1: Look at the signals above the lanes: an X or an arrow?
q0726.h2: An X above a lane means: do not drive in it. A green arrow means: allowed. The green arrows are above the lanes on the right side.
q0726.p: Correct. Drive only under a green arrow.

q1538.h1: Think about how a load is seen from behind, even in the dark.
q1538.h2: At the rear you mark with the warning colour red. A reflective triangle shows up when headlights hit it.
q1538.p: Correct. A red reflective triangle at the end of the load.

q0094.h1: The ATV in the picture comes out of the field. What ground is it built for?
q0094.h2: An ATV travels on dirt roads. Inside a moshav or kibbutz it can also use the internal road.
q0094.p: Correct. Dirt roads, or an internal road in a moshav or kibbutz.

q0239.h2: A private vehicle is not meant for carrying people for money. There are no exceptions — not during a strike and not at a low price.
q0239.p: Correct. No paid passengers in a private vehicle.

q1311.h1: Who gives you your driving licence?
q1311.h2: The Licensing Office must know if your health has changed. You tell it right away, by registered mail.
q1311.p: Correct. Notify the Licensing Office at once.

q0291.h1: Someone pushing a vehicle is also moving a vehicle on the road.
q0291.h2: The law treats a person who moves a vehicle by physical force as a driver. The same rules apply to him.
q0291.p: Correct. Pushing a vehicle counts as driving it.

q0338.h1: A warning triangle warns other drivers. Of what?
q0338.h2: A vehicle standing on the road is a danger to other drivers. So you place a triangle every time you have no choice but to stop a vehicle on the road.
q0338.p: Correct. Vehicle stopped on the road? Place a triangle.

q0085.h1: Look at the solid white line in the middle of the road.
q0085.h2: You do not cross a solid line, not even to overtake. Drive only on its right side.
q0085.p: Correct. Stay to the right of the solid line.

q0225.h1: The door in the picture is open. What if the car drives like this?
q0225.h2: An open door while driving puts passengers and people on the road in danger. There is no case where it is allowed.
q0225.p: Correct. Drive only with the doors closed.

q0197.h1: The sign marks a motorway. Does stopping suit such a road?
q0197.h2: Stopping on a motorway is dangerous for everyone. So it is forbidden, except where a marking clearly allows it.
q0197.p: Correct. No stopping on a motorway without a marking.

q0138.h1: The arrow shows the gap. The question asks the legal minimum, not the recommended one.
q0138.h2: The law measures the gap in travel time. The legal minimum is one second.
q0138.p: Correct. By law: at least one second.

q1757.h1: A solid line and one lane each way. Can you pass a stopped vehicle there?
q1757.h2: On such a road you cannot pass a vehicle that is standing. So stopping and parking are forbidden, even on the shoulder.
q1757.p: Correct. No stopping there, even on the shoulder.

q0353.h1: The question is whether it is required. And who approves the bin?
q0353.h2: A private vehicle must have a rubbish bin. It must be a type approved by the Licensing Authority.
q0353.p: Correct. An approved rubbish bin is mandatory.

q1752.h1: The two vehicles cannot pass. Who needs to move?
q1752.h2: On a narrow road neither one has right of way. Both move right as far as they can, even onto the shoulder.
q1752.p: Correct. Both keep to the right.

q1356.h1: Notice two things: the colour, and whether it is uniform.
q1356.h2: Headlights shine white or light yellow. And the light must be one uniform colour.
q1356.p: Correct. White or light yellow, and uniform.

q1758.h1: Who is near schools and playgrounds?
q1758.h2: Children may run into the road suddenly. So you drive slowly and pay more attention.
q1758.p: Correct. Near children, slow down and stay alert.

q0089.h1: Which side of the road do you drive on here?
q0089.h2: You pass an obstacle on its right side, just as you drive on the right. Only a marking can change that.
q0089.p: Correct. Pass an obstacle on the right.

q0227.h1: The door in the picture opens to the road side. What passes there?
q0227.h2: Getting out on the road side is dangerous because of passing vehicles, so it is forbidden. Exception: the driver, and the passenger next to him when parked on the left side.
q0227.p: Correct. Don't get out on the road side.

q0798.h1: Who is holding the steering wheel?
q0798.h2: Even if someone helps you from outside, you are the driver. Safety is your responsibility.
q0798.p: Correct. When reversing, the driver is responsible.

q0078.h1: In a shared street, who else uses the street besides you?
q0078.h2: In a shared street, pedestrians and children are all over the street. The driver adapts to them and does not endanger them.
q0078.p: Correct. In a shared street, watch out for pedestrians.

q0079.h1: The picture shows the road, shoulders and a separation area. Where do cars drive?
q0079.h2: The shoulder and the separation area are not for driving. A private vehicle drives on the road, where there is a road.
q0079.p: Correct. Drive on the road only.

q0177.h1: Who walks on the pavement in front of the exit?
q0177.h2: When you exit, you cross the pavement. Slow down, and stop if needed, so pedestrians can pass safely.
q0177.p: Correct. When exiting, let pedestrians pass.

q0070.h1: You have the right licence. But do you know this vehicle?
q0070.h2: Vehicles of the same type differ from each other. You may drive a vehicle only if you know how to operate it.
q0070.p: Correct. Drive only a vehicle you know how to use.

q1767.h1: Usually you pass on the left. Where is there a separate lane?
q1767.h2: A vehicle in a public transport lane drives in its own lane. So it may pass vehicles in the lane next to it.
q1767.p: Correct. In a public transport lane you may pass on the right.

q0072.h1: The medication affects driving. What does that mean for you?
q0072.h2: Such medication harms your ability to drive. So you may not drive right after taking it.
q0072.p: Correct. Medication that affects you — no driving.

q0217.h1: What could happen to a parked vehicle on a slope?
q0217.h2: A parked vehicle must stay in place. The driver makes sure it will not move or roll.
q0217.p: Correct. A parked vehicle must not move.

q0158.h1: The train in the picture is near the crossing. Who can stop quickly — you or it?
q0158.h2: A train cannot stop quickly. When it is near or signalling, stop before the crossing and wait for it to pass.
q0158.p: Correct. Train coming? Stop and wait.

q1707.h1: What must the gap allow you to do?
q1707.h2: Keep a gap that lets you stop safely. The law requires at least one second of travel.
q1707.p: Correct. Room to stop safely, at least one second.

q0178.h1: Who is already on the road you are coming out onto?
q0178.h2: Whoever is already on the road or the pavement goes first. You wait for vehicles and pedestrians, and only then go out.
q0178.p: Correct. Coming out of a property, you give way.

q0756.h1: Which lane do you use when there is no special reason?
q0756.h2: You drive in the right lane. You move to the left one only to overtake or to turn left.
q0756.p: Correct. Keep right unless overtaking or turning left.

q1753.h1: Notice: both before the crossing and after it.
q1753.h2: A vehicle standing near the railway blocks the view and gets in the way. So stopping and parking are forbidden at least 20 meters before and after.
q1753.p: Correct. At least 20 meters from the railway.

q0344.h1: From which sides must the vehicle be identified?
q0344.h2: A vehicle is seen from the front and from the back. So a standard plate is needed on each side.
q0344.p: Correct. One plate in front, one at the rear.

q0210.h1: Two vehicles stand side by side. How much room is left for traffic?
q0210.h2: A vehicle standing next to a parked vehicle blocks the road. This is forbidden, with no exceptions.
q0210.p: Correct. Never stop next to a parked vehicle.

q0345.h1: Who is authorized to inspect vehicles?
q0345.h2: Summoning a vehicle for inspection is an examiner's power. Only someone authorized as an examiner can summon a vehicle.
q0345.p: Correct. An authorized examiner orders the inspection.

q0207.h1: Find the stop line and the sign next to it.
q0207.h2: A vehicle standing just before the stop line blocks the view and the traffic. So you may not stand within 12 meters before it.
q0207.p: Correct. 12 meters before the stop line.

q0270.h1: Look for a dangerous driving offence on the road itself.
q0270.h2: Ask yourself which of these actions on the road puts other people’s lives at risk.
q0270.p: Correct. Unlawful overtaking stops the licence.

q0266.h1: Notice: the question is about accompaniment, not the whole new-driver period.
q0266.h2: Accompaniment is only the start of the new-driver period. It lasts three months from the day you got your licence.
q0266.p: Correct. Accompaniment: three months from the first licence.

q0110.h1: Look at the arrow signs: which way does each street go?
q0110.h2: Streets A and C are both one-way. Turning left? Leave from the left lane of street A and enter the nearest lane of street C.
q0110.p: Correct. From the left lane, into the nearest lane.

q1700.h1: When should the reversing light be on?
q1700.h2: The light shows others that you are reversing. So it comes on only from reverse gear, and only while that gear is engaged.
q1700.p: Correct. It is on only in reverse gear.

q0268.h2: A young new driver may carry up to two passengers besides himself. More than that — only when an accompanist sits next to him in front.
q0268.p: Correct. Up to two passengers, unless an accompanist is in front.

q0147.h1: Next to the motorway sign is a round sign with a number. What does it set?
q0147.h2: The round sign sets a minimum speed. Only a motor vehicle that is permitted and able to go at that speed or faster may enter.
q0147.p: Correct. Only a vehicle that can keep the sign's speed.

q1574.h1: A cargo tractor is a heavy, slow vehicle.
q1574.h2: A cargo tractor has a fixed top speed set by law, even outside town: 40 km/h.
q1574.p: Correct. Cargo tractor: up to 40 km/h.

q1379.h1: What makes a place on the road a pedestrian crossing?
q1379.h2: A pedestrian crossing is part of the road. It is marked with road markings or a sign so pedestrians cross there.
q1379.p: Correct. A crossing is marked on the road.

q0297.h1: Does the police officer need a special reason?
q0297.h2: A police officer may ask any driver for a sobriety test, at any time. He needs no court order or suspicion.
q0297.p: Correct. A sobriety test — at any time.

q0331.h1: Who gives permits to drive special vehicles?
q0331.h2: For emergency and recovery vehicles too, the permit to drive comes from the body that issues driving licences.
q0331.p: Correct. A permit from the Licensing Authority.

q1716.h1: Which document says what the vehicle itself is allowed?
q1716.h2: The vehicle licence sets what is allowed in this vehicle. An extra passenger is allowed only if it is written there.
q1716.p: Correct. Only if it is in the vehicle licence.

q0792.h1: A solid line. Is there any reason that allows crossing it?
q0792.h2: You do not cross a solid dividing line. A U-turn does not justify it either.
q0792.p: Correct. Never cross the solid line.

q1318.h1: Why did the vehicle in the lane next to you slow down?
q1318.h2: The pedestrian may continue into your lane, and the slowing vehicle hides him. So slow down and let him finish crossing.
q1318.p: Correct. Let the pedestrian finish crossing.

q0193.h1: Look at the parked cars and at the curb by the road.
q0193.h2: In town you may stop and park on the road or shoulder. Not where a law or sign forbids it, like a red-white curb, and not when you block traffic.
q0193.p: Correct. Allowed, if not prohibited and not blocking.

q0342.h1: Who takes part in transferring ownership?
q0342.h2: A change of ownership has a seller and a buyer. So both are responsible for registering the change.
q0342.p: Correct. Seller and buyer are both responsible.

q0074.h1: Think about the word “limited”. What happens when you can't see well ahead?
q0074.h2: A driver must see the road ahead clearly. Only a very small limitation that does not interfere is allowed.
q0074.p: Correct. You must see clearly ahead.

q0137.h1: Ask yourself: what is the gap for?
q0137.h2: The gap must let you stop in time, even if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly.
q0137.p: Correct. A gap that lets you stop in time.

q1682.h2: The duty applies to vehicles with an engine. Every such vehicle, with no exception.
q1682.p: Correct. A reflective vest in every motor vehicle.

q0128.h1: Think about a lane where all vehicles turn the same way.
q0128.h2: In a lane only for right turns, you are in a separate lane. So you may pass the vehicles on your left.
q0128.p: Correct. In a right-turn lane you may pass on the right.

q0352.h1: Ask yourself: which vehicles are exempt?
q0352.h2: Most vehicles must carry an extinguisher. Private vehicles, tractors and motorcycles are exempt.
q0352.p: Correct. An extinguisher in most vehicles.

q1717.h1: Which action is part of driving itself?
q1717.h2: Take a hand off the wheel only for something you need to drive. A phone or helping a passenger distracts you.
q1717.p: Correct. A hand off the wheel only for driving.

q0962.h1: Look at the triangle sign on the right. What does it show?
q0962.h2: The sign warns: vehicles merge into your road from the right. They must give you the right-of-way. Still, watch them closely.
q0962.p: Correct. Your right-of-way, but stay alert.

q0229.h1: Who decides how many passengers may sit next to the driver?
q0229.h2: Only one passenger sits next to the driver. More is allowed only if the vehicle's license permits it.

q0967.h1: There are two signs and a bend. How far ahead can you see?
q0967.h2: The bend hides the road ahead, so overtaking is forbidden. The sign with the number 90 limits the speed.

q1740.h1: Does pushing a vehicle count as driving?
q1740.h2: The law treats a person pushing a vehicle as driving it. So what is forbidden when driving is also forbidden when pushing.

q0187.h1: Several conditions must be met together, not just one.
q0187.h2: Cross the tracks only when all is safe: the crossing is clear, the barrier is up, and there is room to finish crossing.
q0187.p: Correct. Cross only when the crossing is clear and safe.

q1218.h1: Think about how traffic moves on an expressway.
q1218.h2: On an expressway traffic is fast, and stopping puts everyone at risk. So you may not stop there to drop off passengers.
q1218.p: Correct. No dropping off passengers on an expressway.

q0077.h1: Where is it written what a driver must do while driving?
q0077.h2: The duty depends on what is written on the driving licence. If it says glasses or lenses, you must wear them.

q1784.h1: What is hard to see as you approach a summit?
q1784.h2: Before a summit you can't see what is coming toward you. When the view is limited or blocked, overtaking is dangerous and forbidden.

q1781.h1: Which side of the road do you drive on?
q1781.h2: The rule is to pass a traffic island on its right, just as you drive on the right. Only a sign can say otherwise.
q1781.p: Correct. Pass on the right, unless a sign says otherwise.

q1211.h1: Who gets the permit — the driver, or the disabled person's vehicle?
q1211.h2: The permit belongs to the disabled person's vehicle. So it applies even when a person accompanying them drives.
q1211.p: Correct. The permit applies even when a companion drives.

q1471.h1: Note: a light commercial vehicle, a non-urban road, no dividing area.
q1471.h2: On a non-urban road without a built-up dividing area, such a commercial vehicle is limited to 80 km/h.
q1471.p: Correct. 80 km/h on such a road.

q0176.h1: Look for a square sign with a white arrow on the streets.
q0176.h2: Such a sign means: all traffic on the street goes one way. Check which street it stands on.

q1650.h1: Where is it written what a specific vehicle may do?
q1650.h2: An ATV may carry an extra passenger only if the vehicle licence allows it.

q1402.h1: Is it always forbidden, or can you get permission?
q1402.h2: Towing more than one trailer is not fully forbidden. It is allowed only with approval from the Licensing Authority.
q1402.p: Correct. You need Licensing Authority approval.

q0379.h1: Notice two parts: how long, and when it applies.
q0379.h2: Penalty points stay for two years from the day of the offence. This applies when the driver has up to 20 points.
q0379.p: Correct. Two years from the offence.

q0304.h1: Is such a vehicle fit to drive?
q0304.h2: An oil leak or heavy smoke is a sign the vehicle is faulty. So you may not drive it.
q0304.p: Correct. A faulty vehicle is not driven.

q0350.h1: The word “one” tells you a lot.
q0350.h2: On a one-way road all vehicles go the same way. There is no traffic coming toward you.

q1336.h1: What is hard to see at the crest of a hill?
q1336.h2: Before a crest you can't see a vehicle coming from the other side. So a U-turn there is dangerous.
q1336.p: Correct. No U-turn before a crest.

q0264.h1: Who is registered as responsible for the vehicle?
q0264.h2: The owner is responsible. He is cleared only if he proves another person drove, and says who.
q0264.p: Correct. The owner is responsible, unless he proves otherwise.

q0337.h1: Who decides whether you may drive?
q0337.h2: The Licensing Authority gives the licence. So you must tell it right away about a change in your health.
q0337.p: Correct. Notify the Licensing Authority immediately.

q0115.h1: Check which lane on street A goes toward the intersection.
q0115.h2: Street A is two-way, and only lane 1 goes toward the intersection. Street B is two-way too: turning left, enter the lane going your way.
q0115.p: Correct. Enter the lane going your way.

q0283.h1: May you leave a broken-down vehicle as long as you like?
q0283.h2: A broken-down vehicle gets in others' way. Remove it as soon as you can, and within 24 hours at most.
q0283.p: Correct. Remove it fast, within 24 hours.

q1774.h1: The name of the light already tells you something.
q1774.h2: Fog lights are for times when it is hard to see: heavy rain, fog or snow.
q1774.p: Correct. Fog lights only in bad weather.

q0716.h1: From which side does the tractor come, relative to you?
q0716.h2: The tractor comes from your left, so you enter before it. The blue car enters last — it gives right of way to both of you.
q0716.p: Correct. You, the tractor, then the blue car.

q0204.h1: Why must the area near a fire hydrant stay free?
q0204.h2: Firefighters need to reach the hydrant fast. So you may not park within two meters of it.
q0204.p: Correct. Two meters free around a hydrant.

q0891.h1: Does the law set a specific lane for a U-turn?
q0891.h2: A U-turn is allowed from any lane. Only a sign can forbid it.
q0891.p: Correct. From any lane, unless a sign forbids it.

q0109.h1: From which side could a vehicle come when you turn right?
q0109.h2: When turning right you move to the right side. So first check there is no moving vehicle there.
q0109.p: Correct. Before turning right, look right.

q0399.h1: Where do you look when you write a message?
q0399.h2: Writing a message takes your eyes off the road and a hand off the wheel. It is forbidden in every case.

q0116.h1: Check which lanes on street A lead away from the intersection.
q0116.h2: On street A a solid line separates the directions. Turning right? Enter the rightmost lane, nearest the edge of the road.
q0116.p: Correct. Turning right — into the rightmost lane.

q0829.h1: Why is the vehicle ahead of you moving left?
q0829.h2: The vehicle ahead is in a left-turn lane and signaling. It is turning left, so you may pass it on the right.
q0829.p: Correct. Pass a left-turning vehicle on the right.

q0717.h1: Find the sign at the corner near you, on the right.
q0717.h2: The sign at your entrance is “Give way”. So you wait for the other two vehicles and enter after them.
q0717.p: Correct. You have “Give way”? You go last.

q0169.h1: What is the driver ahead of you trying to tell you?
q0169.h2: The signal says he is about to turn or move over. Let him do it: slow down, and stop if needed.
q0169.p: Correct. Let the signaling driver do it.

q1688.h1: The licence says “new driver”. What must he do at first?
q1688.h2: A new driver must drive with a companion during the period set by law. One convicted of breaking this won't get a regular licence.
q1688.p: Correct. A new driver must have a companion.

q1484.h1: Ask yourself: is there any case where you may exceed the speed limit?
q1484.h2: The maximum speed always applies, even while overtaking. If you can't overtake without exceeding it, don't overtake.
q1484.p: Correct. Even when overtaking — not above the limit.

q1539.h1: A protruding load must be easy to see from behind.
q1539.h2: The load is marked with a red reflective triangle. Each side is 60 cm long.

q0111.h1: Look at the signs and lines on each street.
q0111.h2: Street A is one-way, so turn left from its left lane. Street C is two-way: enter the lane going your way.
q0111.p: Correct. From the left lane, into your direction's lane.

q0106.h1: What matters most when you move sideways?
q0106.h2: You may move off your line only when no one on the road is put at risk or disturbed.
q0106.p: Correct. Change your line only without risk or disturbance.

q0305.h1: Why does the police test with a breathalyzer?
q0305.h2: A breath test is an official test. Its result is accepted as evidence in court.
q0305.p: Correct. A breath test is evidence.

q0124.h1: Why is the vehicle ahead of you signaling?
q0124.h2: The vehicle ahead is turning left and signaling. It moves to the left, so you may pass it on the right.
q0124.p: Correct. Pass a left-turning vehicle on the right.

q0196.h1: The sign marks a motorway. What happens when a car stops on it?
q0196.h2: On a motorway traffic is fast, and stopping puts everyone at risk. So you may not stop there for passengers.
q0196.p: Correct. No pick-up or drop-off on a motorway.

q0251.h1: Who has to show the vehicle license to a police officer on the road?
q0251.h2: The vehicle license is held by whoever is driving now. It does not matter if the vehicle is his or someone else's.
q0251.p: Correct. The driver holds the vehicle license.

q0012.h1: What is the difference between a short stop and parking?
q0012.h2: Picking up or dropping off people or cargo, right away and without a break, is not parking. Stopping for any other reason is parking.
q0012.p: Correct. Parking is not for immediate pick-up or drop-off.

q0720.h1: From which side does the motorcycle reach the intersection?
