q0720.h2: No sign gives you the right of way. The motorcycle comes from your right, so it has the right of way. The signs at its street only forbid entering it.
q0720.p: Correct. From your right? Its right of way.

q0238.h1: Two things decide: what is written, and the maximum.
q0238.h2: Carry as many as the vehicle license states. In any case, no more than eight passengers, not counting the driver.
q0238.p: Correct. By the license, and up to eight passengers.

q1500.h1: Ask yourself: which insurance covers damage to others?
q1500.h2: Damage to another person's vehicle is damage to a “third party”. Not you, and not the insurance company.
q1500.p: Correct. Third-party insurance covers another's vehicle.

q0728.h1: Look at the round sign on the traffic island. Where does the arrow point?
q0728.h2: The arrow points down and to the right: pass the traffic island on its right side. Check which side of the island each vehicle uses.
q0728.p: Correct. Pass the island on the arrow's side.

q0067.h1: Who is standing there and sees the situation right now?
q0067.h2: An authorized inspector's instruction overrides the sign. Obey him, and drive with great caution.
q0067.p: Correct. An authorized inspector comes before the sign.

q0172.h1: Compare the lines: which one covers the whole width?
q0172.h2: A “road” is all the area open to the public: the carriageways, the shoulders and the separation area. Find the line that covers all of these.
q0172.p: Correct. A road includes shoulders and the divider.

q1395.h1: What connects the engine to the wheels?
q1395.h2: Going downhill, the vehicle must be in gear. This way the driver controls the vehicle and speed better.

q0046.h1: The seat in the picture has its own belts. Who is it for?
q0046.h2: A safety seat is a standard seat for children. It is fastened to the vehicle with the seat belt, and has its own belts.
q0046.p: Correct. A standard child seat, fastened to the vehicle.

q0235.h2: If the vehicle has seat belts, everyone buckles up: the driver and all passengers.
q0235.p: Correct. There is a belt — buckle up.

q1543.h2: The pavement belongs to pedestrians. You may not drive on it, even to bypass an obstacle.
q1543.p: Correct. Never drive on the pavement.

q0790.h1: Must a lane be marked with lines?
q0790.h2: A lane exists even without lines on the road. So you can stray from a lane even on an unmarked road.
q0790.p: Correct. A lane can be unmarked.

q0165.h2: The signal is for others on the road. So signal at a place and time when they can see it.
q0165.p: Correct. Signal so others can see it.

q0784.h1: On road (a): which lanes go in your direction?
q0784.h2: Turn left from the leftmost of your lanes. Road (b) is one-way, so enter its left lane — the one nearest to you.
q0784.p: Correct. Left to left, into the nearest lane.

q1133.h1: Think: can others see you properly in the dark?
q1133.h2: During lighting-up time both headlights must work. If one fails, you stop and do not keep driving.

q0125.h1: Think about a special lane with its own rules.
q0125.h2: In a public transport lane you are in a separate lane. So you may pass vehicles driving in the regular lane.
q0125.p: Correct. In a public transport lane you may pass on the right.

q0249.h1: Ask yourself: why not stay close to an emergency vehicle?
q0249.h2: Behind an emergency vehicle keep a large distance: at least 100 meters.
q0249.p: Correct. At least 100 meters from an emergency vehicle.

q0306.h1: What does a police officer need to demand a blood test?
q0306.h2: An officer may demand a blood test when he has reasonable suspicion the driver is under the influence of alcohol or drugs.
q0306.p: Correct. Reasonable suspicion is enough for a blood test.

q1295.h1: What happens to the air from a vehicle that gives off a lot of smoke?
q1295.h2: If a vehicle pollutes the air more than allowed, an officer may forbid its use.
q1295.p: Correct. Polluting above the limit — no driving.

q0218.h1: Ask yourself: what will keep the vehicle from moving when you are not in it?
q0218.h2: After parking, turn off the engine, take the key, and apply the parking brake.
q0218.p: Correct. Engine off, key out, parking brake on.

q0105.h1: What matters most when you move from lane to lane?
q0105.h2: Leaving your lane is allowed only when it is safe. It must not endanger or obstruct anyone on the road.
q0105.p: Correct. Change lanes only without risk or obstruction.

q0166.h1: How does the driver behind you know you are braking?
q0166.h2: When you press the brake, red lights come on at the back. They are the braking signal.

q1496.h1: The owner is not here. How will they know who hit their car?
q1496.h2: Leave a written note with your details, your vehicle's details and your insurance details. Also report to the police within 24 hours.
q1496.p: Correct. Leave your details and report to the police.

q0299.h1: What happens if the driver refuses the test?
q0299.h2: A driver must do a breath test when a police officer demands it. A driver who refuses will be considered drunk.
q0299.p: Correct. Refusing the test counts as being drunk.

q0336.h1: Ask yourself: who is in charge of driving licenses?
q0336.h2: The Licensing Authority is in charge of driving licenses. The law gives it the power to send a driver to a refresher course.
q0336.p: Correct. The Licensing Authority may do this by law.

q0121.h1: On a narrow road there is no room for two. What can each driver do?
q0121.h2: Both drivers are responsible. Each one slows down and moves aside, even off the road, so there is no collision.
q0121.p: Correct. Both slow down and move aside.

q0327.h1: Think: what makes a person dangerous behind the wheel?
q0327.h2: Someone disqualified from getting a license will not get one. Neither will someone with a health problem that endangers them and others.
q0327.p: Correct. Disqualification or a dangerous health problem.

q0163.h1: When do the drivers around you need to know what you are about to do?
q0163.h2: Signal before every change in movement: when you start driving, when you turn and when you leave your lane.
q0163.p: Correct. Signal before every change of direction.

q0236.h1: In which situation does the driver have to turn around to see?
q0236.h2: When reversing, the driver turns around to see behind. That is why only then they are exempt from the seat belt.
q0236.p: Correct. When reversing — exempt from the seat belt.

q1756.h1: What is this sign telling you about?
q1756.h2: The sign tells you a railway crossing is coming. Before the crossing, overtaking is forbidden until you are past it.
q1756.p: Correct. No overtaking before a railway crossing.

q1766.h1: Why is a vehicle standing near a pedestrian crossing dangerous?
q1766.h2: A vehicle standing near the crossing hides the pedestrians. So you may not stand in it, or within 12 metres before it.
q1766.p: Correct. 12 metres before a pedestrian crossing.

q0224.h1: Think of a vehicle that has no doors or windows.
q0224.h2: In a normal vehicle your body stays inside, because outside is dangerous. Only on a motorcycle is your body outside anyway.
q0224.p: Correct. Body inside — except on a motorcycle.

q0213.h1: What does the bus need to stop at the stop and pull out?
q0213.h2: A vehicle standing opposite the stop narrows the road for the bus. On a wide road, 12 metres or more, there is enough room.
q0213.p: Correct. Allowed only on a wide enough road.

q0710.h1: Look at the sign next to the red car, and where the motorcycle comes from.
q0710.h2: The sign next to the red car makes it wait. The motorcyclist has no such sign and comes from your right side. So you, turning left, wait for him.
q0710.p: Correct. The red car waits; you wait for the motorcyclist.

q1782.h1: Who finds it harder to start moving again — the one going up or down?
q1782.h2: A vehicle going uphill struggles to start again on the slope. So the descending vehicle stops and lets it pass.

q1720.h1: What does the drug's prescription say?
q1720.h2: Sedatives can harm your driving. So driving after them is forbidden, unless the prescription clearly says it is allowed.
q1720.p: Correct. Sedatives — no driving, unless the prescription allows it.

q0279.h1: Who must be told — and what if they are already here?
q0279.h2: The report is so the police will know. If an officer is at the scene and heard the details, the police already know.
q0279.p: Correct. Officer at the scene — the police already know.

q1780.h1: What does a solid separation line mean?
q1780.h2: A solid line may not be crossed, even with no oncoming traffic. Passing on the right shoulder is also forbidden. So you stay behind the cart.
q1780.p: Correct. Solid line — don't cross, follow behind.

q0298.h1: What does the device check when you blow into it?
q0298.h2: The device tests the air you blow out. That shows how much alcohol is in your blood.
q0298.p: Correct. A breath test measures alcohol.

q0068.h1: Who ordered the sign to be put up?
q0068.h2: A temporary sign placed by order of a police officer is legal. You obey it like any other sign.
q0068.p: Correct. A temporary police sign must be obeyed.

q0220.h1: Who runs the penalty points system?
q0220.h2: The licensing authority runs the points system. It can make a driver with points take tests, and even disqualify their license.
q0220.p: Correct. The licensing authority can also disqualify.

q0286.h1: What must be engaged when you drive downhill?
q0286.h2: Downhill you must not drive without a gear. An engaged gear keeps control of the vehicle.

q0714.h1: Look at the sign on the right, at your entry to the junction.
q0714.h2: There is a Give Way sign at your entry. So you wait for the red vehicle, even though it is turning left.
q0714.p: Correct. The sign is yours — you wait.

q0481.h1: The key question: who uses the road?
q0481.h2: Everyone on the road — driver, rider and pedestrian — must be careful. Caution is everyone's duty.
q0481.p: Correct. Everyone on the road must be careful.

q1486.h1: Note: an urban road, and no other sign.
q1486.h2: In town there are pedestrians, junctions and traffic lights. So the top speed there is 50 km/h.
q1486.p: Correct. In town — up to 50 km/h.

q0480.h1: A child may suddenly run into the road. What will you do?
q0480.h2: Near children, slow down and be ready to stop. If needed, stop. A horn or a wide sidewalk is not enough.
q0480.p: Correct. Near children — slow down, ready to stop.

q0721.h1: The blue signs show a traffic circle. Where is the red vehicle driving?
q0721.h2: A vehicle already driving inside the traffic circle goes first. Whoever enters waits for it, even when coming from the right.
q0721.p: Correct. In a traffic circle — whoever is inside goes first.

q1742.h1: Note: what can forbid a U-turn?
q1742.h2: There is no special lane or junction type for a U-turn. What decides is a sign: if no sign forbids it, it is allowed.
q1742.p: Correct. U-turn allowed unless a sign forbids it.

q1683.h1: When do you need the vest — and where are you sitting then?
q1683.h2: You put the vest on before stepping out onto the road. So keep it in the driver's cabin, within reach. A motorcycle has no driver's cabin.
q1683.p: Correct. The vest stays in the driver's cabin, within reach.

q1785.h1: Does the ban depend on a sign or on the type of road?
q1785.h2: Before a crosswalk there may be a pedestrian you cannot see. So the ban on overtaking there always applies, on every road.
q1785.p: Correct. Never overtake before a crosswalk.

q1795.h1: Think: who has a work reason to drive on the sidewalk?
q1795.h2: The sidewalk belongs to pedestrians. A vehicle cleaning the sidewalk is the only exception in the list.
q1795.p: Correct. On the sidewalk — only to clean it.

q1743.h1: What does a solid line mean, even with a broken line next to it?
q1743.h2: A solid line forbids crossing. The broken line next to it does not cancel the ban.
q1743.p: Correct. There is a solid line — don't cross.

q0113.h1: Street C has a solid line in the middle. What does it tell you?
q0113.h2: The solid line means street C is two-way. Turn left from your left lane, into the first lane past the solid line.
q0113.p: Correct. From the left, into the lane past the line.

q1677.h1: When must the drivers around you know about your movement?
q1677.h2: Signal when you change direction, for example when moving to another lane. A slope or a railway crossing alone does not require signalling.

q1747.h1: Does the ban depend on the type of road or on a sign?
q1747.h2: Before a pedestrian crossing there may be someone you cannot see. So this ban has no exceptions.
q1747.p: Correct. Before a pedestrian crossing — never overtake.

q0117.h2: A U-turn is allowed when it does not disturb traffic or endanger anyone. And only when no sign forbids it.
q0117.p: Correct. U-turn — no disturbance, no danger, no sign against.

q0108.h1: On street B: which lane leads toward the intersection?
q0108.h2: Turn right from your right lane. On street C, enter only the lane nearest the edge of the road, not the one beside it.
q0108.p: Correct. From the right, into the right lane only.

q1286.h1: In a fire — how much time do you have to look for the extinguisher?
q1286.h2: In a fire you must act fast. So the extinguisher is where you can see it and reach it easily.
q1286.p: Correct. The extinguisher is visible and easy to reach.

q0290.h1: Who is responsible for the offense if no one knows who was driving?
q0290.h2: The owner is responsible for what is done with their vehicle. They are released only if they prove who was driving at that time.
q0290.p: Correct. The owner is responsible, unless they prove who drove.

q0118.h1: What do other drivers need in order to watch out for you?
q0118.h2: In a U-turn you cut across the road. If another driver cannot see you, they will not stop in time.
q0118.p: Correct. U-turn only when everyone can see you.

q0168.h1: If the electric signals don't work — what else can you signal with?
q0168.h2: When the electric signals are broken, you still must signal. The law says to signal with your left hand.
q0168.p: Correct. Signals broken — signal with your left hand.

q1783.h1: Is a U-turn the same as a left turn?
q1783.h2: A sign banning left turns does not ban U-turns. A U-turn is allowed if it does not disturb traffic and no sign or marking forbids it.
q1783.p: Correct. A no-left-turn sign is not a no-U-turn sign.

q1297.h1: What matters most now: teaching the other driver, or avoiding a crash?
q1297.h2: The goal is to avoid a collision. Slow down and move right as far as you can, and onto the shoulder if needed.
q1297.p: Correct. Slow down and move right, even onto the shoulder.

q0221.h1: How do you park a vehicle along the road?
q0221.h2: Park parallel to the edge of the road. If the road has other markings, follow them.
q0221.p: Correct. Parallel to the edge, or by the markings.

q1560.h1: Is reversing a normal way to drive?
q1560.h2: Reversing is more dangerous. Do it only when traffic really needs it and there is no other way.
q1560.p: Correct. Reverse only when there is no other choice.

q0343.h1: Who is in charge of licensing vehicles?
q0343.h2: The Licensing Authority is in charge of vehicle licensing. So you notify it when you stop using a vehicle for more than a month.

q1284.h1: Children may suddenly run into the road. What does that require of you?
q1284.h2: Near children, slow down. If needed, stop. A horn or an adult with them is not enough.
q1284.p: Correct. Near children — slow down, stop if needed.

q0226.h1: What can happen when a door opens while driving?
q0226.h2: An open door while moving is dangerous to passengers and to people passing by. So there is no exception at all.
q0226.p: Correct. While moving — doors always stay closed.

q1739.h1: The vehicle ahead is moving left. Which side stays free?
q1739.h2: A vehicle turning left leaves the right side free. So you may pass it on the right.
q1739.p: Correct. Turning left — pass on the right.

q0122.h1: Who finds it harder to start moving again — the one going up or down?
q0122.h2: A vehicle going uphill struggles to start again on the slope. So, if needed, the descending vehicle stops and lets it continue.

q0167.h1: If the electric signals don't work, does the duty to signal disappear?
q0167.h2: The duty to signal stays even when the electric signals are broken. Then you signal by hand.
q0167.p: Correct. Signals broken — signal by hand.

q0275.h1: What matters most when someone is hurt?
q0275.h2: First help the injured person as far as you know and can. Call the rescue services and stay at the scene until they arrive.
q0275.p: Correct. Help, call for rescue, and stay.

q1698.h1: Who does the high beam dazzle?
q1698.h2: High beams dazzle oncoming drivers. So use them only on non-urban roads, when traffic allows and no vehicle is coming toward you.
q1698.p: Correct. High beam — only with no oncoming vehicle.

q0708.h1: What does the sign on the corner, at your entry, say?
q0708.h2: There is a Give Way sign at your entry. So you wait for everyone crossing your path — from the left and from the right.
q0708.p: Correct. Give way to everyone crossing your path.

q0084.h1: The picture shows a separation area in the middle. Which side do you drive on?
q0084.h2: In Israel you drive on the right. So you drive to the right of the separation area, unless marked otherwise.
q0084.p: Correct. To the right of the separation area.

q0231.h1: The picture shows a seat with its own harness. Who is it for?
q0231.h2: A seat belt is built for an adult. A small child needs a safety seat that fits their height and weight.
q0231.p: Correct. Small child — in a fitting safety seat.

q0104.h1: Who sometimes has to get somewhere fast, even against traffic?
q0104.h2: On a one-way road everyone drives the same way. Only emergency vehicles may drive the opposite way.
q0104.p: Correct. Against traffic — emergency vehicles only.

q0127.h1: Ask yourself: does one penalty cancel the other?
q0127.h2: The court gives a penalty, and the Licensing Authority acts separately. Its measures come on top of the penalty.
q0127.p: Correct. Authority measures come on top of the penalty.

q0076.h1: Where should your hands be while driving?
q0076.h2: Your hands belong on the wheel. So use the phone only with a hands-free device, without holding it.
q0076.p: Correct. Phone while driving — hands-free only.

q1762.h1: Why did the vehicle stop before the tracks?
q1762.h2: A train may be coming. If you overtake, you will enter the tracks without seeing. So overtaking there is forbidden.
q1762.p: Correct. Never overtake a vehicle stopped before a railway crossing.

q0725.h1: Who is riding on your right, where you are turning?
q0725.h2: The cyclist is on your right, and your turn crosses their path. Let them continue and turn behind them — no overtaking, no honking.
q0725.p: Correct. Let the cyclist pass, then turn behind.

q0346.h1: A faulty vehicle on the road — what should happen to it?
q0346.h2: A vehicle with defects is dangerous on the road. So the examiner or officer can stop its use and take the vehicle license.
q0346.p: Correct. Defects — stop use and take the license.

q0250.h1: Who controls the vehicle while it is moving?
q0250.h2: The person driving controls the vehicle. So they are responsible for the noise it makes.
q0250.p: Correct. The driver is responsible for the noise.

q1768.h1: Think about the words "right" and "use of the road".
q1768.h2: The road belongs to everyone. Every driver must drive so that others can also use it fully.
q1768.p: Correct. The road belongs to everyone.

q0228.h1: What can happen to someone who jumps from a moving vehicle?
q0228.h2: Getting in or out of a moving vehicle is very dangerous. So there is no exception at all.
q0228.p: Correct. Get in and out only when the vehicle is stopped.

q1530.h1: What happens to a fast vehicle in a bend?
q1530.h2: In a curve the vehicle is harder to control. So slow down when entering the curve and while in it.
q1530.p: Correct. In a curve — slow down.

q1777.h1: Think: what kind of repair, and how much does it bother others?
q1777.h2: Only a minor repair is allowed, one that does not bother road users. And the vehicle may not stay there more than 24 hours.
q1777.p: Correct. Minor repair, no disturbance, up to 24 hours.

q1210.h1: Not every disabled tag allows driving in this lane.
q1210.h2: Only a disabled person with paralysed legs who uses a wheelchair, and has the special tag for it, may drive in the public transport lane.
q1210.p: Correct. The lane is open only to the paralysed-legs tag.

q1546.h1: A load on the road is a danger to other drivers.
q1546.h2: A fallen load can cause an accident. The driver who dropped it is responsible — he stops and makes sure it is removed at once.
q1546.p: Correct. Load fell — stop and remove it at once.

q0707.h1: There is no sign at the junction entries. Which side does each vehicle come from?
q0707.h2: At a junction with no signs, give right-of-way to the vehicle coming from your right. The vehicle from your left is the one that waits for you.
q0707.p: Correct. No sign — the one on the right goes first.

q1552.h1: Think about what alcohol does to a driver.
q1552.h2: Alcohol slows your reactions and harms your judgement. There is no situation in which it is allowed.
q1552.p: Correct. If you drank, you don't drive.

q0330.h1: A category B license limits the trailer's weight. What is the limit?
q0330.h2: A category B holder may tow a trailer, but only a light one: its maximum permitted gross weight is up to 1,500 kg.
q0330.p: Correct. Category B — trailer up to 1,500 kg.

q0269.h1: Who runs the penalty points system?
q0269.h2: The Licensing Authority runs the points system. A driver with 36 points loses the license for three months and must take a theory test again.
q0269.p: Correct. 36 points — disqualification and a theory test.

q1525.h1: Who knows how the medicine affects you?
q1525.h2: The doctor and the prescription tell you if the medicine harms driving. If it says not to drive — it is forbidden.
q1525.p: Correct. Follow the doctor and the prescription.

q0333.h1: The question is about a category B license — for a private car.
q0333.h2: You can get a category B license only from age 17. There is no exception.

q1321.h1: Notice: is the light flashing or steady?
q1321.h2: A flashing orange light warns of road works. Slow down and watch for changes on the road.

q1573.h1: Are you allowed to cross a solid separation line?
q1573.h2: You may not cross a solid separation line. You can overtake only if there is room to do it without crossing the line.
q1573.p: Correct. Solid line — you don't cross it.

q0097.h1: Ask yourself: who could fall off an ATV?
q0097.h2: On an ATV both the driver and the passenger can fall. So everyone on it wears a helmet.
q0097.p: Correct. On an ATV — a helmet for everyone.

q0081.h1: Think: does the rule change with the type of road?
q0081.h2: The rule to keep to the right side is a general rule. It does not depend on the type of road.
q0081.p: Correct. Always keep to the right.

q1792.h1: Check each answer: does the law really allow it?
q1792.h2: Lights, wipers and tires must always be in good order. Even by day and in summer, you may not drive a faulty vehicle.
q1792.p: Correct. The vehicle must always be in good order.

q0296.h1: What is the job of the accompanying driver next to a new driver?
q0296.h2: The accompanying driver must watch the road and help the new driver. Someone under the influence of alcohol cannot do that.
q0296.p: Correct. An accompanying driver — only without alcohol.

q0103.h1: The shoulder is the narrow strip at the edge of the road.
q0103.h2: The shoulder is at the edge, beyond the yellow line at the side of the carriageway. It is not part of the lanes. Find the number that marks only that strip.
q0103.p: Correct. The shoulder — at the side, outside the lanes.

q1383.h1: What can you see before a crest? Very little.
q1383.h2: When you can't see far, you won't manage to stop in front of an obstacle. So you slow down to match what you can see.

q1517.h1: Category B is a license for a private car. What is the weight limit?
q1517.h2: Category B allows a private car and a light commercial vehicle, with a maximum authorized mass of up to 3,500 kg.
q1517.p: Correct. Category B — up to 3,500 kg.

q1501.h1: Watch the units: millimetres or centimetres? And what about the spare wheel?
q1501.h2: The tread must be at least 2 mm deep. The spare wheel must meet this too — you may need it.
q1501.p: Correct. 2 mm — the spare wheel too.

q1381.h1: Ask yourself: which way will the car roll if it moves?
q1381.h2: Downhill, the car tends to roll forward. Turn the wheels towards the curb and engage a gear against the direction of the slope.
q1381.p: Correct. Downhill — wheels to the curb, reverse gear.

q0736.h1: An unfamiliar vehicle — what don't you know about it yet?
q0736.h2: Every vehicle has different controls and systems. Before you drive, you must know how to operate it properly.
q0736.p: Correct. First get to know the vehicle, then drive.

q0095.h1: Who gives the notice, and for what reason?
q0095.h2: A police officer, an appraiser or a vehicle examiner may take a vehicle off the road. They do it when the vehicle has a defect or after an accident.
q0095.p: Correct. A defect or an accident — the vehicle comes off the road.

q0171.h1: The horn is not a convenience. When is it really needed?
q0171.h2: In town the horn is only for an imminent danger. And if the danger can be prevented another way, you don't sound it.
q0171.p: Correct. The horn — only to prevent danger.

q1798.h1: Which zone is named for "calming" the traffic?
q1798.h2: A traffic calming zone is meant to slow traffic down. There you must reduce your speed.
q1798.p: Correct. In a traffic calming zone — slow down.

q0777.h1: Who drives slowly and could hold everyone up?
q0777.h2: The shoulder is for slow road users: non-motorized vehicles, tractors and slow-moving vehicles. This way they don't hold up traffic.
q0777.p: Correct. The shoulder — for slow and non-motorized vehicles.

q0300.h1: What does the law assume about someone who refuses the test?
q0300.h2: If refusing had no result, every drunk driver would refuse. So a driver who refuses is treated as driving while intoxicated.
q0300.p: Correct. Refusing the test — like driving drunk.

q0096.h1: Who decides if a passenger may ride on an ATV?
q0096.h2: A passenger is allowed only if the licensing authority permits it. The permit must be registered in the vehicle license.
q0096.p: Correct. ATV passenger — only with a permit in the license.

q1225.h1: What decides here: your license or what the vehicle license says?
q1225.h2: A category B license limits the number of passengers, even if the vehicle is bigger. You may carry up to 8 passengers besides the driver.
q1225.p: Correct. Category B — up to 8 passengers.

q0718.h1: Notice the sign next to the truck, and which way you are turning.
q0718.h2: The sign makes the truck wait; vehicle size does not matter. You are turning left, so you give right of way to the car coming toward you.
q0718.p: Correct. Turning left — wait for the oncoming car.

q1399.h1: A path is not a road. Who is it for?
q1399.h2: A path is a way that is not a road. The definition is broad: it is allocated to a specific type of road user, not necessarily bicycles or pedestrians.
q1399.p: Correct. A path — for a specific type of road user.

q1334.h1: A load that is too high can hit something above it.
q1334.h2: A commercial vehicle up to 3,500 kg has a maximum load height above the road surface: three meters.
q1334.p: Correct. Load — up to three meters above the road.

q0219.h1: Downhill, the vehicle could roll. What holds it in place?
q0219.h2: You need three things: the parking brake, front wheels towards the edge of the road, and reverse gear. In an automatic, the gear rule is different.
q0219.p: Correct. Brake, wheels to the edge, reverse gear.

q0160.h1: Look at the barrier in the picture: is it all the way up?
q0160.h2: A moving barrier, up or down, means the crossing is not clear. You cross only when the barrier is up and not moving.

q0927.h1: Ask yourself: what is the horn for?
q0927.h2: The horn is for preventing danger. You use it only when there is no other way to prevent that danger.
q0927.p: Correct. The horn — only when there's no other way.

q0208.h1: Near a railway crossing you must keep a large distance. How much?
q0208.h2: A vehicle standing close to the crossing blocks the view and gets in the way. So you stop or park only at least 20 meters from the crossing.
q0208.p: Correct. At least 20 meters from the crossing.

q0277.h1: Damage only, nobody hurt. What is the main problem now?
q0277.h2: Vehicles standing in the road block traffic and could cause another accident. Move them and exchange details.
q0277.p: Correct. Damage only — clear the road and exchange details.

q0354.h1: When does a screen distract you from the road?
q0354.h2: A screen while driving takes your eyes off the road. So it is forbidden while the vehicle is moving, except the control and navigation display.

q0793.h1: Think of the shape of the letter U.
q0793.h2: In a U-turn, the vehicle turns around and drives back the way it came.
q0793.p: Correct. U-turn — back in the opposite direction.

q1622.h1: High beam lights up farther than low beam.
q1622.h2: The law sets a minimum distance for each: 100 meters for high beam, 30 meters for low beam.

q0174.h1: Who is already driving on the road you are entering?
q0174.h2: Leaving premises or an access road, you join traffic that is already moving. So you give way to vehicles approaching on that road.

q0211.h1: On a narrow bridge like in the picture, is there room to move aside?
q0211.h2: On a bridge or in a tunnel there is no room to pass a stopped vehicle. So you may not stop there at any time.
q0211.p: Correct. Bridge or tunnel — no stopping.

q0791.h1: What is marked on the road?
q0791.h2: Normally you turn left from the left lane. If several lanes are marked for a left turn, you may also turn from them.
q0791.p: Correct. The markings decide which lane you turn from.

q0715.h1: Look at the sign next to the yellow vehicle.
q0715.h2: The sign makes the yellow vehicle wait, even though it comes from your right. You continue, but carefully and with eye contact — its driver may make a mistake.
q0715.p: Correct. The sign is theirs — still drive with caution.

q1696.h1: A narrow bridge — what if someone comes the other way?
q1696.h2: A narrow bridge has little room. Slow down before the bridge and on it too, so you have time to react.

q0102.h1: The median strip lies between the two carriageways.
q0102.h2: The median strip separates the two directions of traffic. In the illustration it is the strip in the middle, between the carriageways, not at the edge.
q0102.p: Correct. Median strip — between the carriageways.

q0107.h1: Which lane do you turn right from, and into which lane?
q0107.h2: A right turn stays close to the right: from the right lane into the right lane. Drive slowly, without disturbing or endangering anyone.
q0107.p: Correct. Right turn — right lane to right lane.

q1684.h1: Read all the answers. Is each one of them correct?
q1684.h2: The vest is there so that whoever steps onto the shoulder is seen. All the answers describe real rules for using it.
q1684.p: Correct. Stepping onto the shoulder — wear a high-visibility vest.

q0783.h1: Ask yourself: what is marked on the lanes?
q0783.h2: Normally you turn right from the right lane. If more than one lane is marked for a right turn, you may also turn from another marked lane.
q0783.p: Correct. Road markings decide where you turn from.

q1487.h1: Does overtaking change the permitted speed?
q1487.h2: The speed limit always applies, also when overtaking. If you can't overtake without exceeding it, don't overtake.
q1487.p: Correct. Even when overtaking — don't exceed the limit.

q0388.h1: "Calming" means making traffic quieter and slower.
q0388.h2: A traffic calming zone is marked by a sign, and its maximum speed is low: 30 km/h.
q0388.p: Correct. Traffic calming — 30 km/h and a sign.

q0478.h1: Who uses the vehicle, and who is registered as its owner?
q0478.h2: The registered owner and the person driving — both are responsible for the vehicle being roadworthy, at all times.
q0478.p: Correct. The owner and the driver are responsible.

q0719.h1: Look at the signs at the entries of the other two vehicles.
q0719.h2: Each of the two vehicles has a sign that makes it wait. So the way is yours, but you enter the intersection with caution.
q0719.p: Correct. Your right of way — proceed with caution.

q1678.h2: The law requires you to slow down, and even stop, wherever danger is expected. Not just in one particular place.
q1678.p: Correct. Danger expected — slow down, even stop.

q1775.h1: Notice: more than one body has this authority.
q1775.h2: Three bodies may disqualify a license: the Licensing Authority, the court and the Israel Police.
q1775.p: Correct. Licensing Authority, court and police.

q0780.h1: There are two questions here: where may he drive, and how fast?
q0780.h2: A person with paralysed legs may drive in the public transport lane. But the speed limit applies to everyone, even in a hurry.
q0780.p: Correct. The lane is allowed, speeding is not.

q0796.h1: Look at the round signs on the right side of the road.
q0796.h2: The picture shows a sign that prohibits this turn. A turn a sign prohibits stays forbidden, even with care and even with no traffic.
q0796.p: Correct. Here a U-turn is forbidden.

q0323.h1: Where is your home address registered?
q0323.h2: Your home address is registered at the Ministry of Interior. So that is where you report a change.
q0323.p: Correct. Change of address — to the Ministry of Interior.

q1528.h1: What matters more: staying on the road, or avoiding a collision?
q1528.h2: On a narrow road you must make room for the oncoming vehicle. Slow down, move right, and if there is no choice — go off the road.
q1528.p: Correct. Avoid a collision, even by leaving the road.

q1404.h1: Notice: the question is about a trailer for a private passenger vehicle.
q1404.h2: A private passenger vehicle like this may tow only a light trailer. The trailer's gross weight must not exceed 750 kg.
q1404.p: Correct. Here — a trailer up to 750 kg.

q1732.h1: The doctor must know the applicant well. For how long?
q1732.h2: The examining doctor must have treated the applicant for a long time — at least three years. That way he knows the applicant's condition.
q1732.p: Correct. Treating doctor — at least three years.

q0364.h1: Which offenses directly put lives at risk?
q0364.h2: Running a red light and failing to give right-of-way cause serious accidents. A new driver convicted of them does not get a regular license.
q0364.p: Correct. Red light or right-of-way — no regular license.

q0237.h1: Notice the word "only" in the answers.
q0237.h2: The court has broad power. It can disqualify a license, imprison, fine, and impose other penalties set by law.
q0237.p: Correct. The court — all penalties in the law.

q0086.h1: Does the law allow anyone, or is it forbidden for everyone?
q0086.h2: Driving against the direction on a one-way street is forbidden. The exceptions: an emergency vehicle on duty, or a driver a police officer instructed.
q0086.p: Correct. Against the direction — only an emergency vehicle or by police order.

q1681.h1: Notice: a young new driver — and how many passengers?
q1681.h2: A young new driver is limited in the number of passengers. Without an accompanying driver beside him — up to two passengers besides himself.
q1681.p: Correct. Without an accompanying driver — up to two passengers.

q0241.h1: Who controls a vehicle that is being towed?
q0241.h2: A towed vehicle can move suddenly. So apart from the driver, no one may be in it.
q0241.p: Correct. In a towed vehicle — only the driver.

q0232.h1: A regular seat belt fits an adult's body. What about a child?
q0232.h2: A child of this age is too small for the belt alone. He sits in a safety seat or booster seat that fits his height and weight.
q0232.p: Correct. A child — a seat that fits his size.

q1687.h1: Ask yourself: which vehicle, and on which road?
q1687.h2: A private minibus on a motorway, with no other sign, may drive up to 110 km/h.
q1687.p: Correct. Private minibus on a motorway — 110.

q0366.h1: Do the corrective measures replace the penalty, or come on top of it?
q0366.h2: The Licensing Authority and the court act separately. The Authority's corrective measures come in addition to the court's penalty.
q0366.p: Correct. Corrective measures — in addition to the penalty.

q0724.h1: There are no signs at this junction. Who is on each driver's right?
q0724.h2: At a junction with no signs, each driver waits for the vehicle on their right. The one with nobody on their right enters first.
q0724.p: Correct. Give way to the vehicle from the right.

q0653.h1: Notice the age and the word "accompanying".
q0653.h2: Until age 21, a new driver is limited in the number of passengers. When an accompanying driver sits next to him, the limit does not apply.
q0653.p: Correct. Up to two passengers, unless accompanied.

q1686.h1: Which of these offenses is especially dangerous?
q1686.h2: A new driver who drove drunk or on drugs showed he is not ready yet. So he will not get a standard license.
q1686.p: Correct. Alcohol or drugs — no standard license.

q0398.h1: Think: where is stopping a matter of life and death?
q0398.h2: A railway crossing is a very dangerous place. A new driver who did not stop there when needed stays a new driver for two more years.
q0398.p: Correct. Stop before the tracks when needed.

q0230.h1: A regular seat belt is made for an adult, not a small child.
q0230.h2: A small child needs a special seat that fits their size. The seat must be firmly secured to the vehicle.
q0230.p: Correct. A small child sits in a fitting, secured seat.

q1540.h1: The key word is "reasonable". Reasonable compared to what?
q1540.h2: A reasonable speed depends on the road, the weather and the traffic. Even then, you must not go above the permitted speed.
q1540.p: Correct. Fit your speed to conditions, never above the limit.

q0071.h1: Think about the driver's own condition, not the vehicle's.
q0071.h2: A tired, sick or upset driver may endanger others. In such a state he must not drive.
q0071.p: Correct. Drive only when body and mind are fit.

q1745.h1: What is forbidden to do with a solid white line?
q1745.h2: You must not cross the solid line. But if you can overtake without crossing it, overtaking is allowed.
q1745.p: Correct. Overtake only without crossing the solid line.

q0155.h1: The picture shows a railway crossing. What must you be able to do before it?
q0155.h2: A train cannot stop quickly. So you slow down enough to be able to stop before the tracks if needed.
q0155.p: Correct. Near the tracks, slow down and be ready to stop.

q1727.h2: A B license is for a light vehicle. A private minibus is allowed if its gross weight is not over 3,500 kg.
q1727.p: Correct. With a B license — up to 3,500 kg.

q0100.h1: Is any type of vehicle exempt from seat belts?
q0100.h2: The seat belt duty applies in a cargo tractor too. It applies to the driver and to everyone riding with him.
q0100.p: Correct. In a tractor too — everyone buckles up.

q0159.h1: What helps you hear an approaching train?
q0159.h2: At a "Stop" sign you stop completely. Near the tracks you also listen: silence the noise in the car and open a window.
q0159.p: Correct. Stop, silence the car, listen for the train.

q0101.h1: A lane is one strip, from one marking line to the next.
q0101.h2: A lane is a strip of the carriageway for one file of vehicles. Find the number that starts at a white line and ends at the next marking line.
q0101.p: Correct. A lane is a strip for one file.

q0146.h1: Think: when do you need to check that the brakes work?
q0146.h2: You may brake hard to test the brakes. But only when it does not disturb or endanger anyone.
q0146.p: Correct. Brake tests — only without endangering others.

q0242.h1: The points system is meant to correct drivers, not only punish them.
q0242.h2: A driver with this many points needs to learn again how to drive correctly. He gets a course and must take a test.
q0242.p: Correct. Many points — a course and a test.

q0795.h1: Read all the options. Maybe more than one is right?
q0795.h2: A U-turn is forbidden where a sign forbids it. It is also forbidden where other drivers cannot see you, like near a crest or a bend.
q0795.p: Correct. U-turn only where visible and allowed.

q1533.h1: Towing is heavy and dangerous work.
q1533.h2: Such a vehicle tows only one vehicle. A different number is allowed only with the Licensing Authority's approval.
q1533.p: Correct. Tow one vehicle, unless approved otherwise.

q0278.h1: The owner is not there. How will he know who hit it?
q0278.h2: You must not just drive away. Leave your details where they can be seen, and report to the police.
q0278.p: Correct. Leave your details and report to the police.

q1283.h1: Think which vehicle is different from all the others.
q1283.h2: A warning triangle must be in every motor vehicle, trailers too. Only a motorcycle is exempt.
q1283.p: Correct. Triangle in every motor vehicle, except a motorcycle.

q1788.h1: Ask yourself: what was the fine for?
q1788.h2: The Licensing Authority can delay a license because of a fine. But only a fine for a traffic offense.
q1788.p: Correct. A traffic fine can delay renewal.

q0170.h1: Think: what is the horn for?
q0170.h2: The horn is for warning, not for annoying. So you sound it only as much as needed, no more.
q0170.p: Correct. Keep the horn short, only as needed.

q1357.h1: What happens to the trailer when the towing vehicle turns?
q1357.h2: The chains must not be too short. They must let the trailer turn at a wide angle relative to the towing vehicle.
q1357.p: Correct. The chains allow a 90-degree turn.

q0265.h1: How will the pedestrian see the cars that are coming?
q0265.h2: A pedestrian on the road must see the vehicles coming toward him. That way he can step aside in time.
q0265.p: Correct. Walk on the left, facing traffic.

q1755.h2: In town there are many people, junctions and pedestrian crossings. So the permitted speed there is fairly low.
q1755.p: Correct. On an urban road — up to 50 km/h.

q1736.h1: In whose name is the vehicle registered?
q1736.h2: The responsibility is on the registered owner. He is released only if he proves he was not driving and names the driver.
q1736.p: Correct. The owner is responsible, unless he names the driver.

q1685.h1: Which of these offenses puts lives at risk on the road?
q1685.h2: A new driver who drove faster than allowed showed he is not ready yet. So he will not get a regular license.

q1722.h1: In neutral, the engine does not help you slow down.
q1722.h2: Going downhill in neutral, the car speeds up and the brakes work too hard. You lose control of the vehicle.
q1722.p: Correct. Downhill, stay in gear, not neutral.

q1568.h1: Who needs to know the vehicle was changed?
q1568.h2: A change to a vehicle can affect safety. So you need written approval from the Licensing Authority before the change.
q1568.p: Correct. Change a vehicle only after written approval.

q0335.h1: What happens if a driver is no longer fit to drive?
q0335.h2: The Licensing Authority protects road safety. If a driver is not fit to drive, or not medically fit, it can take away his license.
q0335.p: Correct. An unfit driver — the Authority can disqualify.

q0240.h1: Where will the cargo not get in the way or fall?
q0240.h2: You may carry cargo in a private vehicle. Put it only in the places in the car meant for it, so it stays stable and safe.
q0240.p: Correct. Cargo goes only where it is meant to.

q0082.h1: The carriageway includes the lanes, without the shoulder or the median.
q0082.h2: A road also includes a shoulder and a median. The carriageway is only the part where vehicles drive. Find the number that covers only it.
q0082.p: Correct. Carriageway — the part where vehicles drive.

q0729.h1: Look at the signals above the lanes. What is above your lane?
q0729.h2: Above your lane there is a diagonal arrow. It means your lane ends, and you must move carefully to the lane it points to.
q0729.p: Correct. Diagonal arrow — move to the lane it shows.

q0267.h1: The key words are "for the first time".
q0267.h2: Anyone who got a license for the first time needs an accompanying driver. This is true for a private car, and for a light truck C1.
q0267.p: Correct. First license — drive with an accompanying driver.

q0308.h1: Do you need another offence to be considered drunk?
q0308.h2: It is enough that the alcohol in the blood is above the legal level. No other offence is needed.
q0308.p: Correct. Alcohol above the limit — you are drunk.

q0295.h1: Drugs and alcohol affect how you react on the road.
q0295.h2: Alcohol and drugs slow your reactions and harm your judgment. So there is no case where driving under them is allowed.
q0295.p: Correct. Drugs or alcohol — never drive.

q1488.h1: "Taken off the road". What does that say about driving it?
q1488.h2: A vehicle taken off the road does not move on the road. The exception: driving to the nearest garage, if approved on the form.
q1488.p: Correct. Off-road vehicle — only to the garage, with approval.

q1713.h1: The brakes are among the most important parts for safety.
q1713.h2: A lit brake light means there may be a brake fault. Without working brakes you must not keep driving.
q1713.p: Correct. Brake light on — stop, don't continue.

q1294.h1: What comes out of the vehicle and harms everyone?
q1294.h2: A police officer can stop a vehicle for inspection because of harm to the public. Polluting smoke from the engine harms everyone's air.
q1294.p: Correct. Air pollution — a reason to stop a vehicle for inspection.

q1325.h1: Must every vehicle have an extinguisher, or are there exceptions?
q1325.h2: Most motor vehicles must carry a fire extinguisher. A few types are exempt, including the private passenger vehicle.
q1325.p: Correct. Extinguisher in most motor vehicles, with exceptions.

q0090.h1: On a one-way road, everyone drives in the same direction.
q0090.h2: On a one-way road there is no oncoming traffic. So you may pass the obstacle on either side, unless marked otherwise.
q0090.p: Correct. One-way — pass on the right or the left.

q1748.h1: Why don't we park close to a pedestrian crossing?
q1748.h2: A car parked near the crossing hides the pedestrians. So parking a short distance before the crossing is forbidden.
q1748.p: Correct. No parking 12 meters before a crossing.

q1548.h1: Which is more important: a dirt track or a paved road?
q1548.h2: Someone leaving a dirt track joins traffic that is already moving. So he waits for the vehicles on the paved road.
q1548.p: Correct. From a dirt track, give way.

q0216.h1: Look at the symbol on the sign. Who is the spot for?
q0216.h2: The spot is kept for a disabled person's vehicle with the tag on the sign. Other vehicles do not stop there, even when it is empty.
q0216.p: Correct. Disabled spot — only for a vehicle with the tag.

q0112.h1: Look at the solid line on street C, and at your lanes on street A.
q0112.h2: Turn left from your left lane. Street C is two-way, so enter the first lane past the solid line — not the one beside it.
q0112.p: Correct. From the left, into the lane next to the line.

q1641.h1: Why were the restrictions written on the licence?
q1641.h2: A restriction on the licence is a must, not advice. The driver has to drive according to what it says.
q1641.p: Correct. What's written on the licence is binding.

q0307.h1: What may a police officer demand from you?
q0307.h2: A police officer may demand an intoxication test. A driver must not refuse it, whatever kind of test it is.
q0307.p: Correct. You must not refuse an intoxication test.

q0709.h1: What does the sign on the right, at your entry, say?
q0709.h2: There is a Give Way sign at your entry. So you wait for everyone crossing your path, from both directions — not just one of them.
q0709.p: Correct. Give way to everyone who has priority.

q0341.h1: What must be in order before a vehicle passes to a new owner?
q0341.h2: A vehicle passes to a new owner only when it is "clean". Everything is paid, and it has no lien, encumbrance or other restriction.
q0341.p: Correct. Ownership passes only when the vehicle is clean.

q0284.h1: A loud noise is a sign that something in the car is wrong.
q0284.h2: Unreasonable noise disturbs others and may point to a fault. So you must not drive such a vehicle.
q0284.p: Correct. Too noisy a vehicle — don't drive it.

q0247.h1: What makes a vehicle an "emergency vehicle" while driving?
q0247.h2: An emergency vehicle is an approved rescue vehicle, like an ambulance, police or fire service. It counts as one when its flashing light and siren are on.
q0247.p: Correct. Emergency vehicle — flashing light and siren on.

q1797.h1: Think: where does the light change suddenly and the road is closed in?
q1797.h2: Entering a tunnel, your eyes need to adjust to different light, and the space is narrow and closed. So slow down at the entrance and inside.
q1797.p: Correct. In a tunnel, slow down.

q0303.h1: Notice: the sentence is written in the negative.
q0303.h2: The law forbids driving under the influence of drugs. Check whether the sentence in the question says that, or the opposite.
q0303.p: Correct. The law forbids driving on drugs.

q0764.h1: On a two-way road, the left side belongs to oncoming traffic.
q0764.h2: You park in the direction of travel. Only on a one-way road that is not part of a divided road may you park on the left too.
q0764.p: Correct. On the left — only on a one-way road.

q0339.h1: "New driver" is a short starting period.
q0339.h2: A new driver's license is limited in time. After that period, if all is in order, you get a regular license.
q0339.p: Correct. A new driver's license — two years.

q0758.h1: How many files of vehicles fit in one lane?
q0758.h2: The carriageway is divided into strips along its length. Each strip is wide enough for one file of cars.
q0758.p: Correct. A lane — width for one file.

q1547.h1: Sudden braking can make the car behind crash into you.
q1547.h2: Sudden braking endangers whoever is driving behind you. Use it only when there is no other way to prevent an accident.
q1547.p: Correct. Sudden braking — only to prevent an accident.

q1444.h1: Overtaking on a two-way road means entering the oncoming lane.
q1444.h2: To overtake safely you must see the road ahead well. When visibility is poor, you cannot know who is coming toward you.

q0092.h1: A license that ran out long ago. Can you just renew it?
q0092.h2: After a long time without a valid license, renewing is not enough. You must pass the checks and tests the Licensing Authority sets.
q0092.p: Correct. Over one year — tests before renewal.

q0734.h1: When do you need the vest, and where are you then?
q0734.h2: You put on the vest before you step out of the car onto the road. So it must be close, near the driver.
q0734.p: Correct. Keep the vest near the driver.

q0073.h1: In a faulty vehicle, do you have full control?
q0073.h2: A faulty vehicle may not brake or steer as it should. So you must not drive it.
q0073.p: Correct. Drive only a vehicle in working order.

q0066.h1: Which counts more: a sign or a person directing traffic?
q0066.h2: A military police officer's instruction comes before the sign. Obey it, but carefully, because other drivers may not have noticed.
q0066.p: Correct. Obey the military police officer, carefully.

q0559.h1: Ask yourself: what could forbid a U-turn in a lane?
q0559.h2: A U-turn is allowed from a left-turn lane. It is also allowed from another lane, as long as no sign or marking forbids it.
q0559.p: Correct. U-turn — if nothing in the lane forbids it.

q1674.h1: The law gives a new driver a chance to prove himself again.
q1674.h2: After such an offense the authority can test him again. If he passes, the new driver period starts over.
q1674.p: Correct. Retests, then a new driver again.

q0091.h1: Notice the special vehicle and its weight.
q0091.h2: A category B license lets you drive a disabled person's vehicle listed as a special medical vehicle. Its gross weight must be up to 4,000 kg.
q0091.p: Correct. Medical vehicle for a disabled person — up to 4,000 kg.

q0233.h1: A very small baby needs special protection for the back and head.
q0233.h2: A baby rides in the safety seat facing backward. This way the seat supports his back and head when braking.
q0233.p: Correct. A baby rides facing backward.

q0712.h1: What sign is at your entry? And which side does each one come from?
q0712.h2: There is a Stop sign at your entry, so you wait for both. The cyclist comes from the bus's right, so the bus waits for the cyclist.

q0274.h1: Why is it important that the accident scene stays as it is?
q0274.h2: The police need to see how the accident happened. So don't move the vehicle, unless a police officer says so or it is needed to evacuate casualties.
q0274.p: Correct. Don't move the vehicle, except to evacuate casualties.

q1043.h1: What rises from the fuel while refueling, and what could ignite it?
q1043.h2: Fuel gives off vapors that catch fire easily. A running engine can make a spark, and the spark can ignite them.
q1043.p: Correct. Turn off the engine before refueling.

q0314.h1: What does alcohol do to the driver's brain and eyes?
q0314.h2: Alcohol harms vision. With a large amount, the driver sees less to the sides, and the field of vision is impaired.
q0314.p: Correct. Alcohol harms the driver's vision.

q1417.h1: What did the water do to your brakes?
q1417.h2: Wet brakes work less well. Driving slowly and pressing the brake pedal lightly dries them, until braking is normal again.
q1417.p: Correct. After water, dry the brakes gently.

q1298.h1: What is the job of the headlights?
q1298.h2: Headlights must light the road as the law requires. A headlight that is not aimed lights the wrong place.
q1298.p: Correct. Headlights must be properly aimed.

q1518.h1: What really gets rid of tiredness?
q1518.h2: Fatigue does not go away with tricks while driving. What helps the body is rest, so you need to stop.

q1508.h1: What happens to the driver himself after many hours?
q1508.h2: After many hours of driving, the driver gets tired. Fatigue can lead to falling asleep at the wheel.
q1508.p: Correct. Long driving makes the driver tired.

q0855.h1: The danger is in the driver's body, not the vehicle.
q0855.h2: Many hours of driving are tiring. A tired driver may fall asleep while driving.

q0801.h1: What is hard to see when reversing?
q0801.h2: When reversing, it is hard to see around the vehicle. So you keep looking in all directions and move slowly.
q0801.p: Correct. Reversing: look all around, go slowly.

q1721.h1: When do you use the parking brake?
q1721.h2: The parking brake holds the vehicle in place. It keeps the vehicle from moving while it stands.
q1721.p: Correct. The parking brake stops the vehicle moving.

q1044.h1: What keeps the vehicle from moving when the engine starts?
q1044.h2: Before starting, the vehicle must be secured. The parking brake should be engaged, so the vehicle does not move suddenly.
q1044.p: Correct. Check the parking brake before starting.

q1679.h1: When should you slow down — before the curve or in it?
q1679.h2: The vehicle stays stable when you enter a curve slowly. Slow down before entering, and speed up a little as you exit.
q1679.p: Correct. Slow down before the curve, not in it.

q0870.h1: What does the driver gain when the seat fits his body?
q0870.h2: A well-adjusted seat lets you see the road comfortably. Driving becomes easier and less tiring.
q0870.p: Correct. An adjusted seat means comfortable driving.

q1529.h1: What does water on the road do to the wheels' grip?
q1529.h2: On a wet road it is harder to stop and control the vehicle. So slow down and drive at a speed that suits the conditions.
q1529.p: Correct. On a wet road, slow down.

q1699.h1: A panoramic mirror shows a wide area. What happens to size?
q1699.h2: To show a wide area, the mirror makes what you see smaller. So objects look smaller and farther than they really are.
q1699.p: Correct. In a panoramic mirror, things look farther.

q1715.h1: A poorly maintained road holds surprises. What gives you time to react?
q1715.h2: A poorly maintained road has holes and obstacles. When you drive slowly and pay attention, you have time to react.
q1715.p: Correct. Bad road: slow down, stay alert.

q1509.h1: When should you rest — only on the way, or also before?
q1509.h2: A driver should start out well rested. On a long drive, you also need to stop for long rest breaks.
q1509.p: Correct. Rest before driving and on the way.

q0800.h1: Look at the word "blind". What can't the driver do there?
q0800.h2: A blind spot is an area near the vehicle that the driver cannot see. Anyone inside it is also hidden from the driver.
q0800.p: Correct. The driver cannot see into a blind spot.

q1754.h1: Where does a rear camera look?
q1754.h2: A rear camera films only what is behind the vehicle. It shows the driver an area he cannot see himself.
q1754.p: Correct. A rear camera shows only the back.

q0820.h1: Which method does not depend on guessing distance?
q0820.h2: It is hard to guess distance by eye. Count time: the vehicle ahead passes a point, and you count until you reach it.
q0820.p: Correct. Count seconds, don't guess distance.

q1554.h1: When is it easiest to decide who drives — before or after?
q1554.h2: After drinking, it is hard to judge well. So decide in advance who the driver is, and he drinks no alcohol at all.
q1554.p: Correct. Choose the driver in advance; he doesn't drink.

q1292.h1: What does oil do to the tires' grip on the road?
q1292.h2: On oil, tires slide easily. Hard braking can cause a skid, so slow down gently.
q1292.p: Correct. On oil, don't brake hard.

q1082.h1: Which equipment protects the body at the moment of impact?
q1082.h2: In an accident, the body is thrown forward and back. Seat belts, airbags and head restraints hold and cushion the body.
q1082.p: Correct. Belts, airbags and head restraints protect you.

q1293.h1: What happens to the vehicle when it hits a bump fast?
q1293.h2: Bumps and cracks shake the vehicle and make control harder. So slow down and drive to suit the road.

q1523.h1: What does the word "narrow" tell you about the place?
q1523.h2: A narrow bridge has little room and nowhere to escape. So slow down as you approach, and keep slow on the bridge.
q1523.p: Correct. Cross a narrow bridge slowly.

q0799.h1: Who can't you see when you reverse?
q0799.h2: When reversing, there are areas the driver cannot see. A person standing there may get hit.
q0799.p: Correct. Reversing: beware of people you can't see.

q1060.h1: What did the water do to the brakes?
q1060.h2: Wet brakes do not work as usual. Drive slowly until they dry and work normally again.
q1060.p: Correct. After a puddle, drive slowly.

q1296.h1: When the sun is behind you, where does it shine? Who suffers?
q1296.h2: When the sun is behind you, oncoming drivers look into the sun. Your lights help them see you.
q1296.p: Correct. Sun behind you? Turn on lights.

q0823.h1: Before overtaking, what must you be sure of?
q0823.h2: Start overtaking only when it is allowed, and when it is completely clear you can finish it safely.

q0749.h1: What does the driver behind you see when you keep right?
q0749.h2: When you keep right, you do not block the whole road. The driver behind you sees more of what is ahead.
q0749.p: Correct. Keeping right helps the driver behind.

q1071.h1: What does the driver need from the seat: comfort, or control too?
q1071.h2: Sitting correctly lets you reach the wheel and pedals easily. It also helps you see the road better.
q1071.p: Correct. Right seating means control and vision.

q0821.h1: When does it take you longer to see danger or stop?
q0821.h2: With poor visibility, a slippery road, or a tired driver, you need more time and space. So keep a bigger gap.
q0821.p: Correct. Hard conditions mean a bigger gap.

q0864.h1: What do you do before the vehicle even moves?
q0864.h2: Before moving off, look carefully at the road and traffic. That way you see danger before you drive into it.

q1503.h1: Wind pushes on the vehicle. What does that change?
q1503.h2: The wind presses on the vehicle. It can push it off its path and slow it down.
q1503.p: Correct. Wind affects stability and speed.

q0313.h1: What does alcohol do to the brain that controls the body?
q0313.h2: Alcohol affects the brain. It becomes harder to move hands and feet together and precisely.

q1183.h1: A cyclist may swerve suddenly. How much room will you leave?
q1183.h2: A cyclist can lose balance. So pass on his left, and leave as much space between you as you can.
q1183.p: Correct. Keep your distance from cyclists.

q1563.h1: When you see less, what should happen to your speed?
q1563.h2: The sun dazzles you, so you see less of the road. Drive slowly enough to react to what you can see.

q0740.h1: On a long descent, what keeps the brakes from overheating?
q0740.h2: Pressing the brake constantly downhill heats it up. A low gear helps slow the car, and you brake intermittently.
q0740.p: Correct. Downhill: low gear, brake on and off.

q0813.h1: Look at the word "braking". When does braking start?
q0813.h2: Braking distance starts when the foot presses the brake pedal. It ends when the vehicle stops completely.
q0813.p: Correct. Braking: from pressing to stopping.

q1510.h1: A short break helps. But for how long?
q1510.h2: Getting out to refresh helps a little. It does not replace real rest, and the fatigue comes back fast.
q1510.p: Correct. Refreshing helps only for a short time.

q0750.h1: What is on the left side of your lane?
q0750.h2: To your left, vehicles come from the opposite direction. When you keep right, there is more space between you.
q0750.p: Correct. Keeping right gives space from oncoming traffic.

q1072.h1: What directly touches your body while driving?
q1072.h2: Your body sits on the seat, leans on the backrest and holds the steering wheel. Adjust all of them to sit comfortably and safely.
q1072.p: Correct. Adjust seat, backrest and steering wheel.

q0840.h1: Mountains have long descents and sharp curves. What can go wrong?
q0840.h2: On long descents, the brakes may stop working well. On sharp curves, you may drift into oncoming traffic or off the road.
q0840.p: Correct. Drive very carefully on mountain roads.

q0301.h1: Compare the amount of alcohol, not the size of the glass.
q0301.h2: A can of beer has more liquid, but whiskey is stronger. In the end, the effect on the driver is about the same.
q0301.p: Correct. Beer affects you about like whiskey.

q0763.h1: Before changing lanes, who do you need to look at?
q0763.h2: Vehicles are already driving in the new lane. Check where they are and how fast, and only then move over.
q0763.p: Correct. Check the lane first, then move.

q0761.h1: Is signaling alone enough? What else must you check?
q0761.h2: Signaling tells others what you will do, so give it in time. Before you start moving over, look around and in the mirrors.
q0761.p: Correct. Signal in time and check before moving.

q0779.h1: Before entering an intersection — what matters most?
q0779.h2: Don't enter an intersection you can't get out of. First check it is clear and that you can cross it safely to the end.

q1534.h1: A crosswind pushes the vehicle sideways. What helps you control it?
q1534.h2: A strong side wind moves the vehicle, especially one with a large side. Driving slower makes it easier to control.
q1534.p: Correct. In a strong crosswind, slow down.

q1490.h1: Look at the word "reaction". What happens during that time?
q1490.h2: Reaction distance is how far the vehicle goes while the driver reacts. It starts when he sees danger and ends when he starts acting.
q1490.p: Correct. Reaction: from seeing to starting to act.

q1476.h1: Picture sand on a smooth floor. What happens to your foot?
q1476.h2: Sand between the tire and the road reduces grip. The tires hold less, and the vehicle may skid.
q1476.p: Correct. Sand on the road causes skidding.

q0838.h1: How is the shoulder different from the road under the wheels?
q0838.h2: With one wheel on the road and one on the shoulder, each grips differently. Braking then can spin the vehicle.
q0838.p: Correct. On the shoulder, brake very carefully.

q0315.h1: After bright light, what does alcohol change for your eyes?
q0315.h2: After glare, the eyes need time to see again. Alcohol slows this, so the driver stays dazzled longer.
q0315.p: Correct. Alcohol makes glare last longer.

q0760.h1: What do you miss when you swerve suddenly?
q0760.h2: A sudden swerve leaves no time to check the lane. A vehicle you did not see may be there, and you may hit it.
q0760.p: Correct. Check well before changing lanes.

q0868.h1: What can you see far away before you get there?
q0868.h2: Looking far ahead shows you early what is happening on the road. You can plan your drive in advance, and nothing surprises you.
q0868.p: Well done. Looking far ahead prevents surprises.

q1389.h1: Is a medicine without a prescription always harmless?
q1389.h2: Even a medicine bought without a doctor's prescription can adversely affect driving. The season of the year does not change this.
q1389.p: Correct. Non-prescription medicines can affect driving too.

q0877.h1: Notice the word "always". What is true every time you reverse?
q0877.h2: The answer must fit every vehicle and every road. Every time you reverse, be careful and act so you do not endanger, injure, bother or obstruct anyone.

q1075.h1: What does the driver look through to see the road?
q1075.h2: The driver sees the road through the windscreens. Dirt on them hides part of what the driver needs to see.
q1075.p: Correct. Clean windscreens mean clear vision.

q1054.h1: How does the car itself tell you something is wrong?
q1054.h2: Warning lights on the dashboard warn about a problem in the vehicle. Before driving, check that none of them is lit.
q1054.p: Correct. Check the warning lights before driving.

q0818.h1: How does a driver feel with space in front?
q0818.h2: A suitable gap from the vehicle in front lowers stress. Driving is calmer, does not tire you, and prevents dangers.
q0818.p: Well done. A good gap means calm driving.

q1542.h1: Where does the high beam reach, and who is there?
q1542.h2: High beam shines strong and far. In the dark it reaches the eyes of other drivers and dazzles them.

q0836.h1: What should drivers on the road know before you move?
q0836.h2: First you tell others what you are about to do. Only after that do you turn the wheel and enter the road.

q0837.h1: Notice the word "unplanned". What could force you off the road?
q0837.h2: You leave the road without a plan only when something surprising and obstructing appears in your lane. A phone or the air conditioning is not a reason.
q0837.p: Correct. Only a sudden obstacle in your lane.

q0822.h1: What must be true to finish a long overtake safely?
q0822.h2: Overtaking several vehicles takes more road. It is allowed when overtaking is not prohibited and the overtaking lane has enough distance to finish without risk.
q0822.p: Correct. Overtake only with enough room.

q0316.h1: Does alcohol affect only some people, or only at some hours?
q0316.h2: Drinking alcohol harms visual acuity. It does not happen only at night, and not only to people who wear glasses.

q0835.h1: Three actions: what to check, what to signal, how to move?
q0835.h2: Check the traffic on the road and give a suitable signal. The move onto the road itself is gradual, not rushed.
q0835.p: Correct. Check, signal, move on gradually.

q1791.h1: What can cover the road and make it slippery?
q1791.h2: The risk of skidding is especially high when the road surface is slippery. This happens in the first rain, and when there is mud or oil on the road.
q1791.p: Correct. First rain, mud and oil: take care.

q1076.h1: Is the car in the mirror as far away as it looks?
q1076.h2: A panoramic mirror shows a wide area. But the distance of what you see in it does not look like the real distance.
q1076.p: Correct. Distances in a panoramic mirror mislead.

q1493.h1: When you see less, what should happen to your speed and lights?
q1493.h2: When visibility is limited, slow down and match your speed to what you can see. Turn on the low-beam headlights, not the high beam.
q1493.p: Correct. Poor visibility: slow down, low beams on.

q0273.h1: Who decides where an LPG vehicle may park?
q0273.h2: An LPG vehicle parks only in a lot where it is permitted. The guidelines for this come from the Ministry of Environmental Protection.
q0273.p: Correct. The guidelines come from the Environment Ministry.

q1063.h1: Is there any parking where you can skip the parking brake?
q1063.h2: Apply the parking brake every time you park. Not only uphill, not only downhill, and not only on a wet road.
q1063.p: Correct. Every time you park, use the parking brake.

q0748.h1: Think about the vehicle that wants to overtake you.
q0748.h2: When you keep to the right, there is room on your left. That way a vehicle overtaking you can do it safely.
q0748.p: Correct. Keep right and let others overtake.

q1006.h1: Two questions: which gear, and what speed?
q1006.h2: On a flooded road, drive carefully. Use a low gear and drive slowly, not fast.
q1006.p: Correct. In water: low gear, slow.

q1492.h1: What does the left signal tell you about its plan?
q1492.h2: The signal says the vehicle may move to the left. You must take this into account and let it do so.
q1492.p: Correct. It signals? Let it move over.

q1701.h1: On a wet road, what can you change yourself?
q1701.h2: On a wet road, the risk of skidding depends on speed. The faster you drive, the greater the risk.
q1701.p: Correct. On a wet road, drive slower.

q1491.h1: What is the stopping distance made of?
q1491.h2: The stopping distance includes the reaction distance and the braking distance. So it is greater than the braking distance alone.
q1491.p: Correct. Stopping is reaction plus braking.

q0766.h1: What do you check even before you start slowing down?
q0766.h2: First check whether stopping there is permitted. Then look all around. Only then slow down carefully.
q0766.p: Correct. Check, look around, then slow down.

q1709.h1: Think about the drivers coming toward you in the dark.
q1709.h2: High beam is very strong. In the dark it can dazzle other drivers and make it hard for them to see.

q0194.h1: Which gear do you use downhill, and how do you choose it?
q0194.h2: On a long descent, engage a low gear. How low? According to the slope of the road.
q0194.p: Correct. Downhill: low gear, matched to the slope.

q0145.h1: Is emergency braking the first solution or the last?
q0145.h2: Emergency braking is allowed to prevent an accident when there is no other way to prevent it.
q0145.p: Correct. Emergency braking only when there's no choice.

q0737.h1: All the answers include the parking brake. What is different?
q0737.h2: An automatic gearbox has a special position for parking, P. Engage it and also apply the parking brake.
q0737.p: Correct. Parking: P plus the parking brake.

q0858.h1: What can you see when you face the traffic?
q0858.h2: When you walk to the car from the front, your face is toward the traffic. That way you see the vehicles coming.
q0858.p: Correct. Approach your car facing the traffic.

q0857.h1: How long does a short break help?
q0857.h2: A short break relieves fatigue, but not for long. It helps only for a short time.
q0857.p: Correct. A short break helps briefly.

q1061.h1: What leaves the engine, and where can it go indoors?
q1061.h2: The engine gives off burnt gases. These gases are toxic to humans, and in a closed space they have nowhere to go.

q0732.h1: What keeps the car from moving, and helps you sit right?
q0732.h2: First make sure the parking brake is engaged, and adjust the driver's seat. Only after that start the engine and drive.
q0732.p: Correct. Parking brake on, seat adjusted.

q1481.h1: What do you control that affects this force?
q1481.h2: Centrifugal force grows with speed. So slow down in turns and on curves, and the force gets smaller.
q1481.p: Correct. In a turn, slow down.

q0856.h1: Think of two times: before the drive and during it.
q0856.h2: Get enough rest before you start driving. On the way, stop for breaks to rest and refresh.
q0856.p: Correct. Rest before, and take breaks.

q1558.h1: Two questions: what about the wheel, and how to brake?
q1558.h2: With a puncture, grip the steering wheel firmly and do not let go. Brake moderately, not hard.

q1497.h1: Notice: the distance is measured from when you already pressed the brake.
q1497.h2: Your reaction time is already over when you press the brake. The remaining distance depends on speed: the faster you drive, the longer it gets.

q1580.h1: Which pedal should your foot press while the car stands?
q1580.h2: Before shifting from P to another gear, press firmly on the brake pedal. Not the gas pedal and not the clutch.
q1580.p: Correct. Leave P with your foot on the brake.

q1719.h1: Look for factors linked to the driver and their control.
q1719.h2: Important causes of losing control are driving too fast, not being alert, and not knowing the vehicle's mechanisms.
q1719.p: Correct. Speed, alertness, knowing your vehicle.

q0865.h1: Do the mirrors alone show you everything?
q0865.h2: Look in the mirrors, and also turn your head toward where you want to move. That is how you check the road when you start driving.
q0865.p: Correct. Mirrors, then turn your head.

q1598.h1: When you see less, what should grow and what should shrink?
q1598.h2: In poor visibility, slow down. Also keep a larger than usual gap from the vehicle in front, and do not stay close to it.
q1598.p: Correct. Poor visibility: slower and farther back.

q0845.h1: Look for a force pushing away from the turn's center.
q0845.h2: In a turn, a force pushes the vehicle outward, away from the center. This is the centrifugal force.

q0827.h1: Which tool, for how long, and when is it needed at all?
q0827.h2: On a non-urban road you may honk, but lightly. Do it before you pass the vehicle, and only if it is needed.
q0827.p: Correct. A light honk, only if needed.

q0762.h1: Which answer includes checking before you move?
q0762.h2: First look in the mirrors and check the new lane. Then signal and make sure you can move over. Only then move gently, diagonally.
q0762.p: Correct. Check, signal, then move gently.

q0317.h1: Does alcohol harm only some drivers?
q0317.h2: Drinking alcohol impairs your ability to judge distances and speeds. It does not happen only to young drivers or only to people who wear glasses.
q0317.p: Correct. Alcohol distorts distances and speeds.

q0828.h1: On a one-way road, who can be in the left lane?
q0828.h2: On a one-way road there is no oncoming traffic. Vehicles in the left lane go in your direction, and swerving left may disturb them.
q0828.p: Correct. Before swerving, check the left lane.

q0817.h1: Think about brakes and fuel when you keep a gap.
q0817.h2: A suitable gap from the vehicle in front is good for the car itself too. The brakes wear less, and the engine uses less fuel.
q0817.p: Correct. A good gap saves fuel and brakes.

q1332.h1: Can a moving vehicle stop in a single moment?
q1332.h2: Even in emergency braking, the vehicle does not stop on the spot. It keeps going a certain distance, and only then stops.
q1332.p: Correct. Even hard braking takes distance.

q1693.h1: Does more speed give you more control?
q1693.h2: Control of the vehicle also depends on speed. At a reasonable speed you control the vehicle better than at a high speed.

q0833.h1: Notice: the shoulder is lower. How do you move onto it?
q0833.h2: First slow the vehicle to a low speed. Only then move onto the shoulder, gradually and not all at once.
q0833.p: Correct. Slow down, then move over gradually.

q0861.h1: How is the mirror set? Which part of your car shows?
q0861.h2: In the side mirrors you see the edge of the vehicle's side. The rest of the mirror shows the road at the sides of the vehicle.
q0861.p: Correct. Mirror: car edge and the road beside.

q0860.h1: Which window does the interior mirror look through?
q0860.h2: The interior mirror shows what is visible through the rear window. Adjust it so you also see as much as possible on both sides of it.
q0860.p: Correct. The interior mirror is aimed at the rear window.

q1559.h1: When the sun dazzles you, how far can you really see?
q1559.h2: The sun shortens your range of vision. So you slow down to match what you can see, and you use the sun visor.
q1559.p: Correct. Slow down and use the sun visor.

q1738.h1: What might children do when they get out of a vehicle?
q1738.h2: A child getting out of a vehicle may suddenly appear on the road. So slow down, drive at a reasonable speed and be ready to stop.
q1738.p: Correct. Near children, slow down and be ready to stop.

q0893.h1: No one is on the crossing. What about people next to it?
q0893.h2: A pedestrian may reach the crossing at the last moment. So slow down and make sure no pedestrians are near the crossing.
q0893.p: Correct. Slow down even when the crossing is empty.

q0797.h1: A U-turn crosses the whole road. What do you check first?
q0797.h2: A U-turn is not allowed everywhere, and it crosses traffic. So first make sure it is permitted and does not obstruct traffic.
q0797.p: Correct. U-turn only when permitted and not obstructing.

q0738.h1: Think: what can the car do the moment you engage a gear?
q0738.h2: Once a gear is engaged, an automatic car can start to move. So first press the foot brake pedal, and the car stays in place.
q0738.p: Correct. Foot brake first, then the lever.

q0824.h1: How fast are you going compared to the vehicle ahead?
q0824.h2: When the speed difference is small, overtaking takes a long time. So one condition for overtaking is a big speed difference between the two vehicles.
q0824.p: Correct. Overtake when the speed difference is significant.

q0876.h1: Is there any situation where reversing fast is okay?
q0876.h2: When reversing, it is hard to see. This is true by day or night, uphill or downhill, in light or heavy vehicles. So always reverse slowly.

q0874.h1: What comes first: slowing down or changing gear?
q0874.h2: First you slow the vehicle down. Only after the speed has dropped do you shift to a lower gear that suits the new speed.
q0874.p: Correct. Slow down first, then a lower gear.

q0808.h1: At high speed, the road comes faster. What does that mean?
q0808.h2: The problem is not the driver's reaction time. At high speed the vehicle reaches the danger quickly, so the time to react correctly is very limited.
q0808.p: Correct. High speed leaves little time to react.

q0859.h1: What must you fit to your body before starting the engine?
q0859.h2: First fit the vehicle to the driver: the seat, steering wheel, mirrors and head restraints. Then you see well and control the vehicle from the start.

q1531.h1: What can you see when you drive close behind a large vehicle?
q1531.h2: A large vehicle hides the road ahead of it. A greater than usual distance lets you see more and stop in time.
q1531.p: Correct. Keep a greater distance behind large vehicles.

q1532.h1: How many vehicles are moving during overtaking?
q1532.h2: When overtaking, both vehicles are moving. The faster the overtaken vehicle, or the slower you are, the more road you need. So both speeds matter.
q1532.p: Correct. The distance depends on both speeds.

q0309.h1: What does the law check in a driver who drank?
