q0309.h2: The law does not ask whether you mixed drinks. It checks how much alcohol is in your blood and compares it to the level set by law.
q0309.p: Correct. Blood alcohol counts, not the drink type.

q1074.h1: In fog, what decides how fast you can drive?
q1074.h2: In fog you see only a short part of the road. So drive slowly, according to what you actually see, so you can stop in time.
q1074.p: Correct. In fog, drive by what you see.

q0866.h1: A signal tells others your plan. Does it also stop them?
q0866.h2: A signal only shows what you plan to do. It gives you no right to pull out. So you must also look properly before you start driving.
q0866.p: Well done. Signal and also look.

q0951.h1: Who might pass your door the moment you open it?
q0951.h2: When you open a door, a rider or a vehicle may be passing right there. So check before getting out that you do not obstruct or endanger anyone.
q0951.p: Correct. Look before you open the door.

q0930.h1: What could happen if the car moves while it is raised?
q0930.h2: A raised car may fall if it moves. So before raising it, make sure the vehicle will not move from its place.
q0930.p: Correct. Secure it first, then raise it.

q0903.h1: Notice the word "always". Who can you always rely on?
q0903.h2: Even when the law requires another driver to give you right-of-way, he may not do it. So don't rely on him, and be ready to stop.
q0903.p: Correct. Don't rely on other drivers.

q0867.h1: Where are your eyes looking when you drive straight?
q0867.h2: When you watch a nearby line, you keep correcting the wheel and the car drifts. When you focus on the furthest point you can see, driving straight is easier.

q0907.h1: A cyclist may move sideways suddenly. What does that tell you?
q0907.h2: You may overtake the cyclist, but carefully. Slow down, leave enough space at the side, and keep watching what he does.
q0907.p: Correct. Pass cyclists slowly, with space.

q1515.h1: Where around the vehicle are places you cannot see?
q1515.h2: A blind spot is any area around the vehicle you cannot see. Not by looking, not in mirrors, not in any other way. It can be anywhere.
q1515.p: Correct. Blind spots are all around the vehicle.

q0660.h1: What does stopping distance include, and what does braking distance include?
q0660.h2: Stopping distance is the reaction distance plus the braking distance. Because it includes the braking distance and more, it is always greater.
q0660.p: Correct. Stopping includes reaction and braking.

q1397.h1: Is there any steep descent where this duty does not apply?
q1397.h2: On a steep descent the vehicle gains speed. A suitable low gear helps you control it. It applies on every steep descent, with or without a sign, short or long.
q1397.p: Correct. Every steep descent: a low gear.

q0731.h1: Before joining traffic: how do you tell others and check?
q0731.h2: First signal so others know what you are doing. Then look in all directions. Start driving only when you will not disturb anyone.

q0819.h1: If you brake hard, what happens to the car glued to you?
q0819.h2: If you must brake hard, the car behind may hit you. So keep enough distance in front, so you can brake gently.
q0819.p: Correct. Space in front protects you from behind.

q0302.h1: What is in beer that can affect the driver?
q0302.h2: Beer contains alcohol, so it is an alcoholic beverage. Its effect is similar to the effect of any other alcoholic beverage.
q0302.p: Correct. Beer is an alcoholic beverage.

q0854.h1: Where should your eyes go when strong light comes at you?
q0854.h2: Don't look straight into the light, because it dazzles. Slow down and keep to the right side of the road, away from the oncoming vehicle.
q0854.p: Correct. Look away, slow down, keep right.

q0814.h1: What happens if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly?
q0814.h2: If the vehicle ahead stops or slows down, you need room to stop behind it. Without a gap, you will hit it from behind.
q0814.p: Correct. A gap prevents front-to-rear collisions.

q0654.h1: Notice the word "braking". When does braking start?
q0654.h2: Braking distance starts only once the brakes are working. It ends when the vehicle has fully stopped. The driver's reaction time is not part of it.
q0654.p: Correct. Braking: from the brakes to the stop.

q1790.h1: Think about each one separately. What does it do to judgment?
q1790.h2: Both alcohol and drugs impair judgment. The driver makes worse decisions on the road.
q1790.p: Correct. Drugs and alcohol both impair judgment.

q1695.h1: What does the light pass through before reaching your eyes?
q1695.h2: Dirt on the windows scatters the oncoming light, and the glare gets worse. Clean windows reduce glare in the dark.
q1695.p: Correct. At night, clean the windows well.

q1704.h2: Tiredness lowers the driver's alertness. This can happen on any kind of road, even a straight and comfortable one.
q1704.p: Correct. The danger is lower alertness.

q1773.h1: What built up on the road while it did not rain?
q1773.h2: While there was no rain, dust and dirt gathered on the road. The first rain mixes them with water, and the road becomes slippery.
q1773.p: Correct. The first rain makes the road slippery.

q0319.h1: Does alcohol speed the body up or slow it down?
q0319.h2: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down the body and the brain, so the driver reacts more slowly.

q0318.h1: Does alcohol wake you up or make you sleepy?
q0318.h2: Alcohol causes drowsiness. It happens to every driver, at any age and any time of day. A drowsy driver is dangerous on the road.

q1690.h1: What near the wheels gets wet in a deep puddle?
q1690.h2: Water in a deep puddle wets the brakes, and they may brake less well. So check that the braking system works as required.
q1690.p: Correct. After a deep puddle, check the brakes.

q1564.h1: Should you flash back, or protect yourself?
q1564.h2: Your high beams would only dazzle him too. Slow down, keep to the right as much as possible, and don't look into the lights.
q1564.p: Correct. Slow down, keep right, look away.

q0844.h1: When you brake, why is your body pushed forward?
q0844.h2: A moving body wants to keep moving. This is the force of inertia. It acts on the vehicle when you brake and slow down.

q0312.h1: How does alcohol change a driver's decisions?
q0312.h2: Alcohol harms the ability to judge situations on the road. The driver feels too sure of himself, so he takes more risks.
q0312.p: Well done. Alcohol leads to more risk-taking.

q0825.h1: An overtaking vehicle must return to the lane. Where will it go?
q0825.h2: A vehicle overtaking you needs room to return to the lane. A suitable gap between you and the vehicle ahead lets it enter safely.
q0825.p: Correct. Your gap leaves room for the overtaker.

q1705.h1: What gives you time to stop if the vehicle ahead brakes?
q1705.h2: If the vehicle ahead brakes, you need time and space to stop. A sufficient gap gives you both. Lights don't help here.
q1705.p: Correct. A sufficient gap prevents collisions.

q0848.h1: When the wheels skid, what happens when you turn the wheel?
q0848.h2: In a skid the wheels don't grip the road. Steering barely works, and the driver loses control of the vehicle. That is the immediate danger.
q0848.p: Correct. Skidding harms steering and control.

q1555.h1: Think: what gives you time to react to a sudden stop?
q1555.h2: A vehicle may stop suddenly at any moment. If you always keep a sufficient distance, using the distance-keeping method, you will have time to brake.
q1555.p: Correct. Always keep a sufficient distance.

q1550.h1: Do the radio or an open window really remove tiredness?
q1550.h2: Rest is what deals with tiredness. So find a safe place to stop, take a short nap, and don't disturb traffic.
q1550.p: Correct. Tired? Stop somewhere safe and rest.

q0311.h1: After drinking, does the driver react faster or slower?
q0311.h2: Alcohol slows reaction ability. The driver notices danger and brakes later. A good mood does not change this.

q0804.h1: Think about the driver, not the engine and tyres.
q0804.h2: At high speed the vehicle needs more road to stop. So it is harder to stop in time and prevent an accident, and you may even lose control.
q0804.p: Correct. High speed makes stopping in time harder.

q0869.h1: If you know where every button is, where does your attention go?
q0869.h2: A driver who knows the systems in the cabin doesn't need to search for them. So all his concentration stays on the road and traffic.
q0869.p: Correct. Know the car, focus on the road.

q1608.h1: Does a dirty headlight shine strongly or weakly?
q1608.h2: Dirt on the headlights blocks some of the light. The road is lit less, so the driver's field of vision is impaired.

q0810.h1: Notice: does stopping distance start before braking, or with it?
q0810.h2: Stopping distance covers the whole way: from the moment the driver sees the danger, through reacting and braking, until the vehicle stands still.
q0810.p: Correct. Stopping: from the danger until standstill.

q0985.h1: Where is the tanker compared to the right edge of the road?
q0985.h2: A driver must keep to the right of the road. The tanker in the picture is not on the right, so it gets closer to oncoming traffic.
q0985.p: Correct. Keep to the right of the road.

q0834.h1: What passes right next to a car stopped on the shoulder?
q0834.h2: On the shoulder you stand next to vehicles driving on the road. The farther your car is from the edge of the road, the less risk of being hit.
q0834.p: Correct. On the shoulder, move away from the edge.

q0955.h1: From which side can vehicles enter the right lane?
q0955.h2: Even in the right lane, vehicles can merge into your lane. They can come from the right, and also from the lane on your left.

q0185.h1: Which color is lit on the traffic light in front of you?
q0185.h2: The traffic light shows red. A red light means you stop before the junction and do not enter it.

q0979.h1: Which side of the road is each vehicle on?
q0979.h2: Each vehicle in the picture is on the right side of the road. In a sharp curve, this is exactly what is required.
q0979.p: Correct. In a curve, stay on the right.

q0918.h1: The pedestrian is not crossing at the crossing. Does that change anything?
q0918.h2: Even if the pedestrian is not at the crossing, you must be careful of him. Slow down, be ready to stop, and don't startle him.

q0879.h1: Where is the cyclist when you turn right?
q0879.h2: The cyclist rides on the right of the car. When you turn right, you cross his path. So think about him and be careful not to hit him.
q0879.p: Correct. Turning right, remember the cyclist.

q0890.h1: The shoulder is not a driving lane. When does it help you?
q0890.h2: On a motorway, the shoulder is kept for emergencies. When there is danger, you can escape onto it and leave the lane.
q0890.p: Correct. The shoulder is for danger.

q0933.h1: What can you see beyond the top of the rise?
q0933.h2: The road goes up, and you cannot see what is past the top. Someone may come from the opposite direction. So slow down and keep right.
q0933.p: Correct. When you can't see, slow down and keep right.

q0924.h1: Where is the pedestrian, and has he finished crossing?
q0924.h2: The pedestrian is still on the road, at the crossing. Let him finish crossing safely. So slow down and be ready to stop.
q0924.p: Correct. Let the pedestrian finish crossing.

q0910.h1: On how many sides of the road are there children?
q0910.h2: There are children on both sides of the road. Children may suddenly run into the road. So slow down, watch them, and stop if needed.
q0910.p: Correct. Near children, slow down and be ready to stop.

q0948.h1: What is standing where the bus is supposed to stop?
q0948.h2: A vehicle is parked in the bus bay. The bus will not be able to enter the bay. It will stop on the road and obstruct traffic.
q0948.p: Correct. Don't park in a bus bay.

q0895.h1: What covers everything you see through the windshield?
q0895.h2: In the picture the whole road looks grey and blurry. That is fog, and it hides what is in front of you.
q0895.p: Correct. Fog limits what you see.

q0970.h1: What can you see ahead of the truck when driving behind it?
q0970.h2: The heavy vehicle hides the road from you, and the road curves. So keep a distance, drive slowly and be patient.
q0970.p: Correct. Behind a heavy vehicle, keep your distance.

q0769.h1: How many things must a driver do when reaching an intersection?
q0769.h2: At an intersection the driver must look, decide and act — many things together, in a short time. That is what makes it hard.
q0769.p: Correct. Intersections mean many tasks at once.

q0916.h1: The pedestrian is still on the road. What does he need?
q0916.h2: The pedestrian comes out from between parked cars and crosses. Let him clear the road safely. So slow down and be ready to stop.
q0916.p: Correct. Let the pedestrian clear the road.

q0981.h1: Which side of the curve is the truck driving on?
q0981.h2: The truck is not on the right of the road. It enters the side of oncoming traffic. Any vehicle coming toward it is in danger.
q0981.p: Correct. Trucks also keep to the right.

q0885.h1: Look past the silver vehicle. What else is on the road?
q0885.h2: The silver vehicle is not the only one. In front of it you can spot another silhouette of a vehicle. Looking far ahead shows it.
q0885.p: Correct. Look far, past the car ahead.

q0929.h1: Where does the road turn, and what can you see after it?
q0929.h2: The road curves, and you cannot see past the curve. So slow down and keep as far right as you can.
q0929.p: Correct. Before a curve, slow down and keep right.

q0915.h1: When should you notice the pedestrian: early or at the last moment?
q0915.h2: The pedestrian comes out from between parked cars. If you slow down and spot him early, there is time to stop and not hit him.
q0915.p: Correct. Slow down and spot pedestrians early.

q0904.h1: The white vehicle is already in the intersection. What does it need?
q0904.h2: The white vehicle has started turning and is in the intersection. If you go on as usual, it will be in your way. So slow down and let it finish.
q0904.p: Correct. Let the car in the intersection finish its turn.

q0975.h1: Who is standing on the road, and what blocks the lane?
q0975.h2: There is an accident, and people are standing on the road. So slow down until you can stop. Oncoming traffic has right-of-way.
q0975.p: Correct. Near an accident, slow down and be ready to stop.

q0972.h1: How far ahead can you see the road?
q0972.h2: A solid line is marked where you cannot see far enough ahead. There you must not move into the opposite lane.
q0972.p: Correct. Solid line — limited view ahead.

q0936.h1: What can you see past the top of the rise ahead?
q0936.h2: The road goes up, and you cannot see who is coming from the other side. So you must slow down and keep as far right as possible.
q0936.p: Correct. At a hilltop, slow down and keep right.

q0746.h1: What is close to you when you drive on the right?
q0746.h2: When you drive on the right, the shoulder is close to you. In danger, you can escape to it quickly and over a short way.
q0746.p: Correct. On the right, the shoulder is close for escape.

q0745.h1: Who drives on the left side of the road, toward you?
q0745.h2: Oncoming traffic drives on the other side of the road. When you keep right, there is a gap between you, and less risk of a head-on collision.
q0745.p: Correct. Keeping right keeps you away from oncoming traffic.

q0908.h1: Who is playing in the road, and what matters most now?
q0908.h2: Children are playing in the road and don't always pay attention. Most important is not to harm them. So do whatever is needed, even stop.
q0908.p: Correct. Children in the road — be ready to stop.

q0982.h1: Where is the white car compared to the right edge?
q0982.h2: The car is not keeping to the right of the road. So it is close to oncoming traffic and exposed to a head-on collision.
q0982.p: Correct. Keeping right keeps you away from oncoming traffic.

q0984.h1: What do the signs on the right say about the road ahead?
q0984.h2: The signs warn of a curve. Enter the curve carefully on the right of the road, and be ready to downshift.
q0984.p: Correct. Before a curve — keep right, take care.

q0901.h1: From which side can vehicles come in heavy traffic?
q0901.h2: In heavy traffic there are vehicles ahead, behind and on both sides. So look all around, keep a gap on every side, and drive at a reasonable speed.
q0901.p: Correct. In heavy traffic, keep a gap on all sides.

q0969.h1: Where might the white car move as it merges into traffic?
q0969.h2: The white car is coming out from the side onto the road. It may push into your lane. If you slow down, you will have time to react.
q0969.p: Correct. A car is merging — slow down.

q0144.h1: Who is walking at the side of the road, close to traffic?
q0144.h2: Pedestrians are walking close to the road. You must slow down, so you have time to react if one of them moves.

q0909.h1: The children are walking at the edge of the road. What might they do?
q0909.h2: Children may step into the road without looking. So you slow down, watch them, check the mirrors and get ready to stop.
q0909.p: Correct. Near children, slow down and be ready to stop.

q0179.h1: Look at the triangle sign on the right.
q0179.h2: The sign means you must give right-of-way. So you slow down, and if there is traffic at the intersection, you stop.
q0179.p: Correct. At this sign, you give right-of-way.

q0917.h1: A pedestrian is crossing in front of you. May you put him at risk?
q0917.h2: Even if he is not using the crosswalk, you must protect him. Slow down, be ready to stop, and let him clear the road.
q0917.p: Correct. A pedestrian on the road – slow down and let him pass.

q0920.h1: Look in the picture for an open door of a parked car.
q0920.h2: Near an open door, someone may step out of the car. So you slow down and keep a side gap from it – move to the left.
q0920.p: Correct. Near an open door, slow down and keep a side gap.

q0878.h1: The silver car is reversing. Can its driver see you?
q0878.h2: A driver who reverses out sees very little. He may enter your lane. So you slow down and get ready to stop.
q0878.p: Correct. A car reversing out – slow down, be ready to stop.

q0968.h1: The car on the shoulder is stopped. What might its driver do?
q0968.h2: The driver on the shoulder may pull into the road suddenly without seeing you. So you slow down and are ready for him to merge in front of you.
q0968.p: Correct. A car on the shoulder may pull out suddenly.

q0953.h1: Night, and a strong light ahead. What does it do?
q0953.h2: The oncoming light dazzles you, so you see less. Do not dazzle back: dim your lights, stick to the right and slow down so you can stop.
q0953.p: Correct. When dazzled, dim, keep right, slow down.

q0888.h1: A car is leaving a parking space ahead. Fight or help?
q0888.h2: The driver leaving the space must be careful. But you must also prevent an accident. Slow down and let him merge.
q0888.p: Correct. Slow down and let the car merge.

q0889.h1: The dark car wants to reverse-park. What does it need?
q0889.h2: Reverse parking needs room and time. If you come close or overtake, you disturb and create danger. Slow down, and stop if needed.
q0889.p: Correct. Let the parking car finish calmly.

q0913.h1: Look at the barrier and at the red light.
q0913.h2: You may not cross when the barrier only starts to rise. Two things must happen: the barrier is fully open, and the red light is off.
q0913.p: Correct. Barrier fully open, red light off – then go.

q0926.h1: Who is on the crosswalk right now?
q0926.h2: The pedestrians are in the middle of crossing. Their look does not give you permission to go. Slow down, be ready to stop, and let them finish.
q0926.p: Correct. Let the pedestrians finish crossing.

q0815.h1: Ask yourself: what must the distance allow you to do?
q0815.h2: The distance must be the one required by law. It must let you prevent an accident at any moment. So you take into account everything happening on the road.
q0815.p: Correct. A distance that prevents an accident at all times.

q0974.h1: The light is green. What is hidden on the right, between the parked vehicles?
q0974.h2: A green light does not promise an empty road. A pedestrian may suddenly appear from between the parked vehicles. So you stay careful.
q0974.p: Correct. Even on green, watch for hidden pedestrians.

q0898.h1: The cyclist rides on the pavement, close to the edge. What might happen?
q0898.h2: He is very close to the edge of the pavement. He might move onto the road, or stumble and fall into it – right in front of your car.
q0898.p: Correct. A cyclist near the road may end up on it.

q0905.h1: Pedestrians walk on your side. How much room do they have?
q0905.h2: They have no pavement, and they are close to your car. Slow down, move left away from them if possible, and pass carefully.
q0905.p: Correct. Near pedestrians, slow down and keep away.

q0958.h1: Look at the colour of the lines on the road and at the two signs.
q0958.h2: The road markings show there are roadworks ahead. The signs limit your speed and forbid lorries to overtake.
q0958.p: Correct. Roadworks – speed limit, no overtaking for lorries.

q0900.h1: Where is the crosswalk – in front of each car or behind it?
q0900.h2: A car parked right before a crosswalk hides the pedestrians from other drivers. So it is not parked correctly.
q0900.p: Correct. Don't park with a crosswalk in front of you.

q0934.h1: The road climbs to a crest. What can't you see beyond it?
q0934.h2: Beyond the top of the climb there is an area you cannot see. A vehicle in your lane may suddenly appear there.
q0934.p: Correct. Danger hides beyond the crest.

q0921.h1: What is standing along both sides of the street?
q0921.h2: This is an urban road with many parked vehicles. They block your view, and a pedestrian may suddenly appear from between them.
q0921.p: Correct. Pedestrians may appear between parked vehicles.

q0881.h1: The car is coming out of a dirt road. Who has priority?
q0881.h2: A car leaving a dirt road gets no priority. It lets all vehicles on the paved road pass, from both sides. Only then does it enter.
q0881.p: Correct. From a dirt road, enter only when it is clear.

q0896.h1: The drivers ahead of the truck are unpredictable. What then?
q0896.h2: You cannot know what the drivers ahead will do. Do not rely on your right of way. Slow down to the point of stopping until it is safe.
q0896.p: Correct. When unclear, slow down to the point of stopping.

q0943.h1: What is drawn on the triangle sign on the right?
q0943.h2: The sign warns of curves in the road ahead. So you slow down and keep to the right, before the curve.
q0943.p: Correct. Before curves, slow down and keep right.

q0906.h1: Children are crossing ahead of you. What do you check before slowing down?
q0906.h2: Children may move suddenly. Look in the mirrors to know what is behind you, then slow down and get ready to stop.
q0906.p: Correct. Mirrors, slow down, be ready to stop.

q0832.h1: Look at the edge between the road and the shoulder.
q0832.h2: If the shoulder is lower than the road or narrow, it is hard to pull onto it safely. So they should be at the same height, and the shoulder wide enough.
q0832.p: Correct. Shoulder level with the road, and wide enough.

q0954.h1: A cyclist on the right. How much room will you leave?
q0954.h2: A cyclist may swerve or fall. So you slow down near him and move left away from him, if possible.
q0954.p: Correct. Near a cyclist, slow down and keep away.

q0794.h1: A U-turn crosses the road. Who might be affected by it?
q0794.h2: In a U-turn you cross lanes. You may delay vehicles, collide with a vehicle from the front or behind, and make someone brake suddenly.
q0794.p: Correct. A U-turn has several dangers at once.

q0952.h1: Look at the road, the sky and the number of vehicles.
q0952.h2: The road is shiny and wet, the light is weak, and there are many vehicles close together. Together these make driving harder.
q0952.p: Correct. Wet, poor visibility, dense traffic.

q0945.h1: What does the triangle sign on the right show?
q0945.h2: The sign warns of a curve. You lower your speed before you enter it, and keep to the right.
q0945.p: Correct. Slow down before the curve, not in it.

q0939.h1: Look at the two signs. What kind of road are you entering?
q0939.h2: The signs say you are entering an urban road. So you adjust your speed, give way to a vehicle from the right, and watch for pedestrians.
q0939.p: Correct. Urban road – suitable speed and care.

q0944.h1: Does anything in the picture force you to change lanes?
q0944.h2: Nothing in the picture is a reason to change lanes or slow down. Continue driving normally, but keep paying attention to the vehicles going your way.
q0944.p: Correct. Drive normally, but stay alert.

q0919.h1: What is open on the car standing on the right?
q0919.h2: An open door means someone is getting out or will get out. Slow down and be ready to stop, so you do not hit the door or the person.
q0919.p: Correct. Near an open door, slow down, be ready to stop.

q0925.h1: A pedestrian is standing on the crosswalk. Who must act?
q0925.h2: The pedestrian is already on the crosswalk. The one driving must prevent the accident: slow down and get ready to stop.
q0925.p: Correct. At a crosswalk, the driver is responsible.

q0977.h1: What is the green container on the right hiding?
q0977.h2: The container blocks your field of vision on the right. Someone may come out from behind it. So you slow down and get ready to stop.
q0977.p: Correct. When you can't see, slow down.

q0774.h1: Think about the car's grip on a wet road.
q0774.h2: A wet road is more slippery. The vehicle might slide, fail to stop in time, and end up inside the intersection.
q0774.p: Correct. On a wet road, a car can slide.

q0882.h1: Look at the white lines in the middle of the road.
q0882.h2: There is a double solid separation line on the road. You may not cross it. Looking in the mirror or signalling does not change that.
q0882.p: Correct. Never cross a double solid line.

q0928.h1: Notice the slanted white stripes on the road, on the left.
q0928.h2: A separation area is marked with stripes on the road. You may not stand or stop on it. A vehicle standing there obstructs traffic.
q0928.p: Correct. Don't stop on a separation area.

q1723.h1: Ask yourself: does anyone plan to have an accident?
q1723.h2: An accident happens without intention. The result can be injury to a person, the driver too, or damage to property, or both.
q1723.p: Correct. An accident is an unintentional event.

q0956.h1: What happens to the number of lanes further down the road?
q0956.h2: The number of lanes is getting smaller. So you don't stay in your lane. You move to the right lane and keep to the right side of the road.
q0956.p: Correct. Lanes end, so move right.

q0899.h1: The truck is already entering your lane. What is safest?
q0899.h2: If you speed up or block it, you might collide. Leave it room to enter without obstruction.
q0899.p: Correct. Don't fight over the lane.

q0938.h1: Notice the car standing on the right side of the road.
q0938.h2: The car is exiting from a dirt road and may enter the road. Slow down and keep an eye on it, so you have time to react.
q0938.p: Correct. Car at the roadside: slow down, watch.

q0940.h1: Notice the sharp curve and the two vehicles in it.
q0940.h2: The duty is on both drivers, not just one. Each slows down when entering the sharp curve and keeps as far right as possible.
q0940.p: Correct. Sharp curve: both slow down, keep right.

q0842.h1: What keeps you away from the oncoming vehicle?
q0842.h2: On a narrow, winding road it is hard to see who is coming. Drive on the far right, turn on your lights, and adapt your speed to the road.
q0842.p: Correct. Far right, lights on, suitable speed.

q0880.h1: Who is coming toward you in the other lane?
q0880.h2: To get past the silver vehicle you must move into the oncoming lane. First slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass. Only then go around.
q0880.p: Correct. The oncoming vehicle goes first.

q0947.h1: How far can you see past the curve?
q0947.h2: You cannot see the road beyond the curve. Your field of vision is limited, so slow down and keep to the right of the road.
q0947.p: Correct. Limited view: slow down, keep right.

q0902.h1: Think: at what moment is the car still going straight?
q0902.h2: When you enter a sharp curve, your speed should already be low. So finish slowing down in time, while still on the straight part.
q0902.p: Correct. Slow down before the curve, not in it.

q0971.h1: Notice the curve and the rock wall on this mountain road.
q0971.h2: This is a mountain road with a curve. A low gear helps you control the car, and keeping as far right as possible keeps you away from oncoming traffic.
q0971.p: Correct. Mountain road: low gear, keep right.

q0771.h1: Think: how long does it take to read and understand each sign?
q0771.h2: Every sign has a meaning. To identify them all and understand what they say, the driver has to slow down.
q0771.p: Correct. Many signs: slow down and read.

q0892.h1: Look at the gaps between the parked cars.
q0892.h2: Parked cars hide anyone standing between them. A pedestrian or a child may suddenly step out onto the road.
q0892.p: Correct. Expect pedestrians between parked cars.

q0188.h1: Who is already on the road when you want to pull out?
q0188.h2: Traffic does not have to stop for you. Signal, and pull out only when you can merge without endangering anyone.
q0188.p: Correct. Signal, then merge only when safe.

q0978.h1: Look at which lights are on in the traffic light now.
q0978.h2: The light that is on now tells you green is about to appear. Get ready to drive, but move only when the green comes on.
q0978.p: Correct. Get ready, and go only on green.

q0142.h1: Notice the stripes on the road and the signs at the sides.
q0142.h2: Ahead of you is a pedestrian crossing with signs. A pedestrian may cross, so you must reduce your speed.
q0142.p: Correct. Before a pedestrian crossing, slow down.

q0922.h1: What are children doing near a bus that has stopped?
q0922.h2: Children are getting on and off, and may suddenly cross. So slow down until you are able to stop, and pass the bus slowly.
q0922.p: Correct. Near a children's bus, go very slowly.

q0931.h1: What happens to the wheels when they roll over the fruit?
q0931.h2: The fruit on the road disrupts the vehicle's grip on the road. So slow down and drive carefully.
q0931.p: Correct. Fruit on the road: slow down.

q0949.h1: Check where the blue car (1) is on the road.
q0949.h2: The blue car (1) should be in the right lane. It is driving in the left lane, and that is the mistake.
q0949.p: Correct. Drive in the right lane.

q0946.h1: When do you slow down, and when speed up, in a curve?
q0946.h2: Reduce speed before you enter the curve. When you come out of it, add speed gently.
q0946.p: Correct. Slow before, speed up gently after.

q0932.h1: Who is on the right of the green pickup truck?
q0932.h2: A scooter rider is moving on the pickup's right, in the blind spot the driver cannot see. Turning right, the driver might hit him, so great caution is needed.
q0932.p: Correct. Before turning right, check the blind spot.

q0730.h1: What do you gain when you see what is far ahead?
q0730.h2: Looking far ahead shows you early what is waiting on the road. Then you can plan your drive and avoid surprises from other road users.
q0730.p: Correct. Look far ahead, fewer surprises.

q0839.h1: Look at the road in the picture: its width, shape and slope.
q0839.h2: In the mountains the road is narrow. It has many windings and sharp curves, and it climbs and drops steeply.
q0839.p: Correct. Mountain road: narrow, winding, steep.

q0980.h1: Where is the white vehicle compared to the center of the road?
q0980.h2: The white vehicle is too close to the center of the road. An oncoming vehicle in the curve could hit it, so its position is dangerous.
q0980.p: Correct. In a curve, keep to the right.

q0770.h1: When there is a lot to do, what helps you keep up?
q0770.h2: Near an intersection there is a lot to see and do. Slow down before it, look all around, and do nothing except drive.
q0770.p: Correct. Near an intersection, only drive.

q0914.h1: Who usually runs after a ball?
q0914.h2: A child might run after a ball that rolled into the road. So slow down, be careful, and be ready to stop.
q0914.p: Correct. Ball on the road — a child may follow.

q0942.h1: Notice the cyclist on the right.
q0942.h2: The cyclist is close to your lane. Swerve left to give him room, and keep watching all the other road users.
q0942.p: Correct. Move away from the bike, keep watching.

q0983.h1: Read what is written on the orange sign.
q0983.h2: The road is narrow and has no shoulders. In danger there is nowhere to escape. So slow down and stay especially alert to what happens on the road.
q0983.p: Correct. No shoulders: slow down, stay alert.

q1042.h1: What makes an engine give off dirtier exhaust?
q1042.h2: An engine and systems that are not looked after work worse and pollute more. Regular maintenance keeps them in good order.
q1042.p: Correct. A maintained vehicle pollutes less.

q1290.h1: Think about fuel, noise, acceleration and pedals. What really differs?
q1290.h2: A manual car does have a clutch pedal, so that is not the difference. The difference is fuel: a manual car usually uses less.

q1077.h1: What happens if the car moves while it is on the jack?
q1077.h2: First make sure the car cannot move: parking brake and chocks at the wheels. Loosen the nuts a little while the wheel is still on the ground, so it does not spin.
q1077.p: Correct. Stop movement first, then lift.

q1052.h1: What do you see in front of you while driving?
q1052.h2: The dashboard has gauges and warning lights. They show the driver what is happening in the vehicle's systems, like speed, fuel and faults.
q1052.p: Correct. The dashboard tells you about the vehicle.

q0989.h1: What happens to a brake that worked too hard and is very hot?
q0989.h2: Brakes that are too hot brake more weakly. The vehicle needs more distance to stop.

q1066.h1: Can every point under the car carry its weight?
q1066.h2: Not every spot on the car body is strong enough. The manufacturer marks where the jack goes. Place it close to the wheel being changed.
q1066.p: Correct. Jack at a strong point, near the wheel.

q1065.h1: How does a navigator help when you don't know the way?
q1065.h2: The navigator knows where the vehicle is right now. It shows the driver the way to the place he wants to reach.
q1065.p: Correct. It shows where you are and where to go.

q1789.h1: Where is the oil when the engine has not run for a while?
q1789.h2: When the engine is not running, the oil flows down and can be measured correctly. A tilted car gives a wrong reading, so park on a horizontal surface.
q1789.p: Correct. Check oil before starting, on level ground.

q1039.h1: Where can the gases go if they don't leave through the pipe?
q1039.h2: Exhaust gases are poisonous. With a leak, they can get into the cabin. The driver and passengers breathe them and lose focus and alertness.
q1039.p: Correct. An exhaust leak endangers those inside.

q1025.h1: Who knows best what suits this vehicle?
q1025.h2: The vehicle manufacturer built it and set the right pressure for it. Not a garage and not a feeling of comfort decides the pressure.
q1025.p: Correct. Pressure goes by the vehicle manufacturer.

q1288.h1: Careful: every part of the answer must be correct.
q1288.h2: Calm driving saves fuel. Tyres with the right pressure also help. Coasting in neutral downhill is dangerous, and driving in a low gear wastes fuel.
q1288.p: Correct. Calm driving and right pressure save fuel.

q1015.h1: What should a wiper do when it rains?
q1015.h2: A faulty wiper does not clean well, so you see less through the windscreen. A worn wiper can also scratch it.
q1015.p: Correct. A faulty wiper harms vision and glass.

q1024.h1: The spare will replace a normal wheel. What sets its pressure?
q1024.h2: The spare wheel must be ready to drive at any moment. So its pressure is also set by the manufacturer's instructions, not by the other wheels.
q1024.p: Correct. The spare also follows the manufacturer.

q1012.h1: How does the belt sit on the body when the seat is far back?
q1012.h2: A belt works when it lies close to the body. If the seat back tilts far back, the belt does not sit right and the body can slide under it.
q1012.p: Correct. A seat tilted too far weakens the belt.

q0696.h1: Look only for parts that protect the body in a crash.
q0696.h2: A belt holds the body in place. A head restraint supports the neck. An airbag softens the blow. Lights and pedals do not protect the body.
q0696.p: Correct. Belts, restraints and airbags protect passengers.

q0743.h1: The car does not leave P by itself. How many actions are needed?
q0743.h2: There are three actions together: press the brake, press the button on the lever, and only then move the lever. Nothing shifts by itself, and there is no clutch.
q0743.p: Correct. Brake, button, then move the lever.

q0742.h1: Without the lever, which pedal asks the car for more power?
q0742.h2: In an automatic gearbox, a strong quick press on the accelerator drops a gear. Some cars also have a special switch for it. The brake does not downshift.
q0742.p: Correct. A hard press on the gas downshifts.

q1035.h1: Changing tyre size is a change to the vehicle. Who must approve it?
q1035.h2: Only the Licensing Authority can approve this change, and it must be done in advance. Not the insurance company and not the driver.
q1035.p: Correct. A new size needs Licensing Authority approval.

q1018.h1: What happens to the air in a tyre when it heats up while driving?
q1018.h2: Warm air expands, so a hot tyre shows higher pressure. Measure when the tyre is cold, before you drive.
q1018.p: Correct. Check pressure in cold tyres.

q1001.h1: What happens to steering when wheels lock in hard braking?
q1001.h2: A locked wheel slides and does not answer the steering wheel. ABS prevents locking, so you can still steer even in emergency braking.
q1001.p: Correct. ABS keeps your ability to steer.

q1005.h1: What does the bumper absorb when there is a hit?
q1005.h2: The bumper is built to absorb part of the blow in an accident. A broken bumper cannot do this well, so damage to the car and occupants is bigger.
q1005.p: Correct. A whole bumper reduces accident damage.

q1702.h1: What do you feel in your foot when the system starts working?
q1702.h2: In hard braking, the system releases and presses the brakes again and again, very fast. You feel it as pedal vibration and hear noise. It means the system is working.
q1702.p: Correct. Pedal vibration and noise are normal here.

q1014.h1: What is right behind your head on the seat?
q1014.h2: In a crash the head is thrown back. The part behind the head stops it and protects the neck. Airbags and belts work mostly to the front.
q1014.p: Correct. The headrest protects the neck.

q1068.h1: Can you know the pressure just by looking at the tyre?
q1068.h2: You cannot know the exact pressure by eye. A simple tool measures it, and any driver can use it himself.
q1068.p: Correct. Measure pressure with a gauge.

q1040.h1: Where do exhaust gases go when there is no fresh air?
q1040.h2: A closed parking garage has little ventilation. An engine running a long time fills the place with dangerous gases. So don't leave it running.
q1040.p: Correct. Don't idle the engine in a closed garage.

q1023.h1: What is the job of the lens over the bulb?
q1023.h2: The lens aims the light at the road. When it is broken, the light scatters in wrong directions and can disturb drivers facing you.
q1023.p: Correct. A broken lens scatters light and bothers others.

q1011.h1: Where are the airbags, and when do they inflate?
q1011.h2: The airbags are inside the vehicle. In a collision they inflate fast and soften the blow to the occupants.
q1011.p: Correct. Airbags soften injuries in a collision.

q0990.h1: Which two signs can you feel and smell?
q0990.h2: Brakes that are too hot brake more weakly, and you feel it in your foot. Sometimes there is also a smell of something burnt.
q0990.p: Correct. Weak braking and a burnt smell are warnings.

q1037.h1: When might an extinguisher fail when you need it?
q1037.h2: An extinguisher that was used, even a little, may no longer be full. A pressure gauge showing low pressure is also a sign. Then replace it.
q1037.p: Correct. Replace a used or low-pressure extinguisher.

q1004.h1: Which system has stability in its name?
q1004.h2: In a skid the car starts to lose control. The stability control system detects this and helps bring the car back on course.
q1004.p: Correct. Stability control helps in a skid.

q0993.h1: A wheel that slides instead of turning. What else stops working?
q0993.h2: Locked wheels slide on the road. Even if you turn the steering wheel, the car keeps going straight.
q0993.p: Correct. A locked wheel ignores the steering.

q1029.h1: A tyre that is too soft bends more on every turn of the wheel. What does that create?
q1029.h2: A tyre with too little pressure flexes more while driving. Because of this it overheats, and that is dangerous.
q1029.p: Correct. Low pressure makes tyres overheat.

q1289.h1: What happens to an engine that is serviced on time?
q1289.h2: A vehicle maintained by the manufacturer's instructions works better. It uses less fuel and its parts wear less. Maintenance does not replace the licence test.
q1289.p: Correct. Regular maintenance saves fuel and wear.

q1055.h1: Can you trust faulty steering or brakes?
q1055.h2: Steering and brakes give you control of the car. If they have a defect, every bit of further driving is dangerous. So you stop and do not continue.
q1055.p: Correct. Steering or brake defect: stop driving.

q1033.h1: Do the nuts stay tight by themselves after the change?
q1033.h2: On the jack the wheel can turn, so tighten the nuts once the car is on the ground. After some driving they may loosen, so tighten them again.
q1033.p: Correct. Tighten the nuts, and again after driving.

q1048.h1: Which system aims the front wheels?
q1048.h2: The steering turns the front wheels. If the system is not aligned correctly, the tyres wear more on one side.
q1048.p: Correct. Steering faults cause uneven tyre wear.

q1009.h1: What happens to an unbelted passenger when the airbag opens?
q1009.h2: An airbag inflates with great force. The belt holds you in place. Without a belt, the body is thrown forward into the bag, and it can hurt you.
q1009.p: Correct. Airbags work together with belts.

q1062.h1: Which pedal do you press in a manual car when changing gear?
q1062.h2: This part connects the engine to the gearbox, or separates them. That is how you can change gear. You work it with the left pedal.
q1062.p: Correct. The clutch connects and disconnects them.

q1080.h1: Look for checks of things that wear out or run low all the time.
q1080.h2: The driver checks things that change over time: fluids and oils, tyre pressure, and lights and wipers. Documents and mileage are not safety checks.
q1080.p: Correct. Fluids, pressure, lights and wipers, regularly.

q1034.h1: Ask yourself: should the engine be running or resting?
q1034.h2: When the engine is off and cold, all the oil has flowed down and can be measured correctly. A car standing tilted gives a wrong reading.
q1034.p: Correct. Check oil cold, engine off, on level ground.

q1031.h1: Who designed the whole vehicle, wheels included?
q1031.h2: The vehicle manufacturer set the tyre size that fits its vehicle. Neither the tyre shop nor the tyre manufacturer decides this.
q1031.p: Correct. Tyre size follows the vehicle manufacturer.

q1026.h1: Think about the tyre itself and how the car holds the road.
q1026.h2: A tyre that is too soft wears faster. The car is also less stable, especially in a turn. The gearbox and steering wheel are not related to this.
q1026.p: Correct. Low pressure wears tyres and hurts stability.

q1021.h1: Does any bulb that fits the socket suit the car?
q1021.h2: A wrong bulb can give too weak or too strong light, or harm the light unit. The vehicle manufacturer's instructions decide which bulb to use.
q1021.p: Correct. Choose bulbs by the manufacturer's instructions.

q1675.h1: What happens to the engine when the oil pressure is too low?
q1675.h2: The oil pressure light is a danger light. Without oil pressure, the engine can be badly damaged. So you don't keep driving - not slowly, and not to the garage.
q1675.p: Correct. Oil light: stop and turn off the engine.

q1691.h1: When does the safety belt really do its job?
q1691.h2: The belt does not prevent accidents or keep you alert. It holds you in place at the moment of impact, so you are hurt less.
q1691.p: Correct. The belt reduces injury in an accident.

q0992.h1: What do you want to keep in your hands when braking hard?
q0992.h2: In hard braking, the wheels can lock, and then steering does not help. ABS prevents this, so you keep control and can still steer.
q0992.p: Correct. ABS keeps control while braking.

q0886.h1: Why add an extra motor to a car?
q0886.h2: A hybrid has an electric motor that helps the regular engine. So the regular engine works less and burns less fuel.

q1020.h1: The flashing on the panel tells you something about the outside bulbs.
q1020.h2: Too-fast flashing on the panel is a warning sign. It shows that one of the indicator bulbs is not working or is faulty. Check them all.
q1020.p: Correct. Fast flashing: check the indicator bulbs.

q1656.h1: Even a tyre that was never driven can be old.
q1656.h2: A tyre ages with time, even when it is new in the shop. So check when it was made, and don't buy one more than six years old.
q1656.p: Correct. Check the date of manufacture.

q0997.h1: How many wheels does the parking brake work on?
q0997.h2: The parking brake is very weak, and it does not brake all the wheels. It is good for holding a parked car, not for regular braking.
q0997.p: Correct. The parking brake is for parking.

q0988.h1: What happens to the brakes if you press them all the way down?
q0988.h2: On a long descent, help the brakes: shift to a lower gear, and the engine slows the car. Use the brakes only partly, so they don't overheat.
q0988.p: Correct. Downhill: lower gear and partial braking.

q1067.h1: If the regular brake fails, what else do you have?
q1067.h2: The parking brake is mainly for parking. But if the regular brake fails, it can help you stop. Its power is limited, so it is no full replacement.
q1067.p: Correct. Parking brake: also for emergencies, but limited.

q1050.h1: Is a nut easier to loosen with the wheel down or up?
q1050.h2: On the ground, the wheel does not spin. So first loosen all the nuts slightly, then raise the car with the jack, and only then remove them completely.
q1050.p: Correct. Loosen slightly, lift, then remove.

q0994.h1: This is something that happens while driving, not when parked.
q0994.h2: When you brake hard without letting go, the wheels can stop turning while the car slides. That is wheel lock. It is not a clamp or parking device.
q0994.p: Correct. Hard braking can lock the wheels.

q1049.h1: Which wheels does the steering wheel turn?
q1049.h2: The steering wheel turns the front wheels. If one of them has less air, the car pulls to that side. Check the air pressure.
q1049.p: Correct. Pulling: check the front wheels.

q1008.h1: What happens to people and objects inside the car in a crash?
q1008.h2: In an accident, the body is thrown forward and to the sides. A hard, protruding accessory can injure the driver and passengers. So they are forbidden in the passenger compartment.
q1008.p: Correct. Hard, protruding items are dangerous in a crash.

q1744.h1: The name says it all: stability control.
q1744.h2: The system does not prevent faults in other systems. It steps in when the driver makes a braking mistake, corrects it, and helps the car stay stable.
q1744.p: Correct. ESP keeps the vehicle stable.

q1002.h1: Stability is the opposite of what?
q1002.h2: An unstable car skids and loses direction. ESP helps the car stay on its path, and so it reduces the risk of skidding.
q1002.p: Correct. ESP reduces the risk of skidding.

q1041.h1: What makes the engine use a lot of fuel?
q1041.h2: Strong accelerations burn a lot of fuel. A gear that does not suit the road also wastes fuel. Drive in the right gear and accelerate gently.
q1041.p: Correct. The right gear, no strong accelerations.

q1485.h1: Look for something every car already has, not an extra accessory.
q1485.h2: When you press the hazard button, all the car's direction indicators flash together. That way other drivers see there is a problem.
q1485.p: Correct. Hazard lights: all indicators flash together.

q1016.h1: Think of a moment of danger. What helps you get out of it?
q1016.h2: Sometimes you need to speed up to get out of danger, for example when overtaking. A strong, working engine helps then. So the engine affects safety.
q1016.p: Correct. The engine helps you get out of emergencies.

q1032.h1: Who designed the vehicle, and where is it written?
q1032.h2: The vehicle manufacturer sets the tire size, because it designed the whole vehicle. That size is recorded in the vehicle license, and only it is allowed.
q1032.p: Correct. Tire size as in the vehicle license.

q1081.h1: Which fluids can you see when you open the hood?
q1081.h2: The driver should check the engine oil and coolant levels. Don't forget the brake fluid and the windshield washer fluid too.
q1081.p: Correct. Oil, coolant, brakes and washer fluid.

q1059.h1: What happens each time you press the gas pedal hard?
q1059.h2: Every coarse acceleration burns more fuel. Calm, moderate driving burns less, and so you save.

q1778.h1: What can be read straight from the car's dashboard?
q1778.h2: At the test, they record how many kilometers the vehicle has driven, from the odometer. This keeps a record of the vehicle's use over the years.
q1778.p: Correct. The test records the odometer.

q1046.h1: Think of a test that every vehicle must pass anyway.
q1046.h2: Vehicles do pollute the air, so they are checked. The check is done at the annual licensing inspection (test), at a licensing institute.
q1046.p: Correct. Emissions are checked at the test.

q1069.h1: Which light warns of a fault, and which only reminds you of something?
q1069.h2: Engine heat, brake fault and low oil pressure mean danger, so you stop. The fuel light only says fuel is running low. You can keep driving to a gas station.

q1287.h1: What happens to fuel use when you drive very fast?
q1287.h2: The faster you drive, the more fuel the car burns. You save by driving in a suitable gear at moderate speeds up to 90 km/h.
q1287.p: Correct. A suitable gear and moderate speed.

q1694.h1: What is the main job of the headlights?
q1694.h2: Headlights must light up the road ahead of you. If they are aimed wrongly, the light goes to the wrong place, and you don't see the road well.
q1694.p: Correct. Badly aimed headlights don't light the road properly.

q1056.h1: A safety defect is not a regular repair. Who may work on it?
q1056.h2: Knowledge and experience are not enough, and not every garage will do. Safety is serious, so only a certified professional, in a garage with a license, repairs it.
q1056.p: Correct. Safety defects: only at a licensed garage.

q1051.h1: Insurance and license don't deal with air pressure. Where else do you look?
q1051.h2: There is a sticker in the vehicle with the required tire air pressure. That way the information is always with you when you stop to add air.
q1051.p: Correct. The pressure is on a sticker in the vehicle.

q1468.h1: Where is the best place to mark something about the tyre itself?
q1468.h2: The date is on the tyre itself, pressed into the rubber. So you can check it even when the tyre is already on the car.
q1468.p: Correct. The date is stamped on the tyre.

q1003.h1: Think: what can slow down each wheel on its own?
q1003.h2: ESP does not turn the steering wheel. It brakes each wheel separately, as needed, and controls the engine power. That way the car becomes stable again.
q1003.p: Correct. Braking each wheel and controlling the engine.

q1706.h1: A blue light is special. It belongs to one light only.
q1706.h2: The blue light is on only when the high beams are on. It reminds you to switch them off when a car is coming, so you don't dazzle its driver.

q0830.h1: The word "hybrid" means a mix of different kinds.
q0830.h2: A hybrid has the regular engine, and next to it an electric motor. They are not identical engines, and not a solar motor.
q0830.p: Correct. Hybrid: regular engine plus electric motor.

q1028.h1: The maker of the vehicle knows best. Where does it tell you?
q1028.h2: The vehicle manufacturer or importer provides a vehicle handbook. It lists the correct tire air pressure. The license and the insurance don't have this information.
q1028.p: Correct. The pressure is in the vehicle handbook.

q1562.h1: The light is on while driving. What is the parking brake doing?
q1562.h2: The light means the parking brake is still engaged. While you drive like this, it keeps braking the vehicle. You need to release it.
q1562.p: Correct. Parking brake light: release the brake.

q1057.h1: The word "preventive": what does it prevent?
q1057.h2: Preventive maintenance is regular care planned ahead. You don't wait for something to break. That way the vehicle and its systems stay in good order.
q1057.p: Correct. Regular care keeps the vehicle working.

q1058.h1: Who knows the vehicle best, from the day it was built?
q1058.h2: The vehicle manufacturer designed it and knows how often it needs maintenance. Not the garage, not the insurance company, and you don't wait for a fault.
q1058.p: Correct. Maintain the vehicle as the manufacturer recommends.

q1038.h1: What happens to the air in a tyre after driving?
q1038.h2: While driving, the tyre heats up and the air inside expands. Then the pressure rises, and the reading is not accurate. So check when the tyre is cold.
q1038.p: Correct. Check pressure when tyres are cold.

q0765.h1: What happens when you drive close behind the vehicle in front?
q0765.h2: When you drive close, you keep speeding up and braking. That wears the brakes and burns more fuel. A proper gap allows calm, economical driving.
q0765.p: Correct. A gap saves fuel and brakes.

q1027.h1: An over-inflated tyre: does all of it touch the road equally?
q1027.h2: A tyre with too much air does not touch the road evenly. Part of it wears faster, and the tyre lasts a shorter time.
q1027.p: Correct. Too much pressure shortens tyre life.

q1017.h1: Think of the part that touches the road all the time.
q1017.h2: Moderate driving and correct air pressure protect the tire. It wears slowly and evenly, so it lasts longer.
q1017.p: Correct. Good driving extends tire life.

q0996.h1: Some things you can see, feel and hear yourself.
q0996.h2: The driver doesn't wait for the garage. Check the brake fluid level, notice whether braking works well, and listen for vibrations and noises when braking.
q0996.p: Correct. Fluid level, braking efficiency, vibrations and noises.

q1079.h1: Will driving, slow or fast, really cool the engine?
q1079.h2: Stop the car and let the engine run at medium RPM so it cools down. If it does not cool down, shut off the engine.
q1079.p: Correct. Stop, wait, and if needed, shut off.

q0986.h1: In the picture: what is on both sides of the brake disc?
q0986.h2: When you brake, the piston pushes the pads onto the disc, which turns with the wheel. The friction between them slows the wheel.
q0986.p: Correct. The pads rub on the disc and brake.

q1708.h1: Look at the grooves in the picture. What flows through them when wet?
q1708.h2: On a wet road, water gets between the tyre and the road. The grooves let it out, so the tyre stays on the road. They are not about the engine or pressure.
q1708.p: Correct. Grooves drain water on wet roads.

q0472.h1: Look at the red triangle and the figures inside it.
q0472.h2: A red-bordered triangle warns. Inside, an adult and a child are walking. So people on foot are near the road. Slow down and be ready to stop.
q0472.p: Correct. Triangle with people: slow down, be ready.

q0616.h1: Look at the picture inside the blue square.
q0616.h2: A blue square gives information. Here it shows a tunnel entrance. A tunnel is dark even by day, so you need your normal front lights on.
q0616.p: Correct. In a tunnel, lights on, even by day.

q0591.h1: Look at the white arrow: how many directions does it point to?
q0591.h2: A blue square with one straight arrow means all traffic here goes one way. There is no oncoming traffic, so you turn left from the left side.
q0591.p: Correct. On a one-way road, turn left from the left.

q0663.h1: Look at the short white lines near the edge of the road.
q0663.h2: Short lines coming out from the road edge divide it into spaces. Each space fits one vehicle. You stop only inside the lines.
q0663.p: Correct. These lines mark a space for each vehicle.

q0361.h1: Find a triangle, and look at the roads drawn inside it.
q0361.h2: A red triangle warns. In the right sign, a side road joins the main road at an angle. A circle gives an order, and a blue square gives information.
q0361.p: Correct. A road joining at an angle is merging.

q0912.h1: Look at the posts with red stripes, and the arrows above them.
q0912.h2: Posts with red and white stripes warn of a railway nearby. The arrow above each post shows which road the railway is on.
q0912.p: Correct. The arrow above the post shows the railway.

q0383.h1: Look at the circles: which one is blue, and what is written in it?
q0383.h2: The blue rectangle marks an expressway. On such a road you may not drive too slowly. A blue circle with a number orders at least that speed.
q0383.p: Correct. An expressway also has a minimum speed.

q1348.h1: Find a blue rectangle with a wide road drawn on it, with no line across it.
q1348.h2: A wide road with a bridge above it marks an expressway. A black diagonal line on the same picture marks its end. A blue circle gives an order.
q1348.p: Correct. No black line: the expressway begins.

q0664.h1: Which colour is lit, and where in the traffic light?
q0664.h2: Only the top light is on, and it is red. Red alone is a simple order. You do not drive on.
q0664.p: Correct. Red alone means one thing: stop.

q0571.h1: Look at the black line that crosses the whole sign.
q0571.h2: The sign marks a place for taxis, where others may not park. A black diagonal line over the whole sign says this area ends here.
q0571.p: Correct. A black line over a sign means the end.

q0961.h1: Look at the colour of the sign whose arrows point left.
q0961.h2: The sign with left arrows is green, and the sign to the right is blue. The background colour shows the road type. Green marks a road outside the city.
q0961.p: Nice. The background colour shows the road type.

q0424.h1: Look at the triangle: does it warn, or give right of way to someone?
q0424.h2: A red triangle only warns that there is an intersection ahead. It does not decide who goes first. The rules and the signs at the intersection decide that.
q0424.p: Correct. A triangle warns, but gives no priority.

q0483.h1: Ask yourself: does the road go up or down? Does the stretch start now or later?
q0483.h2: The slope picture on the sign shows which way the road tilts. The small plate below shows the length of the stretch. Here the stretch starts right at the sign.
q0483.p: Correct. The descent starts here and runs the whole stretch.

q1078.h1: Look at the background colour of the sign and the shape of the arrows.
q1078.h2: A green background marks a road outside the city. The arrows draw the intersection ahead in advance, and show where to turn for each destination.
q1078.p: Nice. A green sign with arrows prepares you for the intersection.

q0500.h1: Look at the black line that crosses the circle.
q0500.h2: Two vehicles side by side show overtaking. A black diagonal line on a white circle says a ban that was in force before ends here.
q0500.p: Correct. A black line on a white circle ends a ban.

q0482.h1: Look at the shape: a small plate with an arrow, and nothing else.
q0482.h2: A small white plate with an arrow does not stand alone. It is added to another sign, and shows which direction that sign's message is for.
q0482.p: Correct. The small plate shows who the message is for.

q0423.h1: Look at the triangle and the short line coming off the straight road.
q0423.h2: A red triangle warns, it does not give an order. The straight line is your road. A short line coming off one side shows a road joining from that side.
q0423.p: Correct. A short side line shows a joining road.

q0610.h1: Look at the black diagonal line across the whole circle.
q0610.h2: Two vehicles side by side show overtaking. A white circle with a black line across it marks the end of a ban. It does not add a new ban.
q0610.p: Correct. A black diagonal line marks the end of a ban.

q0590.h1: Look at the shape, the colour, and the single arrow inside.
q0590.h2: A blue square gives information about the road. One straight white arrow shows that all traffic on this street goes the same way.
q0590.p: Correct. One arrow in a blue square: one way.

q0594.h1: Look at the blue square and the man walking on the stripes.
q0594.h2: A blue square with a walker on stripes marks the place of a crossing. People crossing there must finish safely, so you slow down and stop if needed.
q0594.p: Correct. At a crossing, the pedestrian finishes crossing.

q0406.h1: Look at where and in what colour the light is on in sign 701.
q0406.h2: In sign 701 only red is on. The next stage gets you ready before green. In it the red stays on, and yellow is added.
q0406.p: Correct. After red alone comes red with yellow.

q0439.h1: Look at the cars in the triangle, and the black background.
q0439.h2: A red triangle warns. Inside is a tight row of cars. A black background shows the sign gives off its own light.
q0439.p: Correct. A tight row of cars warns of a jam.

q0576.h1: Look at the red circle and the vehicle inside it.
q0576.h2: A red-bordered circle forbids. Inside there is only a bicycle, and nothing else. So the ban applies only to bicycles.
q0576.p: Correct. A red circle forbids what is inside.

q0451.h1: Count how many red stripes are on each post.
q0451.h2: Posts with red stripes show how close the railway is. The fewer stripes, the closer it is. Two stripes mean about 200 meters before it.
q0451.p: Correct. The number of stripes shows the distance.

q0484.h1: Look at the triangle and the black shape at its bottom.
q0484.h2: A red triangle warns. The black shape is a small round bump on the road surface. It is there to make drivers go slowly.
q0484.p: Correct. A bump in the road makes you slow down.

q0443.h1: Look at the triangle: which way does its point face?
q0443.h2: An empty red triangle pointing down is a special sign. It does not warn. It tells you to let traffic on the road you cross go first.
q0443.p: Correct. Upside-down triangle: the crossing road goes first.

q0419.h1: Look at the shape of the sign: a triangle or a circle?
q0419.h2: A red-bordered triangle warns, it does not forbid. The bicycle inside tells you what to watch for on the road ahead.
q0419.p: Correct. A bicycle in a triangle: watch for riders.

q0492.h1: Look at the arrows: where does each one turn, and what does it look like?
q0492.h2: A red circle with a diagonal line forbids. Each sign has one arrow turning to one side. Each sign forbids the next turn to its arrow's side.
q0492.p: Correct. Each sign forbids one turn, by its arrow.

q0672.h1: Look at the yellow lights, and the figure in one of them.
q0672.h2: A flashing yellow light does not always stop you. It says: be careful. The walking figure reminds you that people cross here, and you must let them.
q0672.p: Correct. Flashing yellow: take care, let the pedestrian cross.

q0384.h1: Compare the two signs: the shape and the colour are different.
q0384.h2: A red triangle warns of something still ahead. A blue square gives information and marks the place itself. Both show a crosswalk.
q0384.p: Correct. A triangle warns before, a square marks the place.

q0651.h1: Look at the white arrow in your lane: which way does it curve?
q0651.h2: An arrow painted in a lane shows where you go from that lane at the next intersection. Here there is only one arrow, and it curves left.
q0651.p: Correct. The arrow in the lane sets your direction.

q0598.h1: Look at the bandaged hand and the symbol next to it.
q0598.h2: The sign gives information about a service on the road. A hand with a bandage shows an injury. The Star of David is a symbol of medical help.
q0598.p: Correct. A bandaged hand marks a place for first aid.

q0367.h1: Find a triangle, and look at what is drawn inside it.
q0367.h2: A red triangle warns of something still ahead. A traffic light with no triangle is the light itself. The right sign has a small traffic light inside a triangle.
q0367.p: Correct. A traffic light in a triangle warns ahead.

q0524.h1: Look at the blue circle with the red border and the single line.
q0524.h2: This sign forbids parking. Such a ban continues along the street. It ends where the street meets another one, or where another sign changes the rule.
q0524.p: Correct. The ban ends at a junction or a sign that changes it.

q0596.h1: Look at the shape: a square standing on its corner, yellow in the middle.
q0596.h2: A yellow square standing on its corner means your road goes first. Drivers coming from the side must let you pass.
q0596.p: Correct. Yellow square on its corner: you go first.

q0628.h1: Look at everything drawn together: people, a child with a ball, and a car.
q0628.h2: A blue square gives information. People, a playing child and a car are drawn in the same place. So everyone uses the same street together.
q0628.p: Correct. Walkers and cars in one street: drive slowly.

q0966.h1: Look at the colour of the arrow on the road, and the signs on the right.
q0966.h2: The arrow on the road is yellow, not white. Yellow road marking belongs to public transport. The signs at the side forbid other vehicles to go on.
q0966.p: Correct. A yellow arrow belongs to public transport.

q1776.h1: Think about what a median strip is for.
q1776.h2: A median strip separates the parts of the road. You do not drive on it, even if it is paved, and not to cross it.
q1776.p: Correct. You never drive on a median strip.

q0382.h1: Look at the round blue signs and where each arrow points.
q0382.h2: A blue circle gives an order. The arrow shows which side to pass on. Look for a single arrow pointing down to the left.
q0382.p: Correct. 215: one arrow, down and left.

q0440.h1: Look at the red triangle and the row of cars inside it.
q0440.h2: A red triangle warns about what is ahead. Cars packed in a row mean traffic may be congested. So get ready to slow down.
q0440.p: Correct. A row of cars: expect congestion.

q0786.h1: Look at the colour that repeats on most of these signs.
q0786.h2: Most of the signs are orange, and one shows a worker. Orange on the road belongs to roadworks. So they are placed only where work is going on.
q0786.p: Correct. Orange signs mark a work site.

q0636.h1: Look at the line in the middle: does it have gaps?
q0636.h2: A solid white line, with no gaps, must not be crossed. So you may not move to its left side and drive there.
q0636.p: Correct. Never cross a solid line.

q0395.h1: Look at the frame colour and the arrow direction on each sign.
q0395.h2: A circle with a red frame forbids. A blue circle gives an order. You need a sign that forbids, with an arrow turning left.

q1278.h1: Find a red triangle, and check the picture inside it.
q1278.h2: A red triangle warns about what is ahead. A blue square only informs. Look for a triangle with a tunnel entrance inside.
q1278.p: Correct. 138: a tunnel in a warning triangle.

q0646.h1: Look at the arrows in the lanes: which lane has a left-turn arrow?
q0646.h2: An arrow on the road shows where you may go from that lane. The left-turn arrow is painted in the leftmost lane. You turn from there.
q0646.p: Correct. Turn left from the leftmost lane.

q0470.h1: Look at the picture on sign 135, and find the same picture on another sign.
q0470.h2: The red triangle warns in advance of a pedestrian crossing. After it, at the crossing itself, comes a blue square with the same picture.

q0531.h1: Look at the pictures from top to bottom, and the number next to the car.
q0531.h2: A blue square tells who the lane is for. It shows light rail, a bus and a taxi. The number next to the car says how many people at least must be in it.
q0531.p: Correct. The lane is only for those shown.

q0356.h1: Look at the picture in each triangle: which one shows the road surface?
q0356.h2: All the triangles warn. Only one shows the road itself, with bumps. It warns that the road is uneven, so you drive according to its condition.
q0356.p: Correct. 101: bumps in the road itself.

q0634.h1: Look at the white line: is it solid or does it have gaps?
q0634.h2: A white broken line marks the middle of the road, or the border between two lanes. Its job is to divide the road.
q0634.p: Correct. A broken line: road axis or lane line.

q0560.h1: Look at the yellow arrow: which way does it point?
q0560.h2: The yellow arrow points down, toward you, from the opposite direction. Yellow on this sign is for public transport and for vehicles a sign allows.
q0560.p: Correct. Oncoming yellow arrow: public transport.

q0545.h1: Look at the circle's colour and the arrow's direction.
q0545.h2: A blue circle is an order you must follow. It has only one arrow, pointing up. So only one direction is allowed.
q0545.p: Correct. One up arrow in blue: straight only.

q0644.h1: Look at the diagonal broken line and the arrows in the left lane.
q0644.h2: The diagonal line and the arrows show that from here the leftmost lane has another use. So watch the arrows in your lane.
q0644.p: Correct. Here the left lane gets a new use.

q0349.h1: Look at the black stripe across the whole sign.
q0349.h2: The sign shows a taxi station. A black diagonal stripe across a sign means it ends here. So the taxi station area ends here.
q0349.p: Correct. A black diagonal stripe means end.

q0563.h1: Look at the colour of the circle and the vehicle inside it.
q0563.h2: A blue circle says who the road is for. Inside is a car, meaning a motor vehicle. A bicycle is not a motor vehicle, so it may not enter.
q0563.p: Correct. A car in blue: no bicycles.

q0428.h1: Look at the black line in the triangle: where does each branch go?
q0428.h2: A red triangle warns of a junction ahead. Read the drawing from bottom to top, as you drive. The first branch goes right, the second goes left.
q0428.p: Correct. Read the drawing from bottom to top.

q0553.h1: Look at the arrows in the blue circle: how are they arranged?
q0553.h2: A blue circle gives an order. The arrows follow each other around a circle. That marks driving around, which is a roundabout.
q0553.p: Correct. Arrows in a circle: roundabout.

q0685.h1: Look at the black line in the triangle: to which side does a branch go?
q0685.h2: A red triangle warns of a junction ahead. The main line goes straight, and only one branch leaves it to the left. There is no branch on the right.
q0685.p: Correct. One branch, to the left.

q0622.h1: Count the arrows in the blue square, and see where they start.
q0622.h2: A blue square gives information about the road. At the bottom there is one line, and at the top it opens into two arrows. So a lane is added.
q0622.p: Correct. One arrow becomes two: a lane is added.

q0420.h1: Look at the black mark in the triangle: how do the lines meet?
q0420.h2: A red triangle warns about what is ahead. Two lines crossing each other show two roads that cross. This is a crossroads intersection.
q0420.p: Correct. A black cross in a triangle: crossroads.

q0371.h1: Compare the posts with red stripes and the red X marks.
q0371.h2: A red X is placed at the crossing itself. Before the crossing there are posts with red diagonal stripes. They show how far the track still is.
q0371.p: Correct. 130: a post with red stripes.

q0632.h1: Look at the black stripe across the whole sign.
q0632.h2: The sign shows a zone where traffic is slowed down. A black diagonal stripe says it ends here. So this is the end of the zone, not its start.
q0632.p: Correct. A black diagonal stripe: end of zone.

q0375.h1: Compare the picture on sign 135 with the pictures on the other signs.
q0375.h2: Sign 135 is a warning triangle: a pedestrian crossing ahead. At the crossing itself stands a blue square with the same walker on stripes.
q0375.p: Correct. After the warning comes the crossing sign.

q0529.h1: Look at the red frame of the circle.
q0529.h2: A circle with a red frame is a prohibition sign. This prohibition does not end by itself at a junction. It lasts until a sign cancels it.
q0529.p: Correct. It lasts until a cancelling sign.

q0182.h1: Look at the white lines on the road, before the crosswalk.
q0182.h2: The sign at the side is a stop sign. The white line across the lane shows exactly where to stop. Stop just before it.
q0182.p: Correct. There is a stop line? Stop there.

q0405.h1: See which light is on in sign 705, and what comes next.
q0405.h2: In a traffic light, after yellow alone comes red. Look for the light that shows only red.
q0405.p: Correct. After yellow alone comes red.

q0310.h1: Look at the shape of each sign: is there another sign like it?
q0310.h2: These two signs have a shape no other sign has: an octagon and an upside-down triangle. So you can recognise them even when it is hard to see.
q0310.p: Correct. A special shape is seen in poor visibility.

q0186.h1: Look at the right traffic light: which light is on?
q0186.h2: A flashing yellow light does not give you right of way and does not stop you. It says: be careful. So slow down, and stop only if traffic requires it.
q0186.p: Correct. Flashing yellow: slow down and look around.

q0502.h1: Look at the red frame and the vehicle drawn inside it.
q0502.h2: A circle with a red frame forbids. The drawing is a car, so the ban is on motor vehicles. A motorcycle without a sidecar is not included.
q0502.p: Correct. A motorcycle without a sidecar may enter.

q0184.h1: Look at the shape: how many sides, and what is drawn on it?
q0184.h2: A red octagon with a hand is the only sign with this shape. It requires a full stop, and only then giving right of way.
q0184.p: Correct. Red octagon: always a full stop.

q0370.h1: Compare the picture on sign 126 with the other triangles.
q0370.h2: On sign 126 your road joins another road. Drivers on the other road see the same merge from the other side. So look for a similar picture, flipped like in a mirror.
q0370.p: Correct. 123 is a mirror image of 126.

q0409.h1: Look at the curved black line in the triangle: which way does it bend?
q0409.h2: A red triangle warns about what is ahead. One curved line bending right shows a road that turns sharply right.
q0409.p: Correct. A line bending right: a right curve.

q0436.h1: Look at the two black lines in the triangle: how do they meet?
q0436.h2: A red triangle warns. In the drawing two roads become one, joining on the left side. In such a merge you do not turn left, and you give way.
q0436.p: Correct. Two roads become one: a merge.

q1801.h1: Look at what is drawn in each square, and what comes out of the car.
q1801.h2: Look for a car with a cable and plug, like a charger. Note: another sign also has a battery under the car. Choose the one without the battery.
q1801.p: Correct. S-130: a car with a charging plug.

q0457.h1: Look at the shape of the red X and its ends.
q0457.h2: A red X like this stands near a railway crossing. A train cannot stop quickly. So slow down enough to stop before the crossing if needed.
q0457.p: Correct. Red X: railway, be ready to stop.

q0385.h1: Look at the black line that crosses the number.
q0385.h2: A white circle with a black diagonal line cancels an earlier restriction. Here it cancels the speed set for the section.
q0385.p: Correct. A black line over a number cancels it.

q0505.h1: Look at the red border and at the two vehicles inside it.
q0505.h2: A circle with a red border forbids. Every vehicle drawn inside it may not enter. A motorcycle is drawn here.
q0505.p: Correct. What is drawn in a red circle is forbidden.

q0489.h1: Look at the triangle shape and the drawing inside it.
q0489.h2: A triangle with a red border warns about what is drawn in it. Here it is a bicycle, so slow down and be ready.
q0489.p: Nice. A red triangle warns: slow down.

q0458.h1: Look at the shape of the red and white X.
q0458.h2: An X like this stands right next to a railway track. Never get stuck on the track: slow down, then cross in one go without stopping.
q0458.p: Correct. Never stop on the track.

q1561.h1: Think which line is closer to you: the solid or the broken one.
q1561.h2: The line closest to you is the one that binds you. The solid line is on your side, so you may not cross. The broken line is on the oncoming side.
q1561.p: Correct. The line closest to you decides.

q0496.h1: Notice the color of each arrow inside the circle.
q0496.h2: The arrow pointing ahead is your direction, and it is red. Red means you give way: the vehicle from the opposite direction passes first.
q0496.p: Correct. Your arrow is red, so you give way.

q0372.h1: Find the sign that stands closest to the track itself.
q0372.h2: The signs with red stripes stand at a distance from the track. The red and white X stands right by the track, so it is the final warning.
q0372.p: Correct. The X stands right by the track.

q0645.h1: Look at the arrows painted in your lane.
q0645.h2: An arrow on the road shows where you may continue from the lane. Here there is a straight arrow and a left-turn arrow, so both directions are allowed.
q0645.p: Correct. Lane arrows set the direction.

q1477.h1: Find a circle with a bicycle, and notice its color.
q1477.h2: A circle with a red border forbids. A blue circle commands and permits. So the sign that permits bicycles is the blue circle with the bicycle.

q0556.h1: Look at the white shape and the red bar on the right side.
q0556.h2: On a blue square sign, a red bar at the end of a road means the road ends there. The red bar is on the road to the right.
q0556.p: Correct. A red end bar means no exit.

q0602.h1: Look at the two drawings in the sign: a tree and a house.
q0602.h2: A white square sign with a black drawing points to a place or a service. A house by a tree marks simple lodging for young people.
q0602.p: Nice. House and tree: lodging for youth.

q0153.h1: Look at the red border and the number inside it.
q0153.h2: A circle with a red border forbids. The number inside is the speed you must not go above. Driving slower is allowed.

q0550.h1: Look at the color of the circle and the direction of its arrows.
q0550.h2: A blue circle tells you what to do. The arrows show the direction of travel around the roundabout. Traffic already in it goes first, and you give way.
q0550.p: Correct. In a roundabout, give way to traffic inside.

q0759.h1: Look at the shape and the orange and black stripes.
q0759.h2: This is not a sign on a pole but an object placed on the road. Orange appears on the road when there are works. It shows where to drive and where an obstacle is.
q0759.p: Correct. An orange cone guides around road works.

q0446.h1: Look at the drawing in the triangle and the arrows on the plate below.
