q0446.h2: A red triangle warns. A light rail train crosses the road here, and the arrows show it comes from both directions. Slow down and keep the right-of-way rules.
q0446.p: Correct. A warning means slow down.

q0413.h1: Look at the black line inside the triangle: how many times does it bend?
q0413.h2: A red triangle warns about the road. A line that bends several times in a row marks a series of curves, not a single curve.
q0413.p: Nice. Several curves in a row: a winding road.

q0397.h1: Look at the empty red circle: does it have an arrow or a direction?
q0397.h2: Sign 401 is an empty red circle, with no arrow. It closes the road to every vehicle, from every side. So the same sign stands at the other entrance too.
q0397.p: Correct. An empty red circle closes both sides.

q0377.h1: Look at the shape of sign 302, and find it inside a triangle.
q0377.h2: A red triangle warns ahead of time about what is drawn in it. So the warning before sign 302 is a triangle with its shape inside: an octagon.
q0377.p: Correct. A triangle warns about what is inside it.

q0528.h1: Look at the red border and the blue mark inside it.
q0528.h2: A circle with a red border forbids what is inside it. Inside is the mark of a driving instruction vehicle. The ban applies while the vehicle is used for a lesson.
q0528.p: Correct. Learner mark in a red circle: no entry.

q0669.h1: Notice: the green light shows an arrow, not a full circle.
q0669.h2: A full green light allows every direction permitted at the junction. A green arrow allows only the direction it points to.
q0669.p: Correct. A green arrow allows only its direction.

q0432.h1: Look at the shape of the sign and the three colors inside it.
q0432.h2: A red triangle warns about what is waiting further along the road. The drawing inside is a traffic light, so be ready to stop.
q0432.p: Correct. A triangle warns about what is inside it.

q0418.h1: Look at the number and the two small triangles above and below it.
q0418.h2: A circle with a red border forbids. The triangles point from top to bottom, meaning height. A vehicle taller than the number, with its load, may not enter.

q0589.h1: Notice the color of the arrow pointing ahead.
q0589.h2: The arrow pointing ahead is your direction, and it is white. The red one belongs to the oncoming vehicle, which must give way. Still, slow down and check it really does.
q0589.p: Correct. You have priority, but check.

q0662.h1: Look at the colors of the line around the bay.
q0662.h2: A red and yellow line around a bay reserves it for a certain type of vehicle. Which one? It is written on the sign posted there.
q0662.p: Correct. The sign at the spot says who may stop.

q0569.h1: Look at the word at the top of the sign and the circle below it.
q0569.h2: The word taxi shows who the place is kept for. The red circle with a line forbids other vehicles to stop or park. Only dropping off passengers is allowed.
q0569.p: Correct. The place is kept for taxis.

q0459.h1: Count how many X shapes are on the sign.
q0459.h2: A red and white X marks a railway crossing. When there is more than one X, there is more than one track.
q0459.p: Nice. More X shapes mean more tracks.

q0686.h1: Look at the person in the triangle: what is he doing?
q0686.h2: A red triangle warns about what is drawn in it. Here a person is digging a pile with a shovel. That is how a road looks when people work on it.
q0686.p: Nice. A person with a shovel: road works.

q0586.h1: Look at the white shape and the red bar on top of it.
q0586.h2: On a blue square sign, a red bar at the end of a road means the road ends there. Here the bar blocks the road ahead of you.
q0586.p: Correct. A red end bar means no exit.

q0587.h1: Look at the white shape and the red bar on the right side.
q0587.h2: On a blue square sign, a red bar at the end of a road means the road ends there. The red bar is on the road to the right.
q0587.p: Nice. The red bar on the right closes the road.

q0506.h1: Check exactly what is drawn inside the red circle.
q0506.h2: The red circle forbids only what is drawn in it: a car and a motorcycle. Bicycles are not drawn, so the ban does not apply to them.
q0506.p: Correct. The ban covers only what is drawn.

q0540.h1: Look at the color of the circle and where the arrow bends.
q0540.h2: A blue circle tells you what to do. The arrow first goes straight up and only then turns left. So you turn left only after passing the sign.

q0520.h1: Look at the black drawing inside the circle.
q0520.h2: The drawing is a house. The sign marks entry to an area where people live. People walk there, so drive with care.
q0520.p: Correct. A house on the sign: a residential area.

q0640.h1: Look at both sides of the solid line: where is the broken line?
q0640.h2: A solid line may not be crossed. The broken line allows crossing only for those driving on its side. So you cross only when the broken line is to the right of the solid one.
q0640.p: Correct. The line closest to you decides.

q0526.h1: Look at the blue circle with the red border and the single line.
q0526.h2: This sign forbids parking. Such a ban does not last forever. It ends at the next intersection, or when another sign cancels it or allows parking.
q0526.p: Correct. The ban ends at a junction or a new sign.

q0666.h1: Look at which light is on, and what it looks like.
q0666.h2: A full green light allows you to go. But green does not mean the junction is empty. Enter only when the junction is clear.
q0666.p: Correct. Green allows, but only into a clear junction.

q1382.h1: Look at the black line that crosses the whole sign.
q1382.h2: This is a taxi station sign, but a black line runs across it. A black line like this cancels the sign and shows its area ends here.
q1382.p: Correct. A black line over a sign marks the end.

q0504.h1: Find a sign that shows the lanes from above, like a map.
q0504.h2: The red triangles warn about a narrow road or oncoming traffic. The blue square sign shows lanes merging, so the number of lanes changes.
q0504.p: Correct. The blue sign shows the lanes.

q0463.h1: Look at the shape drawn inside the red triangle.
q0463.h2: A red triangle warns about what comes next. Inside it is a stop sign. So further down the road you will have to stop, and it is mandatory.
q0463.p: Correct. A triangle warns ahead of time.

q0570.h1: Look at the red circle with a line, under the taxi symbol.
q0570.h2: A circle with a diagonal line forbids parking and waiting here. A short stop only to let passengers off is still allowed for any vehicle.
q0570.p: Correct. Drop passengers off and move on.

q0572.h1: Look at the taxi symbol and the circle under it.
q0572.h2: The sign is for taxis. The circle with a line forbids parking and waiting. So the taxi only picks up and drops off passengers, without waiting for them.
q0572.p: Correct. A taxi here does not wait.

q0657.h1: Look at the colors of the kerbstones along the pavement.
q0657.h2: Blue on the kerbstones marks a parking place. The local authority sets the parking arrangement there, for example payment or hours.
q0657.p: Correct. Blue kerbs mean arranged parking.

q1556.h1: Compare the shape of the two signs, not only the animal.
q1556.h2: Sign 146 is a red triangle, and a triangle warns. Sign 411 is a circle with a red border, and such a circle prohibits.
q1556.p: Correct. Triangle warns, red circle prohibits.

q0437.h1: Look at how the two roads inside the triangle join into one.
q0437.h2: A red triangle warns. Here one road joins another. The traffic already on the road to your left goes first, and you merge slowly and carefully.

q0365.h1: First look at the shape: triangle or circle.
q0365.h2: A red triangle warns, and a blue circle tells you what to do. Among the triangles, find the one with only one road branching to the right.
q0365.p: Correct. A warning is always a triangle.

q0532.h1: Look at the vehicles on the sign, especially the top one.
q0532.h2: The sign marks a public transport lane. It is valid until the nearest junction. Because of the tram on it, it can also last until the end of the track.
q0532.p: Correct. It ends at the nearest junction.

q0427.h1: Look at the shape of the sign. What is a triangle for?
q0427.h2: A red triangle warns in advance. A warning must come before the place, so you have time to slow down and get ready.
q0427.p: Correct. A warning stands before the place.

q0578.h1: Look at the circle's border and at who is drawn inside.
q0578.h2: A circle with a red border prohibits. Inside are pedestrians. So they may not enter here, not even on the road shoulder.

q0568.h1: Look at the black line crossing the blue sign.
q0568.h2: The blue sign shows a motorway. A black diagonal line on a sign means something ends. Here the motorway ends.
q0568.p: Correct. A black diagonal line means end.

q1237.h1: Look at the triangle drawing and the plate below it.
q1237.h2: The drawing shows a road going down. The small plate below says how far away it is. So the descent begins about 2,500 meters ahead of you.
q1237.p: Correct. The small plate gives the distance.

q0600.h1: Look at the drawing inside the white square.
q0600.h2: A white square with a black drawing shows a service on the road. The drawing is a pump with a hose, used to fill up the vehicle.
q0600.p: Correct. A pump with a hose means fuel.

q0638.h1: Look at the dashed line beside the bicycle.
q0638.h2: A blue sign shows what is allowed. The dashed line marks a lane beside another lane, not a separate path. This lane is for bicycles in one direction.
q0638.p: Correct. A dashed line marks a lane.

q0465.h1: Look at the black drawing. Which way does the road go?
q0465.h2: A red triangle warns. The drawing shows a steep descent. Going down, slow with a low gear, because long braking overheats the brakes.
q0465.p: Correct. A low gear helps on steep descents.

q0670.h1: Look at where the two arrows on the signs point.
q0670.h2: Each arrow points diagonally to the next lane. It tells you to move to the adjacent lane, on the right or left, and merge into the traffic there.
q0670.p: Correct. A diagonal arrow means change lane.

q0181.h1: Look at the red sign to the right of the intersection.
q0181.h2: A Stop sign means you always stop, even when the road looks empty. After stopping, give right-of-way to a vehicle coming to the intersection from another road.
q0181.p: Correct. First stop, then give right-of-way.

q0449.h1: Count the red stripes on each post.
q0449.h2: Posts like these show how far the railway crossing is. The more stripes, the farther the crossing. Here you see the largest number of stripes.
q0449.p: Correct. More stripes, the crossing is farther.

q0659.h1: Look at the white shape drawn next to the road edge.
q0659.h2: A rectangle with an X inside, next to the road edge, marks a place where you may not leave a vehicle parked.
q0659.p: Correct. An X by the kerb forbids parking.

q0599.h1: Look at the big letter inside the square.
q0599.h2: A white square with a black symbol shows a service place on the road. This letter marks a place that treats sick and injured people all the time.
q0599.p: Correct. This letter on a sign means hospital.

q0412.h1: Look at the black line. How many times does it bend?
q0412.h2: A red triangle warns. The drawing shows a road with several bends in a row. In bends, slow down and keep right, because you cannot see who is coming.
q0412.p: Correct. In bends, drive slowly and keep right.

q0593.h1: Look at the figure and the stripes under its feet.
q0593.h2: The drawing shows a person walking on crosswalk stripes. The sign marks the place of the crosswalk itself. There, pedestrians go before you.
q0593.p: Correct. At the crosswalk, pedestrians go first.

q0426.h1: Look at the shape of the black line inside the triangle.
q0426.h2: A red triangle warns about what is ahead. The black line shows the road shape: your road ends at a road that crosses it.
q0426.p: Correct. The drawing shows the junction shape.

q0681.h1: Think about what the barrier does when it blocks the whole road.
q0681.h2: A lowered barrier blocks the road on purpose. Do not go around it or under it. Stop before it and wait.
q0681.p: Correct. A lowered barrier means stop and wait.

q0519.h1: Look at the drawing in the circle. What does it show?
q0519.h2: This circle shows a house. A house marks a built-up area, like a town. The sign stands where this area begins.
q0519.p: Correct. A house means entering an urban area.

q0680.h1: Look at the colors and the long shape of the bar.
q0680.h2: A long red and white bar across the road is a barrier. Such a barrier closes the road before the train passes.
q0680.p: Correct. A red-white bar across is a barrier.

q0381.h1: Look at where the two arrows in the triangle point.
q0381.h2: A red triangle warns. Two arrows in opposite directions show that traffic also comes toward you. So be careful and keep right.
q0381.p: Correct. Opposite arrows: traffic comes toward you.

q0911.h1: Compare the sign on the left with the sign on the right.
q0911.h2: Read each sign on its own, and ask: can both be true on the same road at the same time? Here the answer is no.
q0911.p: Correct. Signs in one place must not contradict.

q0549.h1: Look at the color of the circle and where the arrows point.
q0549.h2: A blue circle tells you what to do. The arrows point only to the two sides, with no arrow straight ahead. So you continue only to one side.
q0549.p: Correct. A blue circle commands; arrows show where.

q0455.h1: Count the red stripes on each post.
q0455.h2: One stripe marks the post closest to the railway crossing. Near the tracks overtaking is dangerous, so from here until after the crossing, overtaking is forbidden.
q0455.p: Correct. Never overtake near a railway crossing.

q0649.h1: Look at the white stripes and their direction on the road.
q0649.h2: Wide white stripes across the road, side by side, mark a place where people on foot cross from side to side.
q0649.p: Correct. White stripes across the road: a crossing.

q0518.h1: Think about what comes after the green light.
q0518.h2: Flashing is a warning. Flashing green says the light will change soon. Get ready to stop and do not speed up.
q0518.p: Correct. Flashing green: green is about to end.

q0579.h1: Compare the color of the white arrow with the red arrow.
q0579.h2: The white arrow going up is your direction. The red arrow is the traffic coming toward you. White against red means you have right of way.
q0579.p: Correct. The white arrow is yours; it goes first.

q0501.h1: Look at the circle's border and the vehicle drawn in it.
q0501.h2: A circle with a red border prohibits entry. The car inside stands for every motor vehicle. Only a motorcycle without a sidecar is excluded.
q0501.p: Correct. Car in red circle: most motor vehicles.

q0574.h1: Look at the border color and the drawing inside.
q0574.h2: A red border on a circle prohibits. What is drawn inside shows who the ban applies to. Here it is tractors and work vehicles.
q0574.p: Correct. On a ban sign, the drawing says who.

q0386.h1: Look at the diagonal line crossing the sign.
q0386.h2: The sign shows a truck and a car, like the sign that limits overtaking. The black diagonal line means this restriction ends here.
q0386.p: Correct. A black diagonal line ends a restriction.

q0552.h1: Look at the circle's color and the two side arrows.
q0552.h2: A blue circle commands. The arrows point diagonally down to both sides of the place. So you may pass it on the right, and also on the left.
q0552.p: Correct. Two side arrows: both sides are allowed.

q0491.h1: Look at the full red circle and its white bar.
q0491.h2: A red circle with a white bar forbids entry to all vehicles. It stands on a one-way road, where traffic comes toward you.
q0491.p: Correct. White bar on red: no entry.

q0442.h1: Look at the shape of the sign and the train inside it.
q0442.h2: A red triangle warns of danger ahead. Here the danger is a railway track. So slow down enough to be able to stop before it.
q0442.p: Correct. Before a track, slow down, ready to stop.

q0476.h1: Look at the red triangle and the exclamation mark inside it.
q0476.h2: A red triangle warns. An exclamation mark means danger, but does not say which. So slow down, be very careful, and be ready to brake suddenly.
q0476.p: Correct. Unknown danger: slow down, take care.

q0396.h1: Compare the four signs: shape, color, and what is drawn on them.
q0396.h2: Most limits in the picture end at the next junction. Sign 424 is different: it stays valid after the junction too.
q0396.p: Correct. Not every sign ends at the junction.

q0448.h1: Look at the triangles and at what falls from the slope inside.
q0448.h2: A red triangle warns of danger ahead. Here rocks may fall onto the road. Be ready to brake, swerve or stop.
q0448.p: Correct. Rocks on the road: be ready to react.

q0421.h1: Look at the red triangle and the black X inside it.
q0421.h2: A red triangle warns. The X marks a junction ahead. The sign gives no one right-of-way, so slow down and follow the rules and signs at the junction.
q0421.p: Correct. Junction ahead: slow down, check who goes first.

q0452.h1: Look at the white posts and the red stripes on them.
q0452.h2: Red stripes on white posts warn that a railway crossing is getting close. So slow down and prepare to stop before the crossing.
q0452.p: Correct. Striped posts: a railway crossing is near.

q1572.h1: Look for a road marking: a bicycle with an arrow.
q1572.h2: The question describes a marking that shows who the lane is for and where to ride. Only marking 804 has a bicycle and an arrow together.
q1572.p: Correct. Bicycle and arrow painted on the road.

q0435.h1: Look at the short road joining the long one. From which side?
q0435.h2: The long line is your road, and it goes straight on. The short line is a road joining from the left. Those joining must give you the right-of-way.
q0435.p: Correct. Keep going, watch traffic merging from the left.

q0618.h1: Look at the blue sign: its drawing, and the line at the side.
q0618.h2: A blue sign like this marks a bicycle lane along the road. It applies to the road section ahead, and the intersection ends that section.
q0618.p: Correct. The sign applies until the next intersection.

q0503.h1: Look at the red border and the vehicle drawn inside it.
q0503.h2: A circle with a red border forbids. The vehicle in the drawing is a motorcycle with a rider, not a bicycle. So the ban applies to it.
q0503.p: Correct. Drawn in a red circle means forbidden.

q0471.h1: Look at the people in the triangle. Any crosswalk stripes below?
q0471.h2: A red triangle warns. An adult and a child walk together, with no crosswalk under them. The warning is about pedestrians in the area, not only children.
q0471.p: Correct. People walking, no stripes: pedestrians nearby.

q0373.h1: Sign 618 is a blue square with one up arrow.
q0373.h2: One arrow means traffic in the section goes one way. From the other end, entry must be forbidden to all vehicles: the red circle with a white bar.
q0373.p: Correct. One-way here, no entry there.

q0566.h1: Look at the blue sign: a wide road with a bridge.
q0566.h2: A blue sign gives information. A wide divided road with a bridge over it stands for an expressway. The sign is placed where you enter it.
q0566.p: Correct. The wide-road drawing marks an expressway.

q0486.h1: Look at the shape of the sign and the vehicle drawn inside.
q0486.h2: A red triangle warns; it does not forbid. The drawing shows a tractor. So a work vehicle may cross the road ahead of you.
q0486.p: Correct. Triangle with a tractor: caution, not a ban.

q0363.h1: Both signs are red triangles. What is drawn on the road in each?
q0363.h2: A red triangle is a warning sign, not an information sign. Both show a bump in the road. Such a warning tells you to slow down and stay alert.
q0363.p: Correct. Red triangle: slow down, stay alert.

q0639.h1: Look at the line on your left. What happens to it further ahead?
q0639.h2: A broken line lets you cross. Here the dashes lead to a double solid line ahead. The marking tells you that soon crossing will be forbidden.
q0639.p: Correct. The dashes announce a double solid line.

q0573.h1: Look at the word on the yellow sign and the circle below.
q0573.h2: The circle below forbids stopping. The word above shows who may still stop. So stopping here is kept for taxis only.
q0573.p: Correct. The yellow sign keeps the spot for taxis.

q0652.h1: Compare the color of the middle arrow with the other two.
q0652.h2: Yellow road markings are linked to public transport. The straight yellow arrow means only public transport goes straight at the junction. The white arrows are for everyone.
q0652.p: Correct. Yellow arrow: public transport only.

q0597.h1: Look at the yellow diamond and the black stripe across it.
q0597.h2: A yellow diamond marks a road with right-of-way. A black diagonal stripe on a sign means an end. Here the road with right-of-way ends.
q0597.p: Nice. Black stripe on the diamond: right-of-way ends.

q0475.h1: What is inside the triangle? A picture of something, or just a mark?
q0475.h2: Most dangers have a triangle with their own picture. An exclamation mark with no picture marks a dangerous place that has no special sign.
q0475.p: Correct. Exclamation mark: danger without its own sign.

q0473.h1: Look at the two arrows in the triangle. Where does each point?
q0473.h2: A red triangle warns; it does not give right-of-way. One arrow up and one down show that traffic on the road ahead moves both ways.
q0473.p: Correct. Opposite arrows in a triangle: two-way traffic.

q0469.h1: Look at the triangle: who is walking, and on what?
q0469.h2: A red triangle warns in advance. The man walks on crosswalk stripes. So there is a crosswalk ahead: slow down and watch for pedestrians.
q0469.p: Correct. Triangle with a crosswalk: slow down, take care.

q1570.h1: Sign 135 is a crosswalk triangle. Find that drawing in another shape.
q1570.h2: A red triangle warns in advance that a crosswalk is coming. After it, at the crossing itself, comes a blue square with the same drawing: sign 306.
q1570.p: Correct. First the warning, then the crossing itself.

q0093.h1: Look at the green light: is it steady or flashing?
q0093.h2: A flashing green tells you the light is about to change to yellow. On a working traffic light the number of flashes is fixed, not based on traffic.
q0093.p: Correct. Green flashes three times, then yellow.

q0536.h1: Think about the side where the sign stands, not only the sign.
q0536.h2: A sign usually stands on the right and applies to everyone. When it is only on the left, it is meant for those turning left or making a U-turn left.
q0536.p: Correct. Sign only on the left: for left turns.

q0627.h1: Look at the parking symbol at the top and the car below it.
q0627.h2: A blue sign with a parking symbol allows parking. The car stands partly on the pavement. This is for private cars and commercial vehicles up to a set weight.
q0627.p: Correct. Pavement parking, but not for every vehicle.

q0604.h1: Look at the circle: a red border, and nothing drawn inside.
q0604.h2: A red-bordered circle forbids. When no specific vehicle is drawn inside, the ban applies to all vehicles, from both directions.
q0604.p: Correct. Empty red circle: closed to all vehicles.

q0617.h1: Look at the color of the circle and what is drawn on it.
q0617.h2: A blue circle commands; it does not warn or forbid. A bicycle in a blue circle marks a path meant for bicycles only.
q0617.p: Correct. Blue circle with a bicycle: bicycles only.

q0493.h1: Look at the black diagonal stripe and the two cars.
q0493.h2: Two cars side by side stand for overtaking. A black diagonal stripe means an end. Here the section where overtaking was forbidden ends.
q0493.p: Nice. Black stripe: the ban ends.

q0447.h1: Which line is closer to you: the solid one or the broken one?
q0447.h2: The line closer to you decides what you may do. A solid line forbids crossing it. The broken line beyond it concerns drivers on the other side.
q0447.p: Correct. Solid line next to you: do not cross.

q0544.h1: Look at the arrow in the blue circle: where does it turn?
q0544.h2: A blue circle commands. The arrow goes straight first and only then turns right. So drive up to the sign and turn right after it.
q0544.p: Correct. The arrow turns after a straight part.

q1007.h1: Look at the arrows pointing down and at what is written above them.
q1007.h2: Down arrows mean the sign hangs above the lanes. Each lane gets a destination and road number. Such signs stand before an interchange, on a non-urban road or motorway.
q1007.p: Correct. Down arrows: destinations above the lanes.

q0391.h1: Sign 305 is green and lets you go. What comes just before it?
q0391.h2: Before you may drive on, you are first stopped. A red circle with a hand means stop. That is sign 304; the green sign after it lets you go.
q0391.p: Correct. First you stop, then you go.

q0788.h1: Sign 308 has a red and a white arrow. Which is yours?
q0788.h2: The white arrow is yours: you have right-of-way entering the section. But if a car from the other side already entered, wait until it leaves.
q0788.p: Correct. Right-of-way does not cancel caution.

q0665.h1: Which lights are on in the traffic light now? Notice all of them.
q0665.h2: Red and yellow together mean green is coming soon. But as long as red is on, you still may not drive.
q0665.p: Correct. Red is on? Stay where you are.

q0362.h1: Sign 144 warns of a bump. Find a road marking that shows it.
q0362.h2: A red triangle warns in advance. Later, on the bump itself, white triangles are painted on the road. That is marking 821.
q0362.p: Correct. First the warning, then the marked bump.

q0538.h1: Look at the color of the circle and the word inside it.
q0538.h2: A green circle with a word lets you drive on. It is a portable sign, so you go ahead with caution.
q0538.p: Correct. Green portable sign: go carefully.

q0546.h1: Look at the color of the circle and where the arrow points.
q0546.h2: A blue circle is a command. The arrow points only straight ahead, so no other direction is allowed at this intersection.
q0546.p: Correct. Arrow straight only: no turning.

q0682.h1: Look at the colors on the kerb. There is no red here.
q0682.h2: Black and white does not limit parking. It only stands out, so you notice the pavement or the traffic island.
q0682.p: Correct. Black and white highlights, it does not forbid.

q0530.h1: Look at the black stripe and the symbol under it.
q0530.h2: A black diagonal stripe marks the end of a ban. The symbol under it belongs to driving instruction vehicles.
q0530.p: Correct. Black diagonal stripe: the ban ends.

q0514.h1: Look at the numbers inside the red circles.
q0514.h2: A speed sign is valid until something changes it: a junction, a sign with another speed, or the end of a special section.
q0514.p: Correct. The limit holds until something changes it.

q0658.h1: Look at the colors on the kerb. There is red here.
q0658.h2: Red and white on the kerb forbids standing there. There is one exception: a taxi picking up or dropping off passengers.
q0658.p: Correct. Red and white: no stopping, except taxis.

q0679.h1: Look at the color and shape of the signal above the lane.
q0679.h2: A red X above a lane means the lane is closed to you. Do not enter it, and if you are in it, leave it.
q0679.p: Correct. Red X: the lane is closed.

q0467.h1: Look at the marks under the car's wheels in the triangle.
q0467.h2: A red triangle warns. The wavy lines behind the car show skidding. On a slippery road every sharp move is dangerous.
q0467.p: Correct. Slippery road: do everything gently.

q0355.h1: Compare the shapes. Three triangles, and one sign with a different shape.
q0355.h2: The sign that always requires a stop has a special shape: eight sides and a raised hand. You cannot mistake it.

q0494.h1: Look at the red ring and the shape of the arrow inside.
q0494.h2: A red ring with a slash forbids. The arrow turns back around, so the U-turn is forbidden. A normal left turn is not shown.
q0494.p: Correct. The ban is on the U-turn.

q0555.h1: Look at how many directions the white arrows point.
q0555.h2: A blue circle tells you how to pass. Here there are two arrows, one to each side. So both sides are open to you.
q0555.p: Correct. Two arrows: either side is allowed.

q0661.h1: Look at the color and shape of the line by the edge.
q0661.h2: A yellow zigzag line keeps a stopping place at the road edge. It replaces a bay where there is no built bay.
q0661.p: Correct. Yellow zigzag: a stopping place without a bay.

q0468.h1: Look at the person and the stripes under his feet.
q0468.h2: A red triangle warns about what is ahead. A person walking on white stripes shows a place where pedestrians cross.
q0468.p: Correct. Person on stripes: pedestrian crossing.

q0015.h1: Look at which side of the road the sign stands on.
q0015.h2: The sign applies to the side where it is posted. On a non-urban road, that side includes the shoulder too.
q0015.p: Correct. The ban covers its side, shoulder included.

q0964.h1: Look where the yellow sign stands and what it says.
q0964.h2: The sign stands by the road and gives drivers an instruction. Such a sign is a traffic sign, and you must obey it like any other.
q0964.p: Correct. A yellow sign is binding too.

q0390.h1: Look at the color of each arrow on sign 308.
q0390.h2: On sign 308 your arrow is white and the oncoming arrow is red, so you have priority. Oncoming traffic needs the opposite sign: a red ring that restricts them.

q0497.h1: Look at the red ring and the type of vehicle inside it.
q0497.h2: A red ring forbids. Two cars side by side mean no overtaking. The drawing is a car, not a motorcycle.
q0497.p: Correct. The ban is on cars, not motorcycles.

q0584.h1: Look at the color of the sign and the letter on it.
q0584.h2: A blue sign with the letter P marks parking. It is valid until the nearest intersection, or until a place where parking is prohibited.
q0584.p: Correct. Parking until the intersection or a ban.

q0411.h1: Follow the black line in the triangle from bottom to top.
q0411.h2: A red triangle warns. The line shows the road in the order you will drive it. The first bend from the bottom is the first one you meet.

q0547.h1: Look at the color of the circle and where the arrow points.
q0547.h2: A blue circle is a command. It has only one arrow, and it points straight. That is the only direction allowed.
q0547.p: Correct. One arrow: only its direction.

q0648.h1: Look at the wide white line across the lane.
q0648.h2: The stop line shows where to stop. It does not require a stop by itself. You stop before it when there is an obligation to stop.
q0648.p: Correct. The line shows where to stop, when needed.

q1403.h1: Think which vehicle type the bus stop sign names.
q1403.h2: At a bus stop you park only as its sign says. On Saturdays and holidays the permit is for one vehicle type, not for every vehicle.
q1403.p: Correct. Saturdays and holidays: private vehicles only.

q0624.h1: Look at the two items drawn on the sign.
q0624.h2: A fork and a knife are eating tools. The sign shows a place where you can sit and eat a meal.
q0624.p: Nice. Fork and knife: a place to eat.

q0676.h1: Look at the color of the arrow above the lane.
q0676.h2: Green above a lane means the lane is open. The arrow points down, to the lane below it.
q0676.p: Correct. Green arrow: the lane is open.

q0215.h1: Look at the top word and the red circle below.
q0215.h2: The place is kept for taxis, and the red circle forbids everyone else to park. You may only stop briefly to drop off passengers.
q0215.p: Correct. Taxi stand: only to drop off passengers.

q0541.h1: Look at the color of the circle and where the arrow points.
q0541.h2: A blue circle with a left arrow requires a left turn. It does not forbid a U-turn. Only another sign can forbid it.
q0541.p: Correct. U-turn allowed unless a sign forbids it.

q0580.h1: Look at the circle color and who is drawn on it.
q0580.h2: A blue circle says who the way is for. It shows pedestrians and a bicycle, so the path is only for them.
q0580.p: Correct. The path is for bicycles and pedestrians.

q0642.h1: Look at which line is closer to your car.
q0642.h2: A solid line must not be crossed. A broken line may be crossed. When the broken line is on your side, right of the solid one, it decides for you.
q0642.p: Correct. The line closest to you decides.

q0564.h1: Look at the color of the circle, not only at the number.
q0564.h2: A number in a red ring is a maximum speed. Here the circle is blue, and blue is a command. So the number is a minimum speed.
q0564.p: Correct. A number in a blue circle: minimum speed.

q0957.h1: Look at which traffic island the Stop sign stands on.
q0957.h2: The sign stands on the left island, next to the lane that turns left. So it applies only to drivers turning there.
q0957.p: Correct. The sign applies to drivers turning left.

q0960.h1: Look at the color of the sign whose arrows point right.
q0960.h2: Each sign has its own color, and the color shows the type of road. The blue sign with the right arrows marks the road turning right.
q0960.p: Correct. The blue sign marks a motorway here.

q0539.h1: Look at the color of the circle and where the arrow points.
q0539.h2: A blue circle with a straight side arrow orders you to turn that way. You turn before the sign, not after it.
q0539.p: Correct. Straight right arrow: turn before the sign.

q0513.h1: Compare the colors of the two arrows.
q0513.h2: The white arrow is for all vehicles. The yellow arrow gives public transport a special permit: to pass the sign on the left.
q0513.p: Correct. The yellow arrow is for public transport.

q0583.h1: Look at the color of the sign and the letter on it.
q0583.h2: A blue square gives information. The letter P is the known symbol for parking, and here it is not limited to one vehicle type.

q1711.h1: Look at the orange-black stripes and the board lights.
q1711.h2: Orange and black are road work colors. The flashing board stands at the work site, warns you and guides you where to drive.

q0643.h1: Look at where the yellow lines run on the road.
q0643.h2: The yellow lines run along both edges of the road. They show where the carriageway ends when there are no kerbstones.
q0643.p: Correct. Yellow edge line: the road boundary.

q0441.h1: Look at the sign shape and what is drawn on it.
q0441.h2: A red triangle warns. A train inside it warns that the road crosses a railway. It has no number or extra mark.
q0441.p: Correct. Train in a triangle: railway crossing.

q1569.h1: Look for a red triangle with an animal drawn inside.
q1569.h2: A red triangle warns about something on the road. A red circle forbids. Here you need a warning, so pick the triangles with animals.

q0369.h1: Look at the arrows in the blue circle of sign 303.
q0369.h2: Sign 303 shows a traffic circle. A red triangle is sometimes placed before it to warn ahead. Find the triangle with the same round arrows.
q0369.p: Correct. A triangle warns before a traffic circle.

q0609.h1: Look at the two colors on the curbstone: red and yellow.
q0609.h2: Red-and-yellow on the curb forbids any stopping. Only a vehicle allowed by a sign may stop there.

q0548.h1: Look at the three symbols: P, a plus and a bus.
q0548.h2: P means parking. The plus joins it to the bus. So you leave your car in the lot and continue by public transport.
q0548.p: Correct. Park, then ride the bus.

q0551.h1: Look at the white arrows: which way do they turn?
q0551.h2: A blue circle tells you what to do. The arrows turn in a circle: a traffic circle. Traffic inside goes first, and you go around from the right.
q0551.p: Correct. In the circle: give way, keep right.

q1204.h1: Find a blue sign with a number and small marks around it.
q1204.h2: A red sign with a number is the road number. The kilometer sign is blue, and its number shows where you are along the road.
q1204.p: Correct. The blue sign counts kilometers.

q0543.h1: Look at the circle's color and the arrow's direction.
q0543.h2: A blue circle with an arrow tells you to go right. A U-turn to the right is also a turn to that side. Only another sign can forbid it.
q0543.p: Correct. A right U-turn is allowed unless forbidden.

q0358.h1: Look for a blue square that shows lane lines.
q0358.h2: A blue square informs you about the road. A red triangle warns. Here two lanes join into one, which changes the number of lanes.
q0358.p: Correct. A merging lane changes the lane count.

q0509.h1: Look at the number and the two side arrows pointing at it.
q0509.h2: A circle with a red border forbids. Arrows from the sides show width. Anything wider than the number, cargo included, may not enter.
q0509.p: Correct. Side arrows mean a width limit.

q0554.h1: Look at the color of each arrow: white or yellow.
q0554.h2: A blue circle tells you where to go. A white arrow is for all vehicles. A yellow arrow is for public transport only. A commercial vehicle follows the white one.
q0554.p: Correct. Yellow is only for public transport.

q0965.h1: Look at the round signs: the blue one and the red ones.
q0965.h2: A blue circle with an arrow tells you where to go. Circles with a red border forbid. Check which direction stays open after both.
q0965.p: Correct. One blue arrow, one direction.

q0623.h1: Count the lanes in the blue square, at start and end.
q0623.h2: A blue square informs you about what is ahead. At the bottom there are two lanes, and at the top only one is left. The left lane joins in.
q0623.p: Correct. Bottom to top: fewer lanes.

q0246.h1: Notice: the yellow light is not steady. It is flashing.
q0246.h2: Flashing yellow means the traffic light is not controlling the intersection now. So you slow down and follow the signs and the right-of-way rules.
q0246.p: Correct. Flashing yellow: slow down, follow the rules.

q0635.h1: Look at the two rows of white squares across the road.
q0635.h2: A normal crosswalk has wide stripes. Here there are two rows of small squares. This marks a place where bicycles cross.
q0635.p: Correct. Rows of squares: a bicycle crossing.

q0378.h1: The question asks for a warning sign. Which shape warns?
q0378.h2: A red triangle warns. A blue square only informs. Look for a triangle with two arrows in opposite directions.
q0378.p: Correct. A warning is always a triangle.

q0374.h1: Count the red X shapes on each sign.
q0374.h2: A red X marks a railway crossing. One X means one track. A double X means more than one track.

q0565.h1: Look at the color of the circle and the number inside it.
q0565.h2: A blue circle tells you what you must do. A number in a blue circle is a minimum speed. A slow-moving vehicle cannot keep it.
q0565.p: Correct. Blue with a number: minimum speed.

q0527.h1: Look at the black stripe across the sign.
q0527.h2: A red circle with one red line on blue forbids parking. A black stripe on a sign means the ban ends here.
q0527.p: Correct. A black stripe ends the ban.

q0637.h1: Look at the middle line: how many lines, and are they solid?
q0637.h2: A solid line may not be crossed. Here there are two solid lines side by side, an even stronger ban. You drive to their right.
q0637.p: Correct. Never cross a double solid line.

q0534.h1: Look at the triangle: which way does its point face?
q0534.h2: An upside-down triangle, point down, means the crossing road goes first. You must not get in the way of a vehicle there, or make it slow down.
q0534.p: Correct. Upside-down triangle: the crossing road goes first.

q0415.h1: Look at the two black lines inside the triangle.
q0415.h2: A red triangle warns. The two lines come closer together because the road gets narrow. Oncoming traffic will be closer to you.
q0415.p: Correct. The road narrows: slow down, keep right.

q1267.h1: Look at the vehicle drawn at the bottom of the sign.
q1267.h2: P and a car on the sidewalk allow parking there. But the picture shows a private car. A bus, even a small one, is another vehicle type.
q1267.p: Correct. Only the vehicle shown may park.

q0577.h1: Look at the circle's color and the single symbol inside.
q0577.h2: A blue circle says who uses the way. It shows only a bicycle, with no pedestrian. So the path belongs to bicycles alone.
q0577.p: Correct. One symbol in a blue circle: only it.

q0608.h1: Which two lights are on together in the traffic light?
q0608.h2: Red and yellow together come after red and before green. It is time to get ready, but not to drive yet.
q0608.p: Correct. Red and yellow: green is coming.

q0495.h1: Look at each arrow's color: which is red, which is black?
q0495.h2: A circle with a red border restricts you. The red arrow is your direction. It gives way to the black arrow coming toward you.
q0495.p: Correct. Your red arrow gives way.

q0180.h1: See the triangle on the right and the road on your left.
q0180.h2: A red triangle warns. You are in a lane that enters the road on your left. Traffic on that road is already moving, and it goes first.
q0180.p: Correct. Entering a road: give way.

q1387.h1: Compare the two red-and-white bars at the bottom of the picture.
q1387.h2: A barrier before a railway looks like a long arm with straight red and white blocks. On the other bar the stripes are slanted.
q1387.p: Correct. Red-white blocks: a railway barrier.

q0631.h1: Look at the blue square around the speed sign.
q0631.h2: A speed sign alone applies at one spot. Inside a blue square, it marks a whole zone. In this zone traffic is calm and slow.
q0631.p: Correct. Speed sign in a square: a whole zone.

q1467.h1: Check each sign: does it have an arrow pointing left?
q1467.h2: A blue circle tells you where you may go. Anything not shown is forbidden. Find the sign whose arrows go only straight and right.
q1467.p: Correct. No left arrow: no left U-turn.

q0557.h1: Look at the middle line of the road: solid or broken?
q0557.h2: A solid line may not be crossed. A broken line has gaps, and you may cross it. So you can overtake, but only when the way is clear.
q0557.p: Correct. Broken line: overtaking allowed with care.

q1787.h1: Think about the order of lights after green.
q1787.h2: A flashing green warns that the green is about to end. After it comes the usual light that follows green, and it does not flash.
q1787.p: Correct. Flashing green is followed by steady yellow.

q0684.h1: Look at the black-and-white arrows: where do they point?
q0684.h2: The sign stands in front of the driver, where the road ends at an intersection. You cannot go straight on. You slow down and turn only where the arrows point.
q0684.p: Correct. Go only where the arrows point.

q0460.h1: Look at the red X: is it single or double?
q0460.h2: A red X marks a railway crossing. Here it is double, meaning more than one track. Slow down, check, and cross without stopping.
q0460.p: Correct. Never stop on the tracks.

q0630.h1: Look at the black stripe across the blue square.
q0630.h2: The blue square with people, a child and a car marks a street where everyone shares the way. A black stripe on a sign marks an end.
q0630.p: Correct. A black stripe means it ends here.

q0535.h1: Look at the shape of the sign and the hand on it.
q0535.h2: A sign with eight sides says: stop completely. Stop before the line, not after it. No line? Stop where you can see the traffic.
q0535.p: Correct. Stop before the line, where you can see.

q0690.h1: Look at the two white posts and the black marks on them.
q0690.h2: These are narrow posts standing at the edge of the road. The black marks help you see the edge of the road, even in the dark.
q0690.p: Correct. The posts guide and warn at the side.

q0393.h1: Compare the red lines inside the blue circles.
q0393.h2: A sign with a black stripe marks the end of a ban. A plain red line forbids parking only. Look for a red line with a white stripe inside it.
q0393.p: Correct. This ban covers stopping too.

q0656.h1: Look at the white striped shapes on the road.
q0656.h2: A shape filled with white stripes marks an area you do not drive on. It is a traffic island painted on the road.
q0656.p: Correct. White striped shapes mark traffic islands.

q0462.h1: Look at the shape drawn inside the triangle.
q0462.h2: A red triangle warns about what comes next. The shape inside it is the sign you will meet at the intersection. Find a sign with that shape.
q0462.p: Correct. The triangle shows what waits at the intersection.

q0633.h1: Notice the color of the lines and the diamonds in the lane.
q0633.h2: Yellow marking in a lane keeps it for certain vehicles. Double yellow lines and diamonds mark a lane for public transport.
q0633.p: Correct. Yellow lane marking means public transport.

q0433.h1: Look at the sign's shape and at what is drawn inside it.
q0433.h2: A red triangle warns, it does not order. It says a traffic light is ahead. Go on carefully and act by the light you see.
q0433.p: Correct. The triangle warns; the traffic light decides.

q0561.h1: Compare the two arrows: their direction and their color.
q0561.h2: The white arrow is your direction. The yellow arrow is oncoming traffic. Yellow means public transport, or a vehicle a sign permits.
q0561.p: Correct. The yellow oncoming arrow means public transport.

q0673.h1: Look at the two lights side by side, and at their color.
q0673.h2: Two red lights flashing in turn stand before a railway crossing. As long as they flash, you stop and wait.
q0673.p: Correct. Alternating red flashes: stop before the railway.

q0487.h1: Look at the sign's shape and at the vehicle drawn on it.
q0487.h2: A red triangle warns of danger ahead. The vehicle in the picture is a tractor. It is heavy and slow, so slow down early.
q0487.p: Correct. Tractor in a triangle: slow down early.

q0431.h1: Look at the sign's shape and at the arrows inside it.
q0431.h2: A red triangle warns of what is ahead. Arrows in a circle mean a roundabout. The sign gives you no right-of-way, so slow down.
q0431.p: Correct. A triangle warns: slow down before the roundabout.

q0625.h1: Look at the picture in the square. What is it for?
q0625.h2: A white square with a picture shows a service near the road. A cup on a saucer shows a place to drink and eat.
q0625.p: Nice. A cup means food and drink.

q0668.h1: Look at the traffic light: which color is on?
q0668.h2: A flashing yellow means the light is not directing traffic now. So the signs at the intersection decide who goes. Proceed with caution.
q0668.p: Correct. Flashing yellow: the intersection signs decide.

q0410.h1: Look at the sign's shape and at the curved line inside it.
q0410.h2: A red triangle warns. The curved line is a curve in the road. Enter the curve slowly, and speed up only towards the exit.
q0410.p: Correct. Slow into the curve, gradually faster out.

q0785.h1: Look at the arrow: not straight, and not turning.
q0785.h2: A slanted arrow does not mean a turn. It means moving to the next lane, in the arrow's direction. Move only when traffic allows.
q0785.p: Correct. A slanted arrow: move to the adjacent lane.

q0678.h1: Look at the color and shape of the middle mark.
q0678.h2: A red X above a lane closes it. Red forbids. If it is above your lane, you must leave that lane.
q0678.p: Correct. A red X above: lane forbidden.

q1390.h1: Compare the small picture in the corner of each sign.
q1390.h2: Sign 505 shows a bus, and sign 506 shows a train car. The picture tells you which station it is.
q1390.p: Correct. The corner picture shows the type of station.

q0380.h1: Look at the arrows in each circle: which has no left arrow?
q0380.h2: A blue circle orders you to follow its arrows. A left arrow also allows a U-turn to the left. Find the sign with no left arrow.
q0380.p: Correct. No left arrow means no U-turn.

q1519.h1: Look at the letter and the black line across it.
q1519.h2: A blue square with the letter P permits parking. A black diagonal line across a sign means it ends here.
q1519.p: Correct. A black diagonal line means the end.

q0417.h1: Look at the sign's shape and at what the man is doing.
q0417.h2: A red triangle warns. The man with the shovel is working on the road. At a worksite, slow down and obey the workers and the signs there.
q0417.p: Correct. Road works: slow down and obey the workers.

q0453.h1: Count the red stripes on each post.
q0453.h2: Posts with red stripes stand before a railway crossing. The fewer the stripes, the closer the crossing. One stripe is the closest post.
q0453.p: Correct. One stripe: the crossing is very close.

q0595.h1: Look at the sign's shape and at the color inside it.
q0595.h2: A yellow diamond with a white border marks a road that has right of way. While you are on it, others let you pass.
q0595.p: Correct. Yellow diamond: your road has right of way.

q0562.h1: Look at the circle's color and the vehicle on it.
q0562.h2: A blue circle orders or allows only what is in the picture. A car in the picture says the road is only for vehicles with an engine.
q0562.p: Correct. A car in a blue circle: motorized only.

q0445.h1: Look at the vehicle in the triangle and the arrows below.
q0445.h2: A red triangle warns. The picture shows a local train car. The two arrows on the plate say it crosses from both directions.
q0445.p: Correct. Two arrows: the train comes from both sides.

q0522.h1: Find a sign like 424, but with a black line.
q0522.h2: A sign with a black diagonal line ends the ban of a similar sign. Look for the picture of 424 crossed out by a line.
q0522.p: Correct. A black line across ends the ban.

q0575.h1: Look at the circle's border and the animal inside it.
q0575.h2: A circle with a red border forbids. A horse in the picture says no entry for animals, and for carts they pull.
q0575.p: Correct. A horse in a red circle: no animals.

q0647.h1: Look at the wide white line across the lane.
q0647.h2: A wide, solid white line across the lane shows where the vehicle stops. You stop at it when there is a requirement to stop.
q0647.p: Correct. A wide line across the lane: stop here.

q1803.h1: Look at the picture in each triangle. Which one has a car?
q1803.h2: A red triangle warns of danger on the road. An accident is drawn as an overturned car. Find the triangle with the overturned car.
q1803.p: Correct. An overturned car: accident ahead.

q1123.h1: Read the destinations written on the sign. Where are they?
q1123.h2: A direction sign shows where each arrow leads. The destinations here are places inside the city, like a market.
q1123.p: Correct. Places in the city: urban road directions.

q1760.h1: Look at the arrows: on which sign do they point down?
q1760.h2: A sign above a lane points down, at the lane itself. Find a sign with arrows pointing down and a city name.
q1760.p: Correct. Arrows down: the sign is above the lane.

q0408.h1: Look at the sign's shape and at the wavy line inside it.
q0408.h2: A red triangle warns. The two bumps in the picture show an uneven road. On such a road, adjust your speed.
q0408.p: Correct. Bumpy road: adjust your speed.

q0360.h1: Which kind of sign comes before an intersection, to warn about it?
q0360.h2: Before an intersection, you get a warning first. A warning sign is a red triangle. Find a triangle showing a T-shaped intersection.
q0360.p: Correct. A warning triangle comes before the intersection.

q0400.h1: Look at where the car stands in the picture.
q0400.h2: A blue square with the letter P permits parking. When the car in the picture is up on the pavement, parking there is allowed too.
q0400.p: Correct. P with a car on the pavement: allowed.

q0523.h1: Which circle has only one arrow, turning back?
q0523.h2: A blue circle orders you to follow only its arrows. If it has only an arrow turning back, only a U-turn is allowed.
q0523.p: Correct. One arrow turning back: U-turn only.

q0485.h1: Look at the sign's shape and at the bump inside it.
q0485.h2: A red triangle warns. One bump on a straight line shows a speed bump on the road. Cross it slowly and carefully.
q0485.p: Correct. One bump in a triangle: speed bump.

q0512.h1: Look at the red border and at the number inside each circle.
q0512.h2: A circle with a red border forbids. The number inside is the highest speed allowed, in km/h. The background color does not change that.
q0512.p: Correct. A number in a red circle: top speed.

q0474.h1: Look at the sign's shape and at the direction of the arrows.
q0474.h2: A red triangle warns. Two arrows in opposite directions show two-way traffic. So keep to the right and watch for oncoming traffic.
q0474.p: Correct. Opposite arrows: keep right and watch out.

q0456.h1: Look at the shape: how many X marks are on the sign?
q0456.h2: A white X with a red border stands where a railway crosses the road. The number of X marks shows how many tracks there are.
q0456.p: Correct. One X: a single track.

q0581.h1: Look at the line splitting the circle, and each side.
q0581.h2: A blue circle commands. The line in the middle splits it in two: bicycles on one side, pedestrians on the other. Each uses its own path.
q0581.p: Correct. A line in the middle: separate paths.
